records.title: 4.3L V6 Intake Manifold Gasket Leak
records.description: Same intake gasket issue as all GM 4.3L vehicles. The composite gaskets fail, allowing coolant leaks. The Astro version is particularly problematic due to the engine positioned under the dash, making repairs more labor-intensive.
records.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the lower intake manifold area for external seepage, then confirm whether coolant is also entering the crankcase or intake ports by checking for milky oil, misfires, or unexplained coolant loss. Repair requires removing the doghouse/interior engine cover and upper intake components, then replacing the lower intake manifold gaskets with the updated metal-reinforced GM/Fel-Pro style set, along with new coolant, thermostat, and often the distributor gasket and heater hose quick-connect if disturbed. Carefully clean the sealing surfaces, check the intake manifold for warpage, and torque the bolts in the proper sequence to spec to prevent repeat leaks. Typical repair cost is about $700-$1,400 due to the Astro van's difficult access and 6-10 hours of labor.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 03V159 - Windshield-Wiper Motor Circuit Board

records.title: Central Port Injection (Spider) Fuel Leak
records.description: The 4.3L Vortec V6 uses a central port fuel injection system (nicknamed "spider" for its appearance) that is prone to leaking fuel internally into the intake manifold. The fuel pressure regulator and poppet nozzles develop leaks, causing hard starting, rough idle, and a fuel smell. This is a fire hazard.
records.solution: Replace the entire CPI (central port injection) unit with the updated MPFI (multi-point fuel injection) spider assembly. The updated design uses standard injectors instead of poppet nozzles and includes a new fuel pressure regulator.
symptoms: Check engine light for lean/rich codes

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 05V099 - Stop and Hazard Lamp Switch

records.title: Rear Differential Bearing Wear and Whine
records.description: The Astro van rear differential develops a whining, humming, or howling noise from worn pinion and carrier bearings. The 7.625-inch ring gear differential in these vans sees heavy loading from the rear-heavy weight distribution. AWD models have additional drivetrain noise sources. Noise typically increases with speed and may change tone under load vs. coast.
symptoms: Whining noise from rear that increases with speed
Humming or howling at highway speeds
Noise changes when accelerating vs coasting

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 03V328 - Lower Ball-Joint Boot Interference

records.title: 4L60E Transmission 3-4 Clutch Failure / Slipping
records.description: Avalanches equipped with the 4L60E automatic commonly lose 3rd and 4th gear due to 3-4 clutch pack burnout, a known factory weak point. The long fluid circuit feeding the 3-4 clutch leaks at the input housing (steel shaft galls the aluminum bore) and at the 2-4 servo, so the clutches slip, overheat, and burn. Symptoms are smooth 1-2 shifts but a flare/neutral feeling into 3rd, often with delayed engagement.
records.solution: Rebuild the transmission with upgraded 3-4 clutch frictions/steels, a new/updated input housing, forward and 3-4 clutch pistons, and resealed 2-4 servo; severe cases get a full remanufactured unit. Adding a transmission cooler helps prevent recurrence.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 04V129 - Tailgate Support Cables

records.title: Brake Line Corrosion (Salt-Belt Vehicles)
records.description: Early Avalanches (1999-2003 GMT800 generation) are subject to steel brake line corrosion, especially in road-salt regions where flaking/scaling pipes can rupture and cause sudden loss of brake pressure. NHTSA investigated roughly 6 million 1999-2003 GM full-size trucks/SUVs including the Avalanche but closed the probe with no defect finding and no recall, instead advising owners to wash the undercarriage.
records.solution: Inspect brake lines for scaling/flaking; replace corroded sections or the full set with coated/stainless lines. Preventively, regularly wash the undercarriage in winter. Severe cases require full line-set replacement.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 03V019 - Fuel-Tank Impact Shield

records.title: Cracked Dashboard (GMT900 Models)
records.description: Second-generation Avalanches built on the GMT900 platform are widely reported to develop spider-web cracks in the dashboard, typically starting around the passenger airbag seam and above the instrument cluster. Cracking usually appears after years of UV/heat exposure, and owners report it spreading progressively (audibly worsening over bumps). GM never issued a recall, and a multi-state class action (E.D. Michigan) was dismissed in GM's favor on appeal, leaving owners to pay for replacement.
records.solution: Replace the dashboard pad/panel assembly (dealer or aftermarket), or fit an aftermarket dash cap/overlay as a lower-cost cosmetic fix. There is no warranty/recall remedy, so most owners pay out of pocket or use a cover.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 10V240 - Heated Washer-Fluid Module Fire Risk

records.title: Erratic Fuel Gauge / Fuel Level Sensor Failure
records.description: The in-tank fuel level sending unit on GMT800 Avalanches wears out, producing erratic readings: the gauge sticks on full or empty, drops suddenly, or reads inaccurately. The cause is wear/contamination of the resistive card the sender wiper rides on, leading to intermittent contact (sulfur in fuel accelerates it). On dual-tank 8.1L trucks the problem can affect tank selection/readout as well.
records.solution: Replace the fuel level sensor; because it is integrated into the in-tank fuel pump module, most shops replace the complete pump/sender module (requires dropping the tank or removing the bed). Cleaning contacts is a temporary fix at best.
symptoms: Fuel gauge stuck on full or empty

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 05V163 - Second-Row Center Seat-Belt Routing

records.title: Excessive Oil Consumption & AFM Lifter Failure (5.3L V8)
records.description: The 5.3L V8 with Active Fuel Management (AFM/cylinder deactivation) is prone to two linked failures: excessive oil consumption from worn piston rings and an AFM oil deflector that sprays oil at the cylinder walls, and collapsed/failed AFM lifters that can damage the camshaft. Burning oil fouls spark plugs and can trip low-oil shutdown commands; a failed lifter causes a ticking/knocking misfire. GM settled the Siqueiros class action ($150M) over the LC9 5.3L piston-ring defect for 2011-2014 vehicles built on/after Feb 10, 2011.
records.solution: For oil consumption, GM's TSB remedy involves replacing the AFM oil-pressure relief valve/deflector and often the pistons/rings; many owners delete AFM (range-disabler or PCM tune + delete kit) to prevent recurrence. For a failed lifter, replace the lifters (and cam if scored), commonly done alongside an AFM delete. Eligible owners can file under the Siqueiros settlement.
symptoms: Burning oil / low oil between changes

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 14V827 - Ignition-Lock Actuator

fixParts.note: MAHLE Clevite 213-1738. Fitment confirmed against the ShowMeTheParts catalog for this vehicle's year and engine.
fixParts.provenance: ShowMeTheParts fitment lookup by year and engine; buy links verified to carry the part number on a matching brand

records.title: HVAC Blend Door / Mode Actuator Failure
records.description: The plastic HVAC temperature (blend) and air-delivery (mode) door actuators fail commonly on GMT800 Avalanches. Internal plastic gears strip or position sensors wear out, producing a repetitive clicking/ticking behind the dash and loss of temperature or vent control. On dual-zone systems one side may blow hot while the other blows cold regardless of setting.
records.solution: Replace the failed actuator (driver-side temp actuator is easy to reach; passenger/mode actuators may require glove box or partial dash removal). After replacement the system may need to recalibrate (pull HVAC fuse or battery briefly).
symptoms: No change in temperature with knob
One side hot, other cold (dual zone)

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 04V045 - Hydro-Boost Relief Valve

records.title: Instrument Cluster Gauge / Speedometer Failure (Stepper Motors)
records.description: First-generation (GMT800) Avalanches share the GM truck instrument cluster that suffers stepper-motor failure, causing gauges (speedometer, tach, fuel, temp, oil, voltage) to stick, read inaccurately, flutter, or go dead. The defect was widespread enough that GM agreed to a 2008 class action special-coverage settlement covering 2003-2005 GM trucks/SUVs including the Avalanche, extending coverage to 7 years/70,000 miles.
records.solution: Replace the stepper motors and rebuild the cluster (DIY or specialist board-repair service), or replace the cluster. Vehicles within the settlement window (7 yr/70k mi) could get free replacement; out-of-coverage owners typically use an aftermarket cluster-repair service for far less than a new cluster.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 05V055 - Transmission Shift-Position Indicator

records.title: Unwanted Low-Speed ABS Activation (Corrosion) - Recall 05V379
records.description: Corrosion of the front wheel-bearing hub can contaminate/affect the ABS tone ring and wheel speed sensor, causing unwanted ABS activation when braking at low speeds (roughly 3-10 mph). This extends low-speed stopping distance and pulses the pedal unexpectedly. GM issued recall 05V379000 (Aug 2005, ~1.35M vehicles) but limited the remedy largely to salt-belt states, frustrating owners elsewhere who report the same symptom.
records.solution: Per the recall, dealers inspect/replace affected front wheel speed sensors / hub bearing assemblies. Out-of-recall vehicles are fixed by replacing the corroded front hub bearing assembly (which contains the wheel speed sensor) and cleaning/replacing the tone ring.
symptoms: ABS engages at low speed when stopping

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 05V379 - Unwanted Low-Speed ABS Activation

records.title: Head Gasket Failure
records.description: Quad 4 and 2.2L engines prone to head gasket failure, especially when overheated. Aluminum heads warp easily. More common on the high-output Quad 4 engine.
records.solution: Replace head gasket. Have head checked for warpage and resurfaced. Replace thermostat and flush cooling system. Check for cracked head.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no visible leak

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 90V065 - Rear Center Seat-Belt Instructions

records.title: Ignition Control Module Failure
records.description: Ignition module mounted on base of distributor or in coil pack housing overheats and fails, causing stalling and no-start conditions. Often fails intermittently when hot.
records.solution: Replace ignition control module. Apply thermal grease to new module mounting surface. Module is under coil pack on Quad 4, on distributor on 3.1L.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 91V083 - Steering-Wheel Retaining Nut

records.title: PASS-Key Security System No-Start
records.description: Passlock security system fails to recognize the key resistor, preventing the vehicle from starting. Security light flashes and fuel is disabled.
records.solution: Wait 10 minutes with key in ON position for security reset. For permanent fix, install a resistor bypass on the key cylinder wiring. Dealer can reprogram or replace lock cylinder.
symptoms: Engine cranks but will not start

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 92V185 - Stop-Lamp Switch

records.title: 4.3L V6 CPI/CSFI "Spider" Fuel Injector Leaks and Poppet Valve Failure
records.description: The 4.3L Vortec V6 used a Central Port Injection system (CPI 1992-1995, CSFI 1996-2002) with a central injector body and six plastic poppet lines — the "spider" — mounted inside the intake manifold. The plastic lines and nut-kit connections crack and leak raw fuel into the plenum, while deposit buildup sticks the poppet valves open or closed, mis-fueling individual cylinders. The result is hard hot starts, persistent misfires, fuel-pressure leak-down, and a rich/fuel-smell condition; GM addressed sticking poppets in TSB 00-06-04-003B by back-servicing the CSFI unit with a redesigned MFI assembly.
records.solution: Replace the spider assembly with the updated GM/Delphi MFI (multi-port) conversion unit, which eliminates the poppet ball-and-seat design, along with the nut kit and upper intake (plenum) gaskets. Fuel-system cleaning sometimes frees sticking poppets temporarily, but replacement is the accepted permanent fix.
symptoms: Hard starting when warm or after sitting overnight
Strong fuel smell under the hood
Long crank times from fuel pressure bleed-down
Poor fuel economy and rich running

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 83V107 - Front Brake Hydraulic Crossover Pipe

records.title: 4.3L V6 Lower Intake Manifold Gasket Coolant Leak
records.description: The Vortec 4.3L V6 (like its 5.0L/5.7L siblings) used plastic-carrier lower intake manifold gaskets that erode and crack at the coolant ports from repeated thermal expansion cycles between the aluminum manifold and iron heads. Failures cluster between roughly 80,000 and 150,000 miles, leaking coolant externally at the front or rear of the manifold or internally into the lifter valley, where it contaminates the oil. Left unrepaired, an internal leak destroys bearings and can take out the engine.
records.solution: Replace the lower intake manifold gaskets with the updated metal-carrier 'premium' design gaskets and torque the manifold bolts to spec in sequence. Change the oil afterward if any coolant entered the crankcase.
symptoms: Unexplained coolant loss with no visible puddle
Milky or chocolate-milk colored oil on the dipstick
External coolant seep at the front or rear of the intake manifold
Low coolant light or repeated reservoir top-offs

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 93V119 - Salt-Corrosion Front Brake Rotors

records.title: 9-Speed Automatic Transmission Shudder
records.description: The 2019+ Blazer with the 9-speed automatic transmission (9T50/9T65) develops a shudder during acceleration from a stop, particularly between 1st and 2nd gear. GM bulletin PIP5608J addresses TCC shudder/surge issues. The root cause involves excess lubrication on internal parts contaminating the transmission fluid. Some owners require torque converter or full transmission replacement.
symptoms: Hesitation or jerking between 1st and 2nd gear

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 20V668 - Start-Stop Transmission Accumulator Endcap

records.title: ABS False Activation at Low Speed from Wheel Speed Sensor Corrosion
records.description: On 1995-2003 Blazer/S10 trucks, rust and debris build up on the front wheel speed sensor mounting surfaces, increasing the air gap between the sensor and the hub reluctor ring. The weakened signal makes the Kelsey-Hayes ABS falsely interpret a wheel as locking during light braking below about 5-10 mph, so the ABS buzzes, the pedal pushes back, and the truck lunges forward with extended stopping distance — without setting any trouble codes or lighting the ABS lamp. GM documented the condition in TSB 02-05-25-006B, and the identical corrosion mechanism triggered a 150,000-vehicle recall on 1999-2002 GM full-size trucks.
records.solution: Per the GM TSB, remove the front wheel speed sensors, thoroughly clean the corrosion from the sensor mounting surfaces on the steering knuckles, and reinstall (replacing sensors damaged by rust jacking). Severely corroded hub/bearing assemblies with integral reluctor rings must be replaced.
symptoms: ABS buzzing or grinding activation during gentle stops below 10 mph
Brake pedal pulsates or pushes back at parking-lot speeds
Truck rolls farther than expected when stopping on dry pavement
No ABS warning light and no stored trouble codes
Worse in winter or in road-salt regions

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 91V108 - Fuel-Tank Sender Seal

records.title: CSFI/CPI "Spider" Fuel Injector Assembly Failure (Poppet Valve Leaks)
records.description: The 4.3L Vortec uses a Central Sequential Fuel Injection (CSFI, often called the "spider") assembly buried under the upper intake plenum, with individual nylon poppet lines feeding each cylinder. The poppet valves and the integrated fuel pressure regulator crack, stick, or leak with age and heat, dumping raw fuel into the plenum. This is one of the single most common driveability failures on the 1995-1999 S-series Blazer and is extensively documented across enthusiast forums and repair sites.
records.solution: Replace the CSFI/CPI spider assembly. The widely recommended fix is to install the updated multi-port (MPFI) style conversion assembly with individual injectors instead of poppets, which is far more reliable than another OE poppet unit. Requires removing the upper intake plenum; inspect/replace intake gaskets while in there.
symptoms: Rough idle and low-RPM stumble that smooths out at higher RPM
Strong fuel smell / raw fuel in the intake
Hesitation and lack of power under load
Fouled plugs / misfire, catalytic converter overheating

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 20V811 - Seat-Belt Fastening Bolts

records.title: Door Hinge Pin and Bushing Wear Causing Sagging Doors
records.description: The heavy doors on two-door S-10 Blazers ride on small hinge pins with soft brass bushings that wear out — accelerated by lack of lubrication — letting the bushing holes in the hinge plates wallow out egg-shaped. The door then drops when opened, no longer aligns with the striker, and must be lifted or slammed to close. It is so universal on these trucks that multiple aftermarket oversized pin-and-bushing kits exist specifically for the platform.
records.solution: Replace the hinge pins and bushings with a repair kit, using oversized bushings (or welding and re-drilling the hinge hole) when the hinge plate itself is wallowed out, then readjust the striker. Regular hinge lubrication prevents recurrence.
symptoms: Door must be lifted or slammed to latch
Clunk or pop when opening the door
Door out of alignment with the striker and body lines
Visible play when lifting the open door by its edge

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 94V093 - Low/Reverse Clutch and Park Engagement

records.title: Electric-Shift Transfer Case Encoder Motor and TCCM Failure (Service 4WD Light)
records.description: Push-button 4WD Blazers use an electric encoder motor on the NP1 electronic-shift transfer case, commanded by the Transfer Case Control Module (TCCM). The encoder motor's internal position sensor and gears wear out, and TCCM faults are equally common, so the transfer case fails to shift into or out of 4WD or gets stuck in a mode. Owners see flashing shift buttons or a Service 4WD light, and the system stores encoder fault codes readable via the TCCM's flash sequence.
records.solution: Diagnose whether the encoder motor runs when a shift is commanded; replace the encoder motor if its gears or position sensor have failed, or the TCCM if the motor never receives a command. Resetting the TCCM (battery or fuse pull) clears stuck states only temporarily when hardware is worn.
symptoms: Service 4WD light on or shift-mode buttons flashing
4WD will not engage when the button is pressed
Transfer case stuck in 4HI or 4LO, won't return to 2HI
Whirring or grinding from the transfer case during shift attempts
Intermittent engagement that works after a battery reset

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 96V142 - Rear Seat-Belt Buckles

records.title: Front Lower Ball Joint Premature Wear / Failure (Non-Greaseable)
records.description: The factory front lower ball joints on the S-series Blazer were sealed with no grease fittings and cannot be lubricated, leading to premature wear. NHTSA complaints document serious failures where the ball joint separates, the wheel folds under the vehicle, and steering control is lost - sometimes at low speed. 4WD models carry more front-end weight and are especially prone. This is a safety-critical wear item on high-mileage examples.
records.solution: Replace lower ball joints (and inspect uppers, control-arm bushings, and tie rods). Many owners fit greaseable aftermarket units (e.g., Moog problem-solver) with zerk fittings so they can be maintained. Front-end alignment required afterward.
symptoms: Clunking or popping over bumps and when turning
Sudden loss of steering control / wheel collapse in severe failure

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 94V114 - Trailer-Hitch Bolt Torque

records.title: Infotainment System Freezing and Lag
records.description: The 2019+ Blazer infotainment system (Chevrolet Infotainment 3) suffers from screen lockups, lag, and unresponsive touch input. The screen can freeze on the backup camera view or refuse button and touch input. GM bulletin PIT5790A acknowledges the issue but initially had no fix available. Bluetooth and Apple CarPlay disconnections are also common. Some owners have had the radio module replaced.
symptoms: Screen freezes on backup camera or other display

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 23V172 - Incorrect Transmission Sun Gear

records.title: Instrument Cluster Gauge / Stepper Motor Failure
records.description: The GM truck/SUV instrument clusters of this era use small air-core stepper motors to drive each gauge needle. Over time the internal dampening grease dries and the motors fail, causing needles to stick, read wildly wrong, or drop to zero. The speedometer and tachometer ("S" type motors on 1995-1999 clusters) are the most commonly affected, though the fuel gauge is also frequently impacted. It is a wear/age failure, not a sending-unit fault, so replacing senders does not fix it.
records.solution: Rebuild the cluster by replacing the affected air-core stepper motor(s) with the GM-authorized Switec X27.168 - a common DIY with widely available motor kits - or send the cluster to a rebuild service. Recalibrate/sweep needles after replacement.
symptoms: Speedometer stuck, jumpy, or reading zero
Fuel gauge stuck on full or empty / inaccurate
Temperature or other needles pinned or erratic
Multiple gauges misbehaving with sending units known good

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 96V234 - Fuel-Tank Prop-Shaft Shielding

records.title: Kelsey-Hayes ABS: Wheel Speed Sensor / EBCM Faults & Corroded Grounds
records.description: The S-series Blazer's Kelsey-Hayes ABS system is prone to age-related faults: front wheel-speed sensors (integrated into the hub bearings) corrode and give erratic signals, the EBCM ground at the radiator support gets rusty/loose, and later Kelsey-Hayes 325 modules can fail internally. Symptoms include an ABS warning light, erratic wheel-speed codes, and in some cases the ABS pump running with the key off. Corroded grounds and connectors are a very common root cause on rust-belt trucks.
records.solution: Scan for C-codes and inspect. Clean and tighten the EBCM ground straps at the radiator support first. Replace corroded front wheel-speed sensors / hub bearing assemblies as needed. If the EBCM itself is faulty, a repair-and-return board service is a cost-effective alternative to a new module.
symptoms: ABS activating at low speed / false activation
ABS pump running with the ignition off
Intermittent faults that worsen when wet

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 95V180 - Engine-Cooling Fan Rivets

records.title: Lower Intake Manifold Gasket Coolant/Oil Leak
records.description: The 4.3L Vortec rarely fails head gaskets but very commonly fails its lower (plenum) intake manifold gaskets. The original-equipment gaskets use plastic/composite carriers that harden and shrink with heat cycling, typically leaking between roughly 100k-150k miles. Left unaddressed the leak can push coolant into the oil and eventually damage the bottom end.
records.solution: Replace the intake manifold gaskets with the upgraded metal-reinforced design (Fel-Pro, Mahle, or Victor Reinz). Resurface/clean sealing surfaces and use proper RTV at the front/rear China-wall seals. Spider injector service is commonly done at the same time since the plenum is already off.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no obvious external leak
Coolant seeping at the intake-to-block joint
Milky oil / coolant in the oil
White exhaust smoke / sweet smell in extreme cases

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 22V359 - Driver Seat Cushion-Frame Weld

records.title: NP8 Push-Button 4WD Transfer Case Encoder Motor / Selector Failure ("Service 4WD")
records.description: 4WD Blazers with the electric push-button New Process 233 transfer case (RPO NP8) use a TCCM-controlled encoder motor to shift ranges. The encoder motor, its position sensor, corroded selector-button contacts, and connector moisture are all common failure points, producing a "Service 4WD" warning, refusal to engage 4-Hi/4-Lo, or the case getting stuck in neutral. A frequent aggravating factor is corrosion at the button module and connectors.
records.solution: Diagnose with a scanner (encoder position codes). Clean/repair corroded selector-switch contacts and connectors first. Replace the encoder motor if faulty; codes must be cleared with a scan tool after replacement or the case may not shift correctly. Verify the truck actually has RPO NP8 before buying parts.
symptoms: 4WD buttons flash or do not respond
Won't shift into or out of 4-Hi / 4-Lo

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 23V869 - Fracturing Door Strikers

records.title: 4.3L V6 Intake Manifold Gasket Leak
records.description: Same as the S-10 truck - the 4.3L Vortec V6 develops intake manifold gasket leaks. The Blazer version is identical mechanically.
records.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the front and rear edges of the lower intake manifold for external coolant seepage; on the 4.3L Vortec, leaks are commonly caused by the original lower intake manifold gaskets deteriorating. The proper repair is to remove the upper plenum and lower intake manifold, replace the lower intake manifold gaskets with the updated metal/rubber design, install new intake bolts if specified, and refill with fresh coolant and engine oil if contamination is present. While apart, inspect the distributor, heater hose fittings, and CPI/CSFI lines for related age-related failures, then torque the intake in the correct sequence to spec. Typical repair cost is about $700-$1,300 depending on labor rates and whether coolant/oil contamination or additional tune-up parts are needed.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 90V107 - Windshield and Side-Window Primer

records.title: 4WD Thermal Actuator and Encoder Motor Failure
records.description: The front axle thermal actuator (push-button 4WD models) and transfer case encoder motor fail, preventing engagement or disengagement of 4WD. The thermal actuator uses coolant heating to engage, which is slow and unreliable.
records.solution: Diagnose the system by checking for transfer case control module codes, verifying 4WD switch operation, and confirming power/ground at the front axle actuator and transfer case encoder motor; also inspect the vacuum/electrical connectors and front axle engagement fork for damage. On push-button 4WD models, replace the original thermal actuator with the updated GM motor-style actuator conversion kit and spacer, which engages faster and more reliably; if the transfer case will not shift or sets encoder-related faults, replace the encoder motor assembly and clean/corrosion-proof the connector. After repair, verify 2HI/4HI/4LO operation on a lift and road test to confirm the front axle fully engages and disengages. Typical cost is about $150-$300 for the updated front actuator kit installed, or roughly $300-$700 for an encoder motor replacement depending on labor rates and parts quality.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 93V105 - Outboard Rear Seat Belts

records.title: Dashboard Cracking and Warping
records.description: The 1998-2004 S-10 Blazer (and related S-10, GMC Jimmy, GMC Sonoma) dashboards crack severely from UV exposure and heat cycling. The instrument panel trim pad warps, splits, and crumbles. This is a known manufacturing defect in the dashboard material used across the entire S-10 platform during these years.
records.solution: Confirm the failure is cosmetic dashboard substrate deterioration rather than loose trim by inspecting for cracks around the defroster vents, gauge hood, and passenger airbag area, then checking whether the dash pad has lifted or become brittle from sun exposure. The permanent repair is replacement of the upper instrument panel pad/dash cap assembly with a new OEM, NOS, or quality aftermarket molded cap; this typically requires removing trim panels, cluster bezel, defroster grille fasteners, and in some cases partially lowering the steering column for access. If the original pad is badly fragmented, many owners install a full overlay dash cap bonded with automotive urethane or silicone after trimming loose material, which is cheaper but less factory-correct. Typical cost is about $150-$350 for an aftermarket cap, $400-$900 for a replacement dash pad if available, and roughly 4-8 hours labor, bringing total installed cost to about $500-$1,500 depending on parts source and interior disassembly required.
symptoms: Large cracks appearing on dashboard surface
Dashboard warping near windshield defroster vents
Pieces of dashboard material crumbling or flaking
Dashboard becoming sticky in hot weather
Windshield glare from warped dashboard surface

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 97V096 - Front Seat-Belt Webbing Protection

records.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump Premature Failure and Stalling
records.description: Blazer in-tank fuel pumps fail well before normal service life — NHTSA complaints document failures from roughly 34,000 to 102,000 miles (averaging around 44,000 on the 2000 model year), often preceded by an erratic fuel gauge from the integrated sending unit corroding. GM product bulletins also note that fuel pump module electrical connectors on 1988-2005 vehicles loosen from vibration, creating high-resistance connections. Failure causes sudden stalling at speed (with loss of power steering assist) or a no-start, making this a recurring safety complaint.
records.solution: Replace the complete fuel pump module/sending unit assembly (requires dropping the tank) along with the tank-side wiring connector or pigtail if it shows heat damage. Replacing the fuel filter at the same time and avoiding chronic low-tank running extends the new pump's life.
symptoms: Engine stalls while driving, then restarts after sitting
No-start with no fuel pump hum from the tank
Whining noise from the fuel tank
Erratic or inaccurate fuel gauge readings

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 03V093 - Exterior-Mirror Switch Short Circuit

records.title: Vacuum/Thermal Front Axle Actuator Failure — 4WD Won't Engage Front Wheels
records.description: S-series 4x4s use a front axle disconnect operated by a vacuum-diaphragm actuator (or the notoriously slow thermal linear actuator on early-90s trucks) to couple the front axle after the transfer case shifts. The actuator diaphragm cracks and the small vacuum lines and switch atop the transfer case leak, so the transfer case engages but the front wheels never pull — engagement is also progressively slower in cold weather as the thermal actuator ages. This is one of the most common 4WD complaints on these trucks, documented across years of forum threads and an entire aftermarket fix category.
records.solution: Replace the failed actuator, vacuum switch, and cracked vacuum lines, or permanently convert to a cable-operated engagement system such as the 4x4 Posi-Lok kit, which eliminates the vacuum/thermal mechanism entirely and is the widely accepted long-term fix.
symptoms: 4x4 indicator lights up but front wheels don't pull
Very slow 4WD engagement, worse in cold weather
Transfer case shifts but front axle never engages
Hissing vacuum leak near the transfer case or front differential
4WD engages intermittently or disengages over bumps

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 04V132 - Incorrect Air-Bag Warning Label

records.title: Battery Capacity Degradation Over Time
records.description: The Bolt EV 60/65 kWh battery pack experiences capacity degradation over time, reducing the vehicle range from the original EPA rating. Early 2017-2018 models with the original LG battery showed faster degradation, losing 10-15% capacity in the first 50,000 miles. Vehicles that received the recall battery replacement generally show slower degradation rates. Factors that accelerate degradation include frequent DC fast charging, regularly charging to 100%, leaving the battery at full charge for extended periods, and exposure to extreme heat. The battery management system (BMS) also recalibrates periodically, which can cause sudden apparent range drops.
records.solution: Use the Hilltop Reserve or Target Charge Level feature to limit charging to 80-90% for daily driving — this significantly reduces degradation. Avoid DC fast charging for daily use; save it for road trips. The Bolt EV battery has an 8-year/100,000-mile warranty covering degradation below 60% of original capacity. Vehicles that received the recall battery get a new warranty starting from the replacement date. Monitor battery capacity using the Energy screen or a Torque Pro app with an OBD-II adapter to track state of health over time.
symptoms: Reduced range compared to when vehicle was new
Full charge shows fewer estimated miles
Range drops significantly in cold weather
Battery percentage drops faster than expected

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 18V576 - Rear Brake Caliper Pistons

records.title: High-Voltage Battery Fire Risk Recall (NHTSA 21V-560)
records.description: All 2017-2022 Bolt EV and 2022 Bolt EUV vehicles were subject to a massive recall for battery fire risk. LG Energy Solution manufactured battery cells with two simultaneous defects — a torn anode tab and a folded separator — that could cause an internal short circuit and thermal runaway (fire) during charging, particularly when the battery was charged to 100%. Multiple Bolt EVs caught fire while parked and charging, leading GM to halt sales and production temporarily. GM ultimately replaced every battery module in every affected vehicle at no cost.
records.solution: Check your VIN at my.chevrolet.com/recalls or NHTSA.gov. All affected Bolts receive a FREE complete battery module replacement with updated LG cells that do not have the manufacturing defects. The replacement also includes updated battery management software and an extended 8-year/100,000-mile warranty on the new battery. If you have not had the recall completed, schedule it immediately at any Chevrolet dealer. Until the recall is completed, GM advises: do not charge above 90%, do not deplete below 70 miles of range, do not charge indoors overnight, and park outside away from structures.
symptoms: Recall notification from GM or NHTSA
Charging stopped or limited by vehicle software
Burning smell or smoke from under vehicle (EMERGENCY: call 911)

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 21V560 - High-Voltage Battery Fire Risk

records.title: Cabin Heater Failure in Cold Weather
records.description: The Bolt EV's electric cabin heater (PTC heater) can fail, leaving occupants without heat in cold weather. The heater draws significant battery power and its control module can malfunction, resulting in either no heat output or the "Service High Voltage Charging System" warning. Range is also severely impacted in cold weather due to heater power draw.
records.solution: Diagnose heater control module and PTC heater element. Replacement of the heater assembly or control module resolves the issue. Some owners use seat heaters and a heated steering wheel as a workaround to reduce cabin heater dependency and extend range.
symptoms: No heat output from vents in cold weather
Service High Voltage Charging System message

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 20V184 - Rear Door-Handle Cables

records.title: DC Fast Charging Speed Reduction After Battery Recall
records.description: After the battery recall replacement, many Bolt EV owners report significantly reduced DC fast charging (DCFC) speeds. Where the pre-recall Bolt could sustain 50+ kW at a CCS fast charger, post-recall vehicles often cap at 30-40 kW. GM updated the battery management software to be more conservative with thermal management, limiting charging power to protect the new battery from the conditions that caused the original fire risk. The reduced charging speed adds 15-30 minutes to fast charging sessions on road trips. Cold weather further reduces charging speeds.
records.solution: There is currently no fix — the reduced charging speed is an intentional software limitation by GM to protect the replacement battery. Precondition the battery before arriving at a fast charger by setting navigation to a DC fast charge station (the Bolt will warm the battery en route, improving charging speed by 10-20%). Avoid fast charging when the battery is below 20% or above 80% for best charging rates. Some aftermarket tools can monitor BMS temperature limits, but modifying the charging software voids the battery warranty.
symptoms: DC fast charging peaks at 30-40 kW instead of 50+ kW
Charging sessions take significantly longer than before recall
Charging speed drops rapidly above 50% SOC
Charging extremely slow in cold weather
Battery temperature limiting message during fast charge

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 24V812 - Failed Battery Diagnostic-Software Installation

records.title: Front Drive Motor Bearing Noise
records.description: The front electric drive motor in the Bolt EV develops a whining, humming, or grinding noise from the motor bearings as mileage increases. The single-speed reduction gear unit contains bearings that wear over time, particularly in vehicles driven frequently at highway speeds where the motor spins at high RPM. The noise is speed-dependent (gets louder with speed) and is most noticeable with the radio off and windows up. The Bolt is otherwise a quiet vehicle, making the bearing noise particularly noticeable. Some owners describe it as a "gear whine" that develops after 50,000-80,000 miles.
records.solution: The drive unit bearings are not serviceable individually — the entire drive unit assembly must be replaced or rebuilt. A new drive unit from GM costs $3,000-$5,000 plus $500-$1,000 labor. Some EV specialty shops can rebuild the drive unit with new bearings for $1,500-$2,500. The Bolt EV powertrain warranty covers the drive unit for 8 years/100,000 miles — have the noise documented at a dealer while under warranty. Changing the drive unit fluid (Dexron HP) at 75,000-mile intervals may help prevent premature bearing wear.
symptoms: Whining noise that increases with vehicle speed
Humming or buzzing from front of vehicle
Noise louder during acceleration than coasting
Vibration felt through floorboard at speed

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 20V808 - Front Left Brake Caliper Casting

records.title: Infotainment System Freezing and Black Screen
records.description: The Bolt EV infotainment system frequently freezes, goes to a black screen, or reboots while driving. The touchscreen becomes unresponsive, losing access to climate controls, navigation, and the rearview camera. The issue affects all model years but is most common on 2017-2020 models.
records.solution: Perform a hard reset by holding the power/volume knob for 10+ seconds. Software updates from the dealer may temporarily help. Persistent issues may require infotainment module replacement under warranty or Chevrolet goodwill program.
symptoms: System extremely slow to respond to inputs

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 23V845 - Incorrect Prior Pretensioner Fire Remedy

records.title: Infotainment Screen Ghosting and Flickering
records.description: The 10.2-inch infotainment touchscreen in the Bolt EV develops ghost touch inputs, screen flickering, unresponsive areas, and random screen blackouts. The screen registers phantom touches that change radio stations, adjust climate controls, or activate features without driver input. The issue is caused by a failing digitizer layer in the touchscreen or a loose ribbon cable connection behind the display. Hot weather and direct sunlight on the screen exacerbate the ghosting behavior. The issue affects both the original infotainment system and the updated system in 2020+ models.
records.solution: Perform a system reset by holding the Home and Fast Forward buttons simultaneously for 10 seconds. If ghosting persists, the display panel needs replacement ($500-$1,000 for parts, $200-$400 labor). A loose ribbon cable behind the display can sometimes be reseated without replacing the entire screen — ask the technician to check this first ($100-$200 diagnostic). Some owners have resolved minor ghosting by installing a tempered glass screen protector, which insulates the digitizer from temperature-induced phantom touches.
symptoms: Screen registers touches that did not happen
Screen flickers or goes black intermittently
Ghost touches worse in hot weather or direct sun

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 23V567 - Instrument Panel Air-Bag Perforation

records.title: Cab corners, floor pans and rocker panels rust out at the cab mounts
records.description: The 67-72 C10 cab is a rust trap. The box-section cab supports run from the body mounts to the inner rockers and are spot-welded to both the inner rocker and the floor, so when the rockers and cab corners pack with debris and moisture (the rockers are literally cup-shaped pockets along the bottom of the cab) they rot from the inside out and take the structural cab supports with them. Cab corners behind the rockers are 'almost always rotten,' the lower door pillars rust where the hinges bolt on, and once the supports corrode the cab loses rigidity and can twist/sag on its mounts. This is the single most common reason a 'cheap' C10 turns into a major project.
records.solution: Don't chase pinholes. Restorers cut out and weld in full reproduction cab corners, rocker panels (outer AND inner rocker supports), and a complete one-piece floor pan rather than patching, then re-weld the box-section cab supports so the cab is structurally sound again. Critically: brace the door openings with 1x1 steel tubing before cutting so the cab can't twist while panels are out, restore/replace the rubber cab mount bushings, and after metalwork seal every seam, spray cavity wax/internal frame coating inside the rockers and supports, and re-open the factory drain holes so the new metal doesn't rot from the inside again.
symptoms: Rust bubbling and holes at the lower cab corners and rocker panels
Soft/perforated floor pans under the carpet and pedals
Doors sagging or not latching as cab support sags
Rust at the bottom of the door hinge pillars

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Drop-center frame rust-through at the body mounts
records.description: The drop-center frame that gives the 67-72 its low stance also traps moisture and mud in all the wrong places — most notably where the body mounts bolt through the frame rail and around the rear kick-up over the axle. Decades of trapped grime rust the rails from the inside; by the time it shows on the outside the mount areas can be paper-thin, which is dangerous because the cab/bed mounts and trailing-arm pickups all load those sections. A rotten frame is the difference between a restorable truck and a parts truck.
records.solution: Sandblast or wire-wheel the frame bare and inspect the body-mount and rear kick-up areas with a pick. Repair perforated sections with boxing/repair plate (or source a solid frame from a dry-climate truck), replace ALL the rubber body-mount bushings while it's apart, then protect it for good: internal frame coating sprayed inside the rails through the access holes plus an epoxy-primer/chassis-coat outside. Restorers doing a frame-off take the chance to media-blast, repair, and seal the whole frame so it never rots again.
symptoms: Flaky/scaly rust and perforation at the body-mount pads
Frame sounds dull/thin when tapped near the mounts
Crushed or rotten body mount bushings
Visible rot at the rear frame kick-up over the axle

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 70V094 - Cracking One-Piece Wheels

records.title: External-regulator generator/alternator charging and points ignition are unreliable
records.description: Early 67 trucks used a generator and the rest used a low-output, externally-regulated alternator with a separate mechanical voltage regulator that ages out and either over- or under-charges. Combined with 50-year-old brittle wiring, dirty bulkhead connectors, and breaker-point/condenser ignition that drifts out of tune (dwell and timing wander, points pit and burn), the result is hard starting, dim lights, dead batteries and inconsistent running. Modern accessories (electric fans, stereo, EFI swaps) overwhelm the original output entirely.
records.solution: Convert to a modern internally-regulated single-wire/one-wire alternator (a 10SI/CS-130 style 100A+ unit) using a conversion harness — this deletes the failure-prone external regulator and supports modern loads. On the ignition side, the standard bulletproofing move is an HEI distributor conversion (or a points-to-electronic module) which gives a hotter, maintenance-free spark and stable timing; run the proper 12-gauge switched feed to the HEI. While in there, restorers refresh the bulkhead connector and brittle engine-bay harness so charging and ignition are dead reliable.
symptoms: Battery goes dead / won't hold charge
Ammeter swinging or dim, flickering lights
Hard starting and rough idle as points wear
Need to re-gap points and re-time frequently
Engine 'run-on' or no-charge after HEI/alternator swaps wired wrong

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 70V125 - Carburetor Throttle-Lever Interference

records.title: Four-wheel drum brakes (1967-1970) fade and pull
records.description: 1967-1970 C10s used four-wheel drum brakes on a single-circuit-feel system that is marginal by modern standards. The drums fade badly with repeated or downhill stops, pull to one side when the shoes/wheel cylinders wear unevenly, and the long pedal feels vague — a real safety liability on a heavy truck driven in modern traffic. (Chevrolet only switched the 2WD trucks to front discs and the 5-lug pattern for 1971.)
records.solution: The proven restorer upgrade is a front drum-to-disc conversion kit that bolts to the stock 6-lug spindles, paired with a correct dual-bore disc/drum master cylinder and proportioning valve (and a power booster if desired). This gives fade-free, straight, modern stopping. Many builders go a step further to a 5-lug disc spindle set to open up modern wheel choices. At minimum, restore the drums with new shoes, wheel cylinders, springs and a fresh dual master, but disc conversion is the near-universal bulletproofing path.
symptoms: Brake fade on repeated or downhill stops
Pulling to one side under braking
Grabbing or locking from contaminated/uneven shoes

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 67V005 - Incorrect Brake-Pipe Routing

records.title: Worn rear trailing-arm and front control-arm bushings cause float and rear steer
records.description: Unlike the 3/4-ton trucks, the half-ton C10 2WD uses a coil-spring rear located by two long (~57 inch) trailing arms plus a panhard bar/track bar. The big rubber trailing-arm bushings (and the front upper/lower control-arm bushings and ball joints) perish with age, letting the rear axle move around under power and braking — a vague, floating ride and a feeling that the rear is steering the truck. Tired front bushings and ball joints add to the wander and eat front tires.
records.solution: Replace all the worn bushings — rear trailing-arm bushings front and rear, the panhard/track-bar bushings, and the front upper/lower control-arm bushings — while replacing worn ball joints. Restorers who want sharper handling step up to graphite-impregnated polyurethane (poly) bushings, which are self-lubricating, remove the 'floating' feel and tighten the truck up, and some go to tubular trailing arms/control arms for a full refresh and lowering options. Always do a proper alignment afterward.
symptoms: Floating/wallowing ride and rear-axle 'steer' under power
Clunks from the rear over bumps and on throttle on/off
Front-end wander and clunks, uneven front tire wear
Loose, vague handling on the highway

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Worn steering box and front-end linkage cause vague, wandering steering
records.description: After 50+ years the factory Saginaw recirculating-ball steering box develops slop in the worm/sector, and combined with worn idler arm, tie-rod ends, drag link and ball joints the C10 develops the classic 'wandering' feel where you're constantly correcting and the truck darts on grooved pavement. Many trucks left the factory with manual steering (or the optional ram-assist on early 67s), which only amplifies how heavy and imprecise a tired box feels.
records.solution: First replace the worn linkage — idler arm, tie-rod ends, drag link and ball joints — and set the toe, because a fresh box won't fix worn links. Then either rebuild the original box with a Saginaw rebuild kit and re-set the sector lash, or do the popular bulletproof upgrade: swap to a quick-ratio Saginaw 605/500-series power steering box (with the matching pump, pitman arm and frame-dimple confirmed on 68-72). The result is tight, modern on-center feel that transforms how the truck drives.
symptoms: Excessive play at the wheel before the tires respond
Truck wanders and needs constant correction
Clunk/knock over bumps from worn linkage

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 3.4L V6 (L32) intake and head gasket failure
records.description: The base 3.4L V6 (L32) used in 1993-1995 Camaros has a well-documented gasket weakness. The plastic intake manifold gaskets are considered low quality and commonly break around the coolant ports, leaking coolant and/or oil as they age. More seriously, the 3.4L (1995 and earlier) has a hot spot around one cylinder that tends to blow the head gasket in that one location, leading to coolant loss and overheating. Because coolant can enter a cylinder, a misfire on that cylinder is a common symptom. These leaks, if ignored, cause overheating that can crack the head or warp the deck.
records.solution: Replace the intake manifold gaskets with a quality (upgraded) gasket set for the coolant/oil leak; for head-gasket failure, resurface the head as needed and reassemble with a new head gasket set. Pressure-test the cooling system afterward and address the underlying overheating (thermostat, fan, radiator) so the repair lasts.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no obvious external leak
Oil or coolant seepage at the intake manifold
White exhaust smoke / sweet coolant smell
Oil and coolant mixing (milky oil) in severe cases

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 75V087 - Flexible Cooling-Fan Blade Can Fail

records.title: 3.6L V6 Direct-Injection Intake Valve Carbon Buildup
records.description: The direct-injected 3.6L V6 (LLT/LFX in Gen 5, LGX in Gen 6) sprays fuel directly into the cylinder rather than over the back of the intake valves, so the detergents in gasoline never wash the valves. Over time, oil vapor drawn in through the PCV system bakes onto the intake valves as hard carbon deposits, restricting airflow. This is a well-known DI trait across GM's 3.6L family and is discussed extensively on Camaro/Colorado/Impala forums. Deposits typically become noticeable after 60,000-100,000 miles and are worse on hard-driven or short-trip cars.
records.solution: There is no chemical additive that fully removes hardened intake-valve carbon on a DI engine; the accepted fix is walnut-shell (media) blasting of the intake ports with the intake manifold removed, typically every 60k-100k miles. Installing a catch can / air-oil separator slows future accumulation by keeping oil vapor out of the intake. Symptoms of rough idle, misfire codes, and lost power usually resolve after cleaning.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 09V155 - Positive Battery Cable Can Short at the Starter

records.title: 4L60E automatic transmission 3-4 clutch pack and sun shell failure
records.description: The electronically controlled 4L60E four-speed automatic behind the V6, LT1 and LS1 Camaros has two well-known failure points. The 3-4 clutch pack burns out first: the drum has limited space and thin factory friction plates that wear rapidly under heat and load, so the trans shifts fine through 1st and 2nd but slips or feels like neutral going into 3rd/4th, often with RPM flare on the 2-3 shift. The second is the 'sun shell' (reaction shell), a stamped part prone to fracturing at the hub — when it breaks you typically lose 2nd, 4th and Reverse at once, dropping to 1st and 3rd only. Heat is the primary accelerant on these transmissions; degraded fluid speeds both failures.
records.solution: For a slipping 3-4 clutch or a broken sun shell the fix is a transmission rebuild that includes upgraded (harder) 3-4 clutches and a hardened aftermarket sun shell, plus fresh fluid and a new filter. Adding an auxiliary transmission cooler and keeping the fluid changed on a shorter interval markedly extends life. Catching a slipping 3-4 clutch early (before it damages other components) reduces cost.
symptoms: Slips or feels like neutral shifting into 3rd/4th gear
Loss of 2nd, 4th and Reverse (sun shell failure)

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 72V304 - Improperly Heat-Treated Parking-Brake Pawl Can Fail

records.title: 6L80 6-Speed Automatic 2-3 Upshift Flare / Slip
records.description: Gen 5 Camaros with the 6L80/6L90 six-speed automatic commonly exhibit a 2-3 upshift 'flare' where engine RPM briefly rises before the gear engages, sometimes followed by a firm bump. GM issued bulletins calling a mild 2-3 slip/flare a 'normal characteristic,' but worsening flare typically indicates a real hydraulic leak, most often at the 3-5-Reverse clutch drum or clutch-regulator valve, and can throw pressure/ratio codes. Left unaddressed, slipping accelerates clutch wear.
records.solution: Confirm fluid level/condition and check for pressure codes (e.g., P0776). Mild flare within GM's described range may be lived with; pronounced flare warrants inspecting the 3-5-R drum seals and valve-body regulator valve, a valve-body/clutch repair, or in worst cases a rebuild. Fresh fluid/filter and correct operating temperature help; tuners can also raise line pressure to reduce flare.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 14V409 - Under-Torqued Steering or Control-Arm Fasteners Can Separate

records.title: Big-block cooling shortfall — overheating in traffic
records.description: The tight first-gen engine bay leaves little room for radiator and fan, and the original copper/brass core struggles to shed the heat of a 396 big-block (and a hot 350) in stop-and-go traffic, at idle, or with A/C. Decades of scale and a tired clutch fan or a missing/incorrect fan shroud make it worse, so these cars routinely creep toward the top of the gauge in summer traffic — a real concern for a freshly rebuilt engine.
records.solution: Fit a high-efficiency aluminum radiator sized for the big block. Note the experienced-builder tip: an oversize 2-row aluminum core with large (1.0-1.25 inch) tubes generally out-cools a cheap 3- or 4-row aluminum unit, because too many rows restrict airflow. Add a proper full fan shroud (critical — it forces air through the whole core) and either a correct clutch fan or a high-CFM electric fan/dual-fan setup with a thermostatic switch for idle and traffic. Round it out with a correct thermostat, a 7-lb-plus cap, and back-flushed or new heater/cooling plumbing. Done right the big block stays cool in traffic and on the strip.
symptoms: Temperature climbing in slow traffic, at idle or with A/C on
Boil-over / coolant pushing out the overflow after shutdown
Cooling fine at speed but overheating when stopped
Running hot after an engine rebuild
Steam or sweet smell from the front of the car

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 71V235 - Separated Engine Mount Can Pull the Throttle Open

records.title: A/C Condenser Refrigerant Leak (Weak or No Cold Air)
records.description: The front-mounted A/C condenser and its crimped hose connections are prone to pinhole leaks and stone-strike damage, letting refrigerant escape so the system blows warm. Camaro owners commonly report the condenser leaking at the tubes or at the pressure-hose crimp between condenser and compressor. Because the condenser sits low and forward, road debris accelerates failure, and the leak is often hidden from a quick visual check.
records.solution: Pressure/UV-dye test to locate the leak. A leaking condenser (or the pressure hose) is replaced, then the system is evacuated and recharged to spec; the receiver/drier is typically replaced at the same time. Verify the leak is not simply at an O-ring or Schrader valve before condemning the condenser.
symptoms: A/C blows warm or only mildly cool
Gradual loss of cooling over weeks

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 14V447 - Power-Seat Height Adjuster Bolt Can Fall Out

records.title: Convertible Tonneau Cover / Top Mechanism Binding and Trunk Divider Interlock Faults
records.description: Convertible Camaros commonly develop power-top operating problems involving the tonneau cover, latch alignment, microswitches, hydraulic components, or the required trunk divider/interlock. Owners report the top stopping mid-cycle, warning messages, tonneau covers that will not latch, and repeated need for manual reset procedures. These issues are well represented in owner forums and service bulletins related to top operation and adjustment.
records.solution: Begin with basic checks: confirm the trunk divider is correctly installed, battery voltage is healthy, and no cargo is interfering with the top linkage. Then inspect top position sensors, latch alignment, tonneau cover struts, hydraulic pump/fluid level, and body control module fault history. Repairs range from simple switch adjustment or divider replacement to latch, cylinder, or hydraulic pump service followed by top relearn/calibration.
symptoms: must manually close or reset top

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 13V463 - Sun-Visor Air-Bag Warning Label Can Peel Off

records.title: Cowl and A-pillar rust from clogged cowl drains and a failed hood-to-cowl seal
records.description: The cowl plenum under the vent grille collects leaves and debris, and its drains plug; trapped water then rots the cowl from the inside out and rots the lower corners where the cowl meets the A-pillar and the firewall. The rain-gutter and A-pillar seams are sealed only with seam sealer that cracks with age, letting moisture in behind the A-pillar post. The corner where the hood meets the cowl is a known rot point, made worse when the hood-to-cowl seal is missing so rain and debris hit the outer firewall directly. Because the rot starts inside the double-walled cowl, it is often advanced before it shows, and water leaks into the footwells are an early warning.
records.solution: Pull the cowl vent grille and inspect/clean the plenum; if the inner cowl is perforated, weld in a reproduction cowl vent panel and cowl side panels rather than sealing over rust. Re-open and keep the cowl drains clear, fully seam-seal the rebuilt cowl and the A-pillar/rain-gutter seams, and fit a correct hood-to-cowl seal. Restorers' bulletproofing touch: flush the plenum with cavity wax after repair and, as the forums suggest, run a small drain tube in the lower cowl corner so water can never pool there again — turning the car's worst water trap into a self-draining area.
symptoms: Water dripping onto the kick panels or footwells when it rains or when washing the car
Rust bubbling at the base of the windshield / cowl vent grille
Rot in the lower A-pillar corners and the top of the firewall
Musty carpet and wet floor pans
Debris visible in the cowl vents

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 83V049 - Fiberglass Hood Panels Can Separate

records.title: Excessive Oil Consumption on 6.2L V8 (LS3/L99/LT1)
records.description: Owners of 6.2L V8 Camaros (naturally aspirated LS3/L99 SS and the direct-injected LT1 in Gen 6) report the engine burning noticeably more oil than expected, in many cases 1 quart per 1,000-1,500 miles and sometimes worse under hard driving. Complaints are logged on CarComplaints for multiple model years and are widely discussed on owner forums. Root causes include oil pulled through the PCV/crankcase-ventilation path into the intake, valve-guide/valve-seal wear, and on higher-mileage or hard-driven cars piston-ring wear. Because the LT1 uses direct injection and has no low-oil-level warning that triggers early, some owners discover the problem only when the engine is critically low, risking bearing and top-end damage. This is distinct from the L99 AFM lifter failure already documented.
records.solution: Verify true consumption with a documented oil-consumption test (dealers accept roughly 1 qt/2,000 mi as 'normal' but will investigate worse). Cheap first steps: install a catch can / air-oil separator to stop oil ingestion and check/replace the PCV components. Persistent high consumption points to valve seals or worn rings and may require top-end work or, in severe cases, a short-block/engine replacement, sometimes covered under powertrain warranty if documented early. Use the correct spec oil (5W-30 for LS3/LT1) and monitor level frequently between changes.
symptoms: Blue smoke on startup or hard acceleration
Oil level light or engine damage if run low

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 15V666 - Front Side Air-Bag Inflator Can Rupture

records.title: Front Wheel Bearing / Hub Assembly Failure (Humming, ABS Light)
records.description: The sealed front wheel-bearing/hub assemblies wear out and produce a growing humming, rumbling, or grinding noise that changes pitch when turning or with speed. Because the wheel-speed sensor is integral to the hub, a failed bearing can also set ABS/StabiliTrak faults and light the dash. The bearing is not serviceable separately on these cars; the entire sealed hub must be replaced. Heavier wheel/tire setups and spirited driving accelerate wear.
records.solution: Confirm the noisy side (noise worsens when weight shifts to the bad bearing during cornering) and check for play. Replace the complete sealed hub/bearing assembly; replacing in pairs is recommended if one side has failed from age. A relearn is not usually needed, but the ABS codes clear once the integrated speed sensor is restored.
symptoms: Noise changes when turning left vs right
Vibration felt in the steering wheel
