records.title: Digital LCD Instrument Cluster Failure (1984-1989)
records.description: The 1984-1989 C4's all-digital LCD dash is a notorious failure point now that the electronics are decades old. Heat and vibration crack solder joints on the backlight board connectors and internal power supply, electrolytic capacitors age out, sunlight fades the LCD polarizing film, and the photocell dimmer degrades. The result is a cluster that goes dark, flickers random segments, or becomes unreadable in daylight, leaving the driver without speed, fuel, or temperature information.
records.solution: Rebuild the cluster: re-solder or replace the backlight connectors and power supply components, replace the polarizing film and photocell, and install fresh bulbs. DIY component kits run under $100, while professional cluster rebuilding services handle the complete job.
symptoms: Cluster completely dark with ignition on
Backlighting very dim, too bright, or intermittent
Display faded and only readable with polarized sunglasses or a flashlight
Cluster stuck dim due to a bad photocell

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 86V056 - Headlight Switch Can Flicker or Shut the Headlights Off

records.title: Digital LCD Instrument Cluster Scrambling / Backlight Failure
records.description: The 1990-1996 C4 dash uses analog sweep gauges with a central digital LCD readout (the 1984-1989 cars were fully digital). With age the LCD can scramble into an unreadable mess, especially when the car hits bumps, which is characteristic of a ground/connection problem. Segments drop out, the display flickers, backlight bulbs fail, and the fuel-gauge/'FUEL RATE' readings become erratic. Heat, vibration, aged solder joints, and a degraded polarizer film are the root causes.
records.solution: Send the cluster to a specialist rebuild service (re-solders connections, replaces backlight bulbs, and renews the polarized LCD film), or DIY the polarizer film replacement and re-solder cold joints. For fuel-gauge creep and wrong FUEL RATE readings, repair the ground wire at the center lock pillar on coupes. Cleaning/re-seating cluster ground connections often resolves bump-induced scrambling.
symptoms: Fuel gauge creeping / wrong FUEL RATE reading

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 92V160 - Power-Steering Inlet Hose Can Fracture and Spray Fluid

records.title: Electronic Column Lock (ECL) Failure - NHTSA Recall 04V060
records.description: The electronic column lock system on 1997-2004 C5 Corvettes can fail to unlock when the vehicle is started, leaving the steering wheel locked. The car is designed to shut off fuel above 2 mph if the column stays locked, but if PCM voltage drops the fuel shutoff may not engage and the vehicle can be accelerated while unsteerable. A 'Service Column Lock' or 'Pull Key and Wait 10 Seconds' message often appears on the DIC. GM Recall 04006 (NHTSA 04V060000) covered ~126,624 vehicles; on automatics the lock plate is removed, on manuals the PCM is reflashed and lock plate inspected/replaced. Despite the recall, thousands of owners still report the warning afterward.
records.solution: Verify recall 04006 (NHTSA 04V060000) has been performed - dealers handle free of charge. On automatics the lock plate is physically removed; on manuals the PCM is reprogrammed and lock plate inspected. Aftermarket bypass kits (relay between BCM and lock motor) are available for cars still throwing the message post-recall. Keep battery voltage healthy - low voltage at the PCM is the trigger.
symptoms: Steering wheel will not unlock after starting
Engine cranks but vehicle limited to 2 mph
Intermittent column lock activation while driving

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 04V060 - Electronic Column Lock Can Lock the Steering While Driving

records.title: Fuel Level Sending Unit Failure / Erratic Gas Gauge
records.description: C4 fuel level sending units are a long-standing failure item: corrosion forms where the resistive winding is grounded through a spring, the wiper develops open spots, or the float hangs up against the tank's inner wall. The gauge then sticks on full or empty, jumps erratically, or throws off the trip computer's range display. Owners can unexpectedly run out of fuel, which also risks overheating the in-tank electric fuel pump.
records.solution: Drop the tank or access the sender, then clean the resistive winding and ground contact or replace the sending unit outright — most shops replace the in-tank fuel pump and strainer at the same time since the labor overlaps. New sending units alone run $300 or more.
symptoms: Fuel gauge stuck on full regardless of fuel level
Gauge stuck on empty or reading erratically
Running out of gas with the gauge showing fuel remaining

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 88V017 - Missing Wheel Weld Can Separate the Center from the Rim

records.title: LS1 Excessive Oil Consumption (PCV System and Ring Pack)
records.description: 1997-2002 C5 Corvettes with the LS1 (and 2001-2004 Z06 with LS6) can consume oil at rates of 1 quart per 2,000-3,500 miles or worse. Root causes are blow-by from poor cylinder bore tolerances paired with thin, flat-faced piston rings, exacerbated by a marginal factory PCV system that pools oil in the hoses and pulls it into the intake. The problem hits manual-transmission cars driven hard above 3,200 RPM hardest. GM issued service bulletins acknowledging 'higher than expected oil consumption' on 1999-2002 Corvettes. The LS6 valley cover with its integrated PCV baffle can also seal poorly, sending oil directly into the intake.
records.solution: Install an oil catch can in the PCV return line - many owners report consumption drops from 1 qt/3,500 miles to 1-2 ounces per oil change. Upgrade to LS6-style PCV plumbing on LS1 cars. For LS6, verify valley cover PCV baffle is properly sealed. Use GM-spec 5W-30 (do not run thicker - the LS rings are designed for it). If consumption exceeds 1 qt/1,000 miles, a ring/cylinder reseal is the only permanent fix.
symptoms: Oil pooled in PCV hoses on inspection
Worse with frequent operation above 3,200 RPM

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 97V105 - Torn Fuel-Tank Sender/Pump Seal Can Leak

records.title: Opti-Spark (Optispark) Distributor Failure on LT1/LT4 Engines
records.description: The LT1 (and 1996 LT4) uses a front-of-engine 'Opti-Spark' optical distributor mounted low behind the water pump, driven off the camshaft. It is highly vulnerable to moisture, heat, and ozone. The 1992-1993 units were completely unvented and are notorious for internal condensation and corrosion of the optical sensor disc. The leading real-world cause of failure is a leaking water pump directly above it dripping coolant onto/into the unit, but ordinary humidity and age also kill them. It is one of the single most defining reliability weak points of the 1992-1996 C4.
records.solution: Replace the Opti-Spark distributor (later vented-style unit is the upgrade for 92-93 cars; a vacuum-vented design arrived on 1995-1996 units). Because the water pump sits directly above it and is the most common contaminant source, the accepted practice is to replace the water pump at the same time ('while you're in there'), since the front cover/serpentine and much labor overlaps. Many owners also drill/tap the water pump weep hole and route a hose away from the distributor.
symptoms: No-start (especially after rain or high humidity)
Misfire that worsens when engine/weather is damp

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 90V032 - Rear-Wheel Tie Rod Can Fatigue and Fracture

records.title: Opti-Spark Optical Distributor Failure (LT1)
records.description: The 1992-1996 LT1 uses the Opti-Spark optical distributor mounted low on the front of the engine, directly behind the water pump. Undersized factory vent/drain holes trap condensation, and any coolant seepage from the water pump weep hole or oil from the front crank seal corrodes the optical sensor and internal contacts. When the high-resolution signal degrades, the engine misfires, backfires, and can stall without warning and refuse to restart, often stranding the owner. The 1995-1996 vented design lasts longer but still fails with age.
records.solution: Replace the distributor with a vented (1995-96 style) or upgraded aftermarket Opti-Spark, and replace the water pump at the same time since pump leaks are a primary killer of the new unit. Labor is significant (roughly 4-7 hours) because the water pump, balancer, and accessories must come off; some owners convert to aftermarket coil-pack ignition.
symptoms: Misfire or skip that worsens at higher RPM
Backfiring through the intake or exhaust
Stumbling or stalling in damp weather or after washing the engine
Engine suddenly dies while driving and won't restart

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 91V143 - Front Safety Belts Can Jam in Their Retractors

records.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump / Fuel Sending Unit Failure
records.description: Essentially every 1984-1996 C4 eventually needs its in-tank electric fuel pump. A high-pitched whine from behind the seats is the classic early warning. In-tank connectors become brittle and corroded (adding resistance and overworking the new pump), and the fuel-level sending unit float/rheostat fails, giving inaccurate fuel readings. Ethanol-blend fuels sitting in these older systems accelerate the damage; the original strainer 'sock' also clogs with age.
records.solution: Replace the fuel pump together with the fuel strainer/sock and inspect/replace the in-tank wiring connectors; replace the fuel-level sending unit if gauge readings are off. On C4s this requires dropping/removing the tank. Use fresh fuel and avoid long-term ethanol storage.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 85V118 - Differential Cross Shaft Can Move and Lock the Rear Wheels

records.title: Targa Top and Weatherstrip Water Leaks
records.description: C4 weatherstrip rubber hardens, shrinks, and cracks with age and UV exposure, and the removable targa roof panel relies entirely on these seals. Leaks are most common at the front corners where the windshield A-pillar, targa panel, and door glass meet, and at the lower corners of the rear hatch on coupes. The result is water dripping into the cabin, soaked carpet (which can damage electronics and breed mildew), wind noise, and drafts; a poorly adjusted top or cheap aftermarket rubber makes it worse.
records.solution: Replace the aged weatherstrip with quality seals as a complete kit, adjust the targa top latch/fit per the factory procedure, and maintain the new rubber with weatherstrip lubricant. It is a manageable DIY weekend job; shops charge more for a full reseal.
symptoms: Water dripping at the windshield corner or targa edge in rain or car wash
Wet carpet or damp smell in the cabin
Wind noise at speed around the roof panel or doors
Visibly cracked, hardened, or flattened door/roof seals

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 00V111 - Twisted Lap-Belt Webbing Can Jam the Retractor

records.title: Water Pump Front Seal Leak (Damages Opti-Spark)
records.description: The LT1/LT4 mechanical water pump develops a front seal failure with age, allowing coolant to pass into a chamber that has no outlet except the bottom weep hole. Because the water pump sits directly above the Opti-Spark distributor, the dripping coolant frequently contaminates and destroys the distributor, turning a routine water pump job into a much larger repair. Coolant seeping from the weep hole is the classic warning sign.
records.solution: Replace the water pump when weeping is observed; do not defer, given the Opti-Spark below it. Standard practice is to replace the Opti-Spark at the same time if any contamination has occurred, or proactively since the labor overlaps. Owners commonly drill/tap the weep hole and route clear hose away from the distributor to protect it from any future seepage.
symptoms: Coolant drip/stain from weep hole under front of engine

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 97V044 - Rear Suspension Tie-Rod Links Can Fracture

records.title: ZR-1 LT5 Fuel Injector (Multec) Failure
records.description: The ZR-1's DOHC LT5 uses 16 fuel injectors (primary and secondary sets), and the original Rochester Multec units from this era are known to fail — coil windings short and drop resistance, and the early 1990-1992 injectors were designed before widespread ethanol-blended fuel, which degrades them further. Because the engine runs mostly on its primary injectors, failures show up as rough idle, stumbling, and misfires that integrate-port diagnosis often traces to multiple dead or leaking injectors. Replacement is costly since the plenum must come off and ZR-1 specialists commonly find several failed injectors at once.
records.solution: Remove the plenum and replace or have all 16 injectors professionally refurbished with modern ethanol-resistant equivalents; ZR-1 specialists recommend doing the full set plus seals while the plenum is off rather than chasing individual failures.
symptoms: Check engine light with O2 sensor reading high or low
Fuel smell or fuel-diluted oil from a leaking injector
Knocking noise from the dual-mass flywheel under uneven running

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 90V008 - Incorrect LT5 Fuel-Line Flares Can Crack and Leak

records.title: 6T40 Transmission Shudder (Gen 1)
records.description: The first-generation Cruze with the 6T40 automatic transmission develops a shudder during torque converter lockup in the 25-45 mph range. The torque converter clutch friction material wears and generates debris that contaminates the fluid, worsening the shudder over time in a vicious cycle. The shudder feels like driving over a textured road surface and is most noticeable during gentle acceleration. The 6T40 in the Cruze sees more stress than in larger vehicles because the 1.4T engine produces torque at low RPM, keeping the converter locked more often.
records.solution: Perform a complete transmission fluid exchange (not just a drain and fill) using ACDelco DEXRON VI ATF. Three drain-and-fill cycles with 500 miles of driving between each gives the best results. If the shudder persists after fresh fluid, the torque converter needs replacement ($800-$1,500 including labor). A TCM software update at the dealer can modify lockup behavior to reduce shudder. Change the 6T40 fluid every 30,000 miles to prevent the issue from developing.
symptoms: Rumble strip feeling during gentle acceleration
Harsh or rough shifts between gears

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 16V502 - Replacement Park-Lock Lever Can Permit Rollaway

records.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Failure (1.4T)
records.description: The intake manifold on the 1.4T Cruze has variable-length intake runners controlled by an internal flap actuator. The actuator motor fails or the runner flaps stick due to carbon buildup and oil contamination (especially when the PCV valve cover has also failed). When the runners stick open or closed, the engine loses low-end torque, idles rough, and throws a check engine light. The plastic runner flap pivots can also break, sending debris into the intake port and potentially the cylinder.
records.solution: Clean the intake manifold runner flaps with throttle body cleaner and check the actuator motor for proper operation ($100-$200 for cleaning). If the actuator motor has failed, replacement costs $80-$200 for the part and 1-2 hours of labor. If the runner flaps are broken or cracked, the entire intake manifold assembly must be replaced ($200-$400 for parts, $200-$400 labor). Address any PCV valve cover failures first, as oil contamination from a failed PCV system accelerates carbon buildup on the runner flaps.
symptoms: Check engine light with intake manifold codes
Loss of low-end torque and sluggish acceleration
Rattling noise from intake manifold area

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 13V360 - Brake Vacuum Pump May Not Provide Supplemental Assist

records.title: PCV Valve Cover Failure and Oil Leak (1.4T)
records.description: The 1.4T engine in the first-generation Cruze has the PCV system integrated into the valve cover assembly. The PCV diaphragm ruptures, the check valve fails, or the valve cover gasket deteriorates, causing oil leaks, vacuum leaks, rough idle, and check engine lights. The failed PCV system creates excess crankcase pressure that pushes oil past seals and into the intake manifold. This is the same fundamental design flaw as the Equinox and Malibu 1.5T PCV system. GM released an updated valve cover with improved PCV components.
records.solution: Replace the entire valve cover assembly, which includes the integrated PCV system ($80-$200 for parts). Labor is 1-2 hours ($100-$250). Use the updated GM valve cover design (GM part 55573746 or later revision) with the improved PCV diaphragm. After replacement, check the intake manifold and intercooler for oil contamination — clean any oil found. Also replace the valve cover gasket even if using the same cover, as the gasket is a common secondary leak source.
symptoms: Check engine light with lean or misfire codes
Oil leaking from valve cover area
Whistling or hissing noise from engine (vacuum leak)
Oil in intake manifold or intercooler piping

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 12V288 - Oil Can Collect in the Engine Shield and Ignite

records.title: Turbo Oil Feed Line Leak (1.4T LUJ/LUV)
records.description: The turbocharger oil feed line on the first-generation Cruze 1.4T develops leaks at the banjo fitting connections to the turbo and the engine block. The line uses crush washers that degrade over time, and the line itself can crack due to heat cycling. Oil drips onto the exhaust manifold, creating a burning oil smell and visible smoke from the engine bay. If the oil feed is severely restricted by a damaged line, the turbocharger bearings will be starved of oil and fail catastrophically within a few thousand miles.
records.solution: Replace the turbo oil feed line and both banjo bolt crush washers ($30-$80 for parts). The repair takes 1-2 hours ($100-$250 labor) and requires removal of the engine cover and heat shields for access. Inspect the turbocharger for shaft play while the line is disconnected — excessive play indicates bearing damage from oil starvation. Use a new OEM-style braided line rather than reusing the original rigid line. After the repair, run the engine and check for leaks before reinstalling heat shields.
symptoms: Burning oil smell from engine bay
Oil spots under vehicle near front
Turbo whine or bearing noise developing

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 14V151 - Right Front Half Shaft Can Fracture

records.title: 1.4T Coolant Leak at Water Outlet and Thermostat Housing
records.description: The 2011-2016 Cruze 1.4L turbo engine has chronic coolant leaks from the water outlet housing and thermostat housing. These plastic components crack from heat cycling. The turbo coolant feed and return lines also develop leaks at the crimped rubber-to-metal connections. Some owners report replacing the water outlet multiple times.
symptoms: Sweet coolant smell from engine bay
Visible coolant residue on water outlet or thermostat housing

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 12V289 - Fuel-Tank Strap Bracket Welds May Be Missing

records.title: 1.5L Turbo Charge Air Cooler (Intercooler) Condensation Restricting Airflow — Underboost / Reduced Engine Power
records.description: On 1.5L turbo (LYX) Equinox models, moisture accumulates inside the charge air cooler (intercooler) and, in cold or highly humid weather, can freeze or pool enough to severely restrict intake airflow. This trips turbo underboost/MAP faults and pushes the engine into 'Engine Power Reduced' limp mode with sluggish acceleration. A related GM TSB also documents the charge air cooler outlet tube separating from the throttle body on 2018-2022 1.5L turbo models, producing the same reduced-power symptom. This is distinct from the known coolant-loss/intercooler-condensation head-gasket issue — here the failure is airflow restriction and boost loss, not coolant consumption.
records.solution: Inspect and reseat or replace the charge air cooler outlet duct/clamp at the throttle body per GM TSB; clear accumulated condensate from the intercooler; verify the CAC and ducting for cracks. Reprogram the ECM if a related calibration update applies. Some owners drill a small factory-spec weep provision or follow the TSB ducting repair.
symptoms: Engine Power Reduced warning / limp mode
Loss of acceleration and turbo boost
Worse in cold or humid weather

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 22V724 - Driver-Seat Height-Adjust Pivot Bolt Can Be Loose or Stripped

records.title: 1.5L turbo coolant loss / overheating (head gasket & intercooler condensation)
records.description: The 1.5L turbo (LYX) in 2018+ Equinox is reported to lose coolant with no obvious external leak, leading to overheating and, in some cases, head-gasket failure (coolant entering the combustion chamber). Owners describe the coolant level dropping over time with overheating events. Separately, the early 1.5L turbo had an intercooler/charge-pipe condensation problem in very cold climates where moisture freezes and blocks airflow, triggering reduced-power conditions; GM updated the intercooler and charge-pipe design on later builds.
records.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and perform a combustion-gas (block) test to confirm head-gasket involvement when coolant disappears without an external leak. Repair/replace the head gasket as needed and inspect for warpage. For cold-climate condensation/limp-mode complaints, install the updated intercooler and charge-pipe parts. Monitor coolant level and address overheating immediately to avoid further engine damage.
symptoms: Coolant level drops with no visible leak
White exhaust smoke or sweet smell
Reduced engine power / limp mode in cold weather
Coolant in oil or low coolant warnings

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 1.5L Turbo Fuel Injector Leak Causing Misfire, Fuel Odor and Rough Running
records.description: The direct-injection fuel injectors on the 1.5L turbo can leak - internally past a cracked injector body/tip (dumping raw fuel into the cylinder and causing a misfire) or externally past worn upper O-rings (fuel smell, weeping at the rail). This is distinct from the covered high-pressure fuel-pump and in-tank fuel-pump-module failures. GM issued a Customer Satisfaction Program for a fuel-injector leak on some 2025 Equinox that directs dealers to replace all four injectors and the fuel feed pipe.
records.solution: Diagnose with fuel trims, a misfire counter, and a visual/smell check at the fuel rail. Replace the leaking injector - GM guidance for the 2025 program replaces all four injectors, the rail bolts, and the fuel feed intermediate pipe. For O-ring-only external leaks, new upper O-rings may suffice. Check for any open Customer Satisfaction Program by VIN. Repairs commonly $750-$1,000.
symptoms: Strong fuel smell, especially at idle
Visible fuel weeping at the injector/rail

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 1.5L Turbo Intake Valve Carbon Buildup Causing Misfires and Rough Cold Start (GDI)
records.description: Because the 1.5L turbo (and the earlier 2.4L SIDI) is a gasoline direct-injection engine, no fuel washes over the back of the intake valves. Over 40k-80k miles, oil vapor from the PCV system bakes onto the valves as hard carbon, restricting airflow and disrupting the seal. Owners report a check-engine light with single- or multi-cylinder misfires that are worst on a cold start, plus a slight loss of power and rougher idle. GM technical document PIP5029E acknowledges misfires caused by 'major carbon build up on the intake and/or exhaust valves.'
records.solution: Confirm with fuel trims and a borescope of the intake valves. The definitive fix is walnut-shell media blasting of the intake ports to physically remove the deposits (typically $300-$600). Top-tier fuel and periodic intake/induction cleaners (e.g., CRC GDI IVD, GM Top Engine Cleaner) slow accumulation but will not fully clear heavy deposits. Address any leaking PCV/oil-separator that is feeding oil vapor into the intake, and keep to shorter oil-change intervals to reduce future buildup.
symptoms: Check engine light with misfire codes
Rough or shaky idle, worst on cold start
Slight loss of power and fuel economy
Occasional stumble that may not always be felt by the driver

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 22V929 - Passenger Classification System May Not Disable the Air Bag

records.title: 1.6L Diesel NOx Sensor Failure / DEF System Faults Causing Reduced Power and Limp Mode
records.description: The diesel Equinox (1.6L LH7) is prone to NOx-sensor and diesel-exhaust-fluid (DEF/SCR) emissions faults. Failing or out-of-calibration NOx sensors and reductant-injection problems set codes such as P11DB (NOx sensor 1 performance) and P249D (closed-loop reductant control at limit), trigger a 'service emissions system' warning with a countdown, and ultimately force the vehicle into a speed-limited limp mode to protect the SCR catalyst. Owners report repeat failures because GM revised the NOx sensors multiple times. A holed/leaking charge-air cooler can also let unmetered air in and mimic the same emissions faults, so the intake must be checked too. This is a high-stakes, expensive emissions issue for the relatively rare but enthusiast-tracked diesel.
records.solution: Scan and record all emissions DTCs (e.g., P11DB, P249D) and freeze-frame data. Verify DEF quality and the DEF/reductant injector and pump operation, then test the upstream/downstream NOx sensors against live SCR data. Replace the failed NOx sensor with the latest revised GM part for this engine (verify the exact PN by VIN, as GM issued multiple revisions — a wrong NOx sensor will not resolve the fault). Inspect the charge-air cooler and intake for leaks/holes that can trigger the same limp mode. After repair, perform the required relearn/forced regeneration and confirm the countdown/limp-mode clears.
symptoms: 'Service emissions system' / DEF warning with mileage or speed-limit countdown
Reduced engine power and limp mode at low speed
Check-engine light with NOx/SCR codes (P11DB, P249D)

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 23V339 - Excess Coating Can Block Child-Seat LATCH Anchors

records.title: 2.4L Ecotec excessive oil consumption (worn/stuck oil-control piston rings)
records.description: The 2.4L Ecotec (LAF/LEA) four-cylinder used in 2010-2017 Equinox (and its GMC Terrain twin) consumes oil at an abnormal rate — frequently as much as 1 quart per 1,000-2,000 miles — due to low-tension/stuck oil-control piston rings combined with PCV-system issues that draw oil past the rings. Owners report blue exhaust smoke on startup and acceleration, low-oil warnings between changes, and in severe cases engine damage when the oil level drops unnoticed. GM acknowledged the defect in a 2015 service bulletin instructing dealers to replace the four piston assemblies on affected engines, and nearly 400 NHTSA complaints describe the same failure. A $42M class-action settlement (final approval Nov 2019) covered 2010-2013 vehicles, and a January 2023 suit extended claims to 2014-2017 units.
records.solution: Have an oil-consumption test performed (documented quart-per-mile measurement) to qualify for goodwill/settlement coverage. The proper repair is replacement of all four piston assemblies with updated rings; clean or replace the PCV orifice and check for carbon buildup. Check oil at every fuel fill as an interim measure to avoid running low. If out of coverage, expect ring/piston replacement or, where the engine was damaged from oil starvation, a long-block replacement.
symptoms: Low oil level between changes / oil light comes on
Blue smoke from exhaust on startup or acceleration
Burning more than 1 quart per 1,000-2,000 miles
Engine knock or damage if run low on oil

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 2.4L Ecotec timing/balance chain stretch from tensioner & low oil
records.description: The 2.4L Ecotec in 2010-2017 Equinox is prone to premature timing-chain and balance-chain stretch, driven primarily by a collapsing chain tensioner and made worse by the engine's known oil-consumption problem (low oil reduces hydraulic pressure to the tensioner). Symptoms are a rattle at cold startup, a check-engine light, and rough running or loss of power. Because the engine is an interference design, a chain that skips timing far enough lets the valves contact the pistons, turning a maintenance item into an engine-destroying failure. GM issued Special Coverage Adjustment 12313D covering premature timing/balance chain wear on certain 2010-2011 2.4L engines.
records.solution: Diagnose with cam/crank correlation codes and inspect chain stretch. Replace the full timing chain kit (chains, guides, tensioners) and the balance chain; correct any underlying oil consumption first or the new chain will wear early. Address promptly at first rattle — driving on a stretched chain risks valve-to-piston contact and a totaled engine.
symptoms: Check engine light with cam-crank correlation codes

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 2.4L Exhaust Manifold Cracking Causing Exhaust Leak and Cabin Fumes
records.description: The integrated exhaust manifold on the 2.4L Ecotec is prone to cracking, producing a loud ticking/exhaust-leak sound that is loudest on a cold start and can fade as the metal expands. Beyond the noise, the leak can allow exhaust fumes into the cabin and set oxygen-sensor/misfire-adjacent codes. The problem is often aggravated by the 2.4L's well-known oil consumption (a clogged converter raises backpressure) and repeat failures within a couple of years are commonly reported.
records.solution: Inspect the manifold cold for cracks and check for a leaking manifold-to-pipe gasket and broken/rusted studs. Replace the cracked manifold (or the integrated manifold/converter assembly on federal-emissions cars) with new gaskets and studs. Address underlying oil consumption to protect the new converter. Repairs typically $400-$900 depending on whether the catalytic section is integrated.
symptoms: Loud ticking/tapping exhaust leak on cold start
Noise quiets as engine warms up
Reduced power / possible check engine light
Rusted or broken exhaust manifold studs

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 3.0L / 3.6L V6 Timing Chain Stretch Causing Rattle and P0008/P0016 Codes
records.description: GM's high-feature V6 in the Equinox suffers premature timing-chain stretch, distinct from the covered 2.4L chain issue. Worn chains/guides/tensioners throw off cam-to-crank timing, setting P0008/P0009 (engine position performance) and P0016-P0019 (crank/cam correlation). The classic symptom is a rattle or chain-slap on cold start from the front/passenger side of the engine. Long oil-change intervals and low oil accelerate the wear; left unfixed, a chain can jump time or break and bend valves.
records.solution: Verify with the correlation codes and a cam-timing check; do not keep driving with active correlation codes. Replace the timing chains, guides, and tensioners as a complete updated kit (both banks on the V6), and change oil on time with the correct spec afterward. This is a labor-intensive repair, commonly $2,000-$3,500.
symptoms: Rattle/chain-slap on cold start from front of engine
Check engine light with timing-correlation codes
Rough idle, hesitation, loss of power
Possible no-start if timing has jumped

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 6T70/6T75 transmission shudder, hard shifts & 3-5-reverse wave plate failure
records.description: Equinox models with the GM 6T70/6T75 six-speed automatic suffer shudder, harsh or delayed shifts, slipping, and loss of reverse. A common root cause is failure of the 3-5-reverse wave plate, which can crack and cause extreme shudder when reverse is engaged and eventual loss of drive. Overheated/degraded fluid that loses viscosity accelerates internal wear. Failures typically appear between roughly 60,000 and 150,000 miles. Owners report bucking when engaging gear, failure to shift out of 2nd, and inability to engage reverse.
records.solution: Service the fluid on a strict interval (and after any overheating). For wave-plate failure, the transmission must be removed and rebuilt with the updated/stronger wave plate; a fluid-and-filter service alone will not fix a cracked wave plate. Verify a current 6T70 software/calibration update is installed to address shudder/shift quality.
symptoms: Slipping or failure to move from a stop
Stuck in gear / won't shift out of 2nd

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 04V302 - Ignition-Key Park-Lock Cable Can Be Misadjusted

records.title: Brake Pressure Modulator Valve Corrosion Causing ABS Malfunction and Extended Stops
records.description: A known safety issue on later first-generation Equinox models involves corrosion in the brake pressure modulator valve (BPMV), which can cause the ABS to activate improperly at low speeds. Owners report a sudden buzzing pedal, unexpected increase in stopping distance, and the vehicle seeming to roll through a stop on dry pavement. This problem was serious enough to trigger a GM safety recall in salt-belt states.
records.solution: Diagnosis includes scanning the ABS module, checking wheel speed sensor data, and inspecting whether the vehicle falls under the recall population. The recall remedy involved installing a corrosion-resistant protective coating and, in some cases, replacing the BPMV. If the recall has not been completed, owners should verify VIN status with GM or NHTSA immediately.
symptoms: ABS activates at low speed on dry pavement
ABS warning light in some cases

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 07V520 - A-Pillar Trim Needs Additional Impact Protection

records.title: A/C Compressor Self-Destructs and Contaminates the Entire System With Metal Debris
records.description: A well-documented and expensive failure mode: the A/C compressor on the 2010-2017 Equinox platform fails internally and grenades, shedding fine aluminum/metal particles ("black death") that circulate through the entire refrigerant system. Owners notice the A/C suddenly stops blowing cold, sometimes with a grinding/clunking noise or a seized clutch. Because the debris contaminates the condenser, lines, orifice/expansion device, and accumulator, simply bolting on a new compressor causes the replacement to fail almost immediately. A proper repair requires replacing the compressor AND condenser/accumulator and thoroughly flushing the system. This drives repair bills well above a simple compressor swap and is a top owner complaint on these years.
records.solution: When the compressor has failed internally, do not just replace it. Replace the A/C compressor and the condenser and accumulator/receiver-drier, replace the orifice tube/expansion valve, and flush all serviceable lines and the evaporator until clean of metal debris. Pull a proper vacuum, recharge to spec, and add the correct PAG oil charge. Compressor part numbers vary by year/engine on this platform (e.g., ACDelco 15-22343 and 15-22276 for 2010-2011, 15-22330 for 2015-2017), so verify the exact PN by VIN before ordering. Skipping the flush/condenser is the most common reason a replacement compressor fails again quickly.
symptoms: A/C suddenly blows warm and never cools again
Grinding, clunking, or rattling from the compressor; seized or chattering clutch
Metal/aluminum debris found in the refrigerant or accumulator
Replacement compressor fails shortly after install (system not flushed)
High repair estimate because condenser and lines are contaminated

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 19V704 - Incorrect Rear-Caliper Lubricant Can Cause Brake Drag

records.title: A/C condenser refrigerant leak (warm air from vents)
records.description: The air-conditioning condenser on the Equinox commonly develops refrigerant leaks at its tubes and seals, or from stone-chip damage to the front-mounted core. Because the condenser's internal tubes and seals cannot be serviced individually, a leak requires full condenser replacement. The classic symptom is the A/C blowing warm air, often with an oily, grimy residue visible on the condenser where refrigerant and PAG oil have escaped. This is a frequently reported wear item across multiple model years, especially 2016-2017.
records.solution: Perform a dye/electronic leak test to confirm the condenser is the source. Replace the A/C condenser, evacuate and recharge the system to spec, and replace the receiver/drier or desiccant as recommended. Inspect for stone-chip damage and consider a condenser guard in high-debris environments.
symptoms: Refrigerant low on recharge / repeat recharges needed

records.title: Catalytic Converter Failure (P0420) Caused by Oil-Burning — GM Special Coverage 15810
records.description: On the 2.4L Ecotec Equinox, the catalytic converter is frequently destroyed by the engine's chronic oil consumption (worn piston rings) — burned oil coats and thermally damages the catalyst, setting P0420 (catalyst efficiency below threshold) and the check-engine light. Replacing only the converter without first fixing the oil-consumption root cause leads to rapid re-failure of the new cat. GM acknowledged the thermal/erosion converter failures with Special Coverage 15810, extending coverage to 10 years / 120,000 miles on affected 2010-2011 LAF-engine vehicles. This is a high-demand search because owners face an expensive converter plus the underlying ring/oil repair, and aftermarket "universal" cats often won't clear the code.
records.solution: Diagnose P0420 properly (verify upstream/downstream O2 behavior; rule out exhaust leaks and bad O2 sensors). Critically, fix the oil-consumption root cause first — perform the GM oil-consumption repair (piston rings, per the applicable GM oil-consumption PI/TSB) or the new converter will fail again. Replace with a quality OE-grade catalytic converter (cheap universal cats often won't keep P0420 from returning). Check eligibility for GM Special Coverage 15810 (10 yr / 120k mi) on 2010-2011 LAF vehicles for converter replacement. Clear codes and run a drive cycle to confirm the catalyst monitor passes.
symptoms: Check-engine light with code P0420 (catalyst efficiency below threshold)
Elevated oil consumption preceding the converter failure
Reduced fuel economy and sluggish performance
Repeat P0420 after a cheap aftermarket cat was installed

records.title: Cold-Start Rough Running and Stalling From ECM Software Anomaly (1.5L Turbo)
records.description: GM technical guidance documents 2018-2019 Equinox models with the four-cylinder turbo engine running rough and/or stalling on a cold start with the malfunction indicator lamp illuminated. Performance smooths out once the engine warms. The condition is caused by an engine control module software anomaly, with DTC P050D found set/stored in history. Owners experience repeated cold-start stumble, near-stalls, or actual stalls in cold morning starts.
records.solution: Reprogram the ECM with the latest GM calibrations per the TSB using a GM-authorized programming tool with current software (maintaining stable battery voltage during the flash), then clear all DTCs. The reprogramming is typically covered under powertrain warranty.
symptoms: Stalling shortly after a cold start

records.title: Coolant Surge Tank / Reservoir Cracking Causing Slow Coolant Loss
records.description: The plastic coolant surge/recovery tank on second-generation (2010-2017) Equinox becomes brittle from years of heat and pressure cycling and develops hairline cracks, most often at the seams or around the cap neck. This causes a slow, mysterious coolant loss with occasional sweet smell and pink/orange residue near the front of the engine, and if ignored can progress to overheating. This is distinct from the 1.5T head-gasket coolant loss and the 3.4L V6 head-gasket leak.
records.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system to confirm the tank (not a hose, water pump, or radiator) is the source. Replace the surge tank and its cap with a new assembly; plastic-weld repairs rarely hold under pressure. Refill with the correct DEX-COOL and bleed the system. Parts are inexpensive (aftermarket tanks ~$30-$80, GM assembly more); total job typically $150-$400.
symptoms: Gradually dropping coolant level with no obvious puddle
Dried pink/orange residue on or below the reservoir
Visible crack or seepage at the tank seam or cap

records.title: Door Striker Fracture — Door Can Open Unexpectedly While Driving (Recall 23V869000)
records.description: GM recalled certain 2024 Chevrolet Equinox (gas) vehicles — along with the Blazer, Blazer EV and GMC Terrain — because door strikers supplied by Brano Group A.S. may not have been heat-treated to GM hardness specifications and can fracture. A broken striker can allow a door to open unexpectedly while the vehicle is being driven, increasing the risk of injury or a crash. The gas Equinox portion of the campaign covers a small build window (about 201 Equinox units).
records.solution: Under recall 23V869000, dealers replace all four door strikers and attaching bolts free of charge. Owners can check eligibility by VIN at NHTSA.gov or call Chevrolet customer service at 1-800-222-1020.

records.title: Engine-driven brake vacuum pump failure causing sudden hard brake pedal
records.description: Third-generation Equinox (2018-2022) uses a camshaft-driven mechanical vacuum pump mounted at the rear of the cylinder head to supply the brake booster (the turbo intake is pressurized, so there is no manifold vacuum). This pump can seize and its drive gear break, suddenly eliminating brake assist — the pedal becomes 'hard as a rock' with greatly increased stopping distances. In severe cases the pump shatters and sends metal debris into the engine, causing catastrophic internal damage. NHTSA has over 300 complaints; a related GM recall (19V645000) reprogrammed the brake control module on other models but excluded the Equinox/Terrain, and a February 2026 class action (Thieme v. General Motors) targets 2018-2022 Equinox/Terrain.
records.solution: If the brake pedal suddenly goes hard, stop driving and tow the vehicle — continued driving risks a crash and possible engine destruction. Replace the failed vacuum pump (and brake booster if damaged); inspect for metal debris in the engine if the pump came apart. Check VIN for any applicable recall/special coverage and document the complaint with NHTSA.
symptoms: Greatly increased stopping distance / loss of power assist
Noise from rear of engine before failure

records.description: GM recalled certain 2025-2026 Chevrolet Equinox EV models (and Cadillac Optiq) equipped with optional 21-inch Continental CrossContact RX 275/40R21 all-season tires (RPO QLT). Continental found that tires built during DOT week 4024 (week of October 6, 2024) had inadequate sulfur in the tread-base rubber compound, which can prevent proper adhesion and lead to partial or full tread detachment — raising crash risk. The campaign covers roughly 19,000 Equinox EVs of the ~22,900 total vehicles.
records.solution: Under recall 25V704000, dealers inspect all four tires and replace any built during DOT week 4024 at no cost; owners who already replaced affected tires may seek reimbursement from Continental. Check the tire sidewall DOT code for '4024' and verify by VIN at NHTSA.gov.
symptoms: Vibration or noise from a tire

records.title: Equinox EV: Adaptive Cruise Control Fails to Apply Brakes Hard Enough (Recall 25V012000)
records.description: GM recalled approximately 2,890 model year 2025 Chevrolet Equinox EV all-wheel-drive vehicles (those NOT equipped with Super Cruise) because incorrect brake system control module software can cause the adaptive cruise control system to fail to engage the friction brakes as expected. When a vehicle cuts in front, the Equinox EV may try to slow using regenerative braking torque alone rather than applying the hydraulic brakes aggressively enough, increasing the risk of a collision.
records.solution: Under recall 25V012000, dealers (or an over-the-air update) install corrected brake system control module software at no cost. Owners can verify by VIN at NHTSA.gov or call Chevrolet at 1-800-222-1020.
symptoms: Adaptive cruise control does not brake firmly for cut-in vehicles
Vehicle relies on regen braking instead of hydraulic brakes

records.title: Equinox EV: Pedestrian Alert Sound Too Quiet at Low Speeds (Recalls 24V925000 / 25V639000 / 25V878000)
records.description: Multiple recalls address the Equinox EV's exterior pedestrian warning sound (required on EVs at low speed) being too quiet or not varying enough in volume between standstill and creeping speeds, due to incorrect body control module / sound system software calibration. Pedestrians — especially those who are blind or have low vision — may not hear the vehicle approaching, increasing the risk of a pedestrian crash. The campaigns span the 2024 model year (25V639000), 2025 (24V925000), and a large ~81,000-vehicle 2025-2026 campaign (25V878000).
records.solution: Dealers update the body control module / pedestrian alert sound software (some via over-the-air update) to meet the minimum-sound standard, free of charge under the applicable recall. Owners can check by VIN at NHTSA.gov.
symptoms: Little or no exterior warning sound at low speed

records.title: Equinox EV: Vehicle-Control Software Defect Causing Sudden Loss of Propulsion
records.description: In early 2026 GM launched a broad recall covering roughly 102,000 Chevrolet Equinox EVs (primarily 2024-2026 model years) over a vehicle-control / propulsion software defect that can cause an unexpected loss of power or loss of propulsion while driving. Related field reports describe limp-home behavior, propulsion/stability warnings, and in some cases state-of-charge readings dropping suddenly toward zero, leaving the vehicle stranded. A separate GM customer-satisfaction program covers the drive motor power-distribution control module hardware on some Equinox EV and Blazer EV units. Sudden loss of propulsion in traffic raises the risk of a crash.
records.solution: GM's remedy is a software update (typically dealer-installed, some over-the-air) to correct the propulsion/power-loss logic; the related hardware program replaces the drive motor power-distribution control module and associated parts at no cost. Owners experiencing propulsion or stability warnings should stop driving and schedule service, and verify open recalls by VIN at NHTSA.gov.
symptoms: Sudden loss of power / propulsion while driving

records.title: Continental Tire Tread Separation Recall (21-inch All-Season)
records.description: Certain Equinox EVs fitted with 21-inch Continental CrossContact tires were built with a nonconforming tread-base rubber compound (inadequate sulfur level) from Continental DOT manufacturing week 4024 (week of Oct 6, 2024). The defective compound can allow partial or full tread detachment at speed, risking loss of control. This is NHTSA recall 25V704 (GM N252525030), covering roughly 22,900 vehicles (Equinox EV plus Cadillac Optiq); the 21-inch tires are standard on RS and optional on LT1/LT2.
records.solution: Under recall 25V704, dealers inspect all four tires and replace any tire manufactured during DOT week 4024 free of charge. Owners who already paid for replacement can apply to Continental for reimbursement. Check the DOT date code stamped on the tire sidewall.
symptoms: Vibration or thumping from a tire at speed
Visible tread lifting, bulging, or chunking on the tread/sidewall
Loss of vehicle control from tread detachment

records.title: Front Footwell Water Leak (HVAC Drain / Body Seam Seal)
records.description: Owners of 2024-2025 Equinox EVs report water pooling in the front (often passenger) footwell, especially with A/C running while driving or after rain. GM traced it to the HVAC drain tube becoming disconnected from the bulkhead and to gaps in the body seam sealer under the carpet, and issued Service Update N252528650 / TSB 25-NA-149 directing dealers to water-test, reseal the body seam, and reconnect the drain. Standing water risks soaked carpet, odor/mold, and corrosion of underfloor electrical connectors.
records.solution: Per GM TSB 25-NA-149 / Service Update N252528650, technicians pull back the carpet, inspect and reseat the HVAC drain tube, confirm the leak with a water test, and seal the body seam with compound (no parts required). Dealers also remediate unsold lot inventory. Dry out carpet/padding to prevent mold.
symptoms: Water pooling in the front (often passenger) footwell
Wet or soaked carpet and floor padding
Leak appears mainly with A/C on while driving
Musty / mildew odor in the cabin

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 24V737 - Improperly Heat-Treated Door Strikers Can Break

records.title: High-Voltage Battery Fault / Sudden State-of-Charge Drop to 0% (Bricking)
records.description: Some Equinox EV owners have experienced high-voltage battery faults where the vehicle abruptly drops from a healthy state of charge to 0% and loses all drive power, requiring a tow, sometimes preceded by an in-app 'high-voltage battery' warning. A widely reported case (Tom Moloughney's ~9,500-mile Equinox EV dropping from 46% to 0%) is documented by InsideEVs. NHTSA characterizes this as a software error usually cleared by resetting codes; note it is a shared GM Ultium phenomenon (also Blazer EV, Cadillac Lyriq/Optiq/Vistiq) and is rare relative to fleet size, and is distinct from the separate 12V auxiliary-battery bricking issue.
records.solution: Treat any sudden drop to 0% or a high-voltage warning as a fault: stop, use roadside assistance, and have the vehicle towed to a GM EV-certified dealer to pull BMS logs. Reported fixes to date involve clearing error codes / software updates (and in some cases correcting a corroded battery-cable pin or a failing 12V battery) under warranty; keep the vehicle on the latest BMS/control software.
symptoms: App or cluster high-voltage battery fault warning
State of charge dropping suddenly from a normal level to 0%
Complete loss of drive power requiring a tow
Vehicle temporarily unresponsive / non-recognition of charger

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 24V925 - Pedestrian Alert Sound May Be Too Quiet

records.title: LED Headlamp Snow and Slush Buildup (Winter Visibility)
records.description: In snow and slush, the Equinox EV's deeply recessed LED headlamps progressively pack with snow/ice and dim or black out, because the LEDs produce almost no waste heat to melt accumulation (unlike halogen units) and the deep-set lens design traps buildup. Owners across the Equinox EV forum and complaint sites report having to stop and manually clear the lamps during winter driving, a genuine nighttime visibility/safety concern.
records.solution: No factory fix or recall; mitigation is owner-side. Periodically stop and manually clear snow/slush from the headlamp recesses, apply a hydrophobic coating, or fit aftermarket lens protection. There is no headlight washer/heater on these units, so proactive clearing in heavy snow is required.
symptoms: Headlights dim or go dark in snow/slush
Visible snow or ice packed into the headlamp recess
Reduced forward visibility at night in winter
Need to stop and manually clear the lamps repeatedly

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 25V878 - Pedestrian Alert Sound Change Is Insufficient

records.title: Loss of Propulsion / Vehicle Control Software Defect (Power-Loss Recall)
records.description: A vehicle-control software defect can cause the 2025 Equinox EV to unexpectedly lose propulsion or fail to operate as intended while driving, with owners reporting sudden power drops, hesitation, stalling, or propulsion/stability warnings. GM issued an early-2026 recall of roughly 100,000+ Equinox EVs (2025-2026 model years) to correct propulsion-control logic; the root cause is software calibration in the vehicle's control modules, not hardware failure.
records.solution: Dealer software/calibration update to the affected vehicle-control modules at no cost under the recall. Owners should run their VIN through the NHTSA or Chevrolet recall lookup; if any propulsion or stability warning appears while driving, stop and schedule service immediately.
symptoms: Sudden, unexpected loss of motive power while driving
Reduced power / failure to accelerate (limp behavior)
Propulsion or stability warning messages on the cluster
Vehicle disabling itself requiring a tow

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 26V114 - Electronic Owner Manual May Not Download

records.title: Slow DC Fast Charging and Early Thermal Derating
records.description: The Equinox EV underdelivers on DC fast charging relative to rivals: independent tests show peak power drops sharply (thermal derate) after roughly 10 minutes, falling from ~154 kW to as low as ~63 kW by ~29% SOC, with 10-80% sessions taking ~50 minutes on both 150 kW and 350 kW stations. The cause is the pack's low ~288 V nominal architecture (requiring very high amperage to hit peak) plus conservative battery thermal management on this first-generation Ultium platform. Owners also report occasional charging stalls/handshake failures at public stations.
records.solution: Pre-condition the battery before fast charging when possible, use high-current stations, and keep the vehicle on the latest software (GM has tuned charging behavior via updates). Persistent stalls at one station should be reported and rechecked against another charger to isolate vehicle- vs. charger-side faults. This is a platform characteristic, not a recall.
symptoms: DC fast-charge rate well below the rated peak
Charge speed drops sharply after about 10 minutes (thermal derate)
Minimal benefit from 350 kW vs 150 kW stations
Charging session stalls or fails to initiate at public chargers

records.title: EVAP Canister Purge Valve Stuck Open Causing P0496 / Rough Running (3.0L & 3.6L V6)
records.description: The vapor-canister purge solenoid on the V6 Equinox (and Terrain) commonly fails stuck-open, letting fuel vapor flow into the intake when it shouldn't. This sets DTC P0496 (EVAP flow during a non-purge condition) and sometimes P0455/P0446, illuminates the check-engine light, and can cause a rough/rich idle, hard starting, and even a faint fuel smell. It is one of the most frequently replaced emissions parts on the V6 Equinox because the valve is a known weak point and the repair is cheap and easy. The valve sits on top of the engine and is a roughly one-hour DIY job.
records.solution: Confirm P0496 and inspect the purge-valve vacuum lines for cracks and the connector for damage before replacing. Replace the vapor canister purge valve with the GM/ACDelco OE part 12690512 (supersedes 12610560). After replacement, clear codes and run a drive cycle to confirm the EVAP monitor passes and the light stays off. Also verify the gas cap and EVAP lines if leak codes (P0455/P0446) accompany the purge code.
symptoms: Check-engine light with code P0496 (sometimes P0455/P0446)
Rough or rich idle, occasional stumble
Hard starting, especially right after refueling

records.title: Front Wheel Bearing and Hub Assembly Failure Triggering ABS/Traction Warnings
records.description: Premature front wheel bearing and hub assembly wear is a common issue on the 2005-2009 Equinox. Owners often first notice a humming or growling noise that changes with speed, followed by ABS or traction control warnings when the integrated wheel speed sensor signal becomes erratic. Because the sensor is built into the hub on many replacements, a failing hub can create both noise and brake/traction system faults.
records.solution: Diagnosis involves road-testing for bearing noise, checking for wheel play, and scanning ABS data for an intermittent or weak wheel speed signal. The standard repair is replacement of the affected hub assembly, often in pairs if both sides are noisy or high-mileage. After replacement, technicians should verify sensor wiring condition and clear any stored ABS codes.
symptoms: humming or growling from front wheels

records.title: Head Gasket Coolant Leak and Overheating on 3.4L V6
records.description: The first-generation Equinox commonly uses the GM 3.4L LA1 V6, and owners have repeatedly reported coolant loss, overheating, and eventual head gasket failure. In many cases the problem starts as an external or internal coolant leak, then progresses to overheating, rough running, white exhaust smoke, or coolant contamination. This issue is well documented in owner complaints and repair discussions for the 2005-2009 Equinox/Torrent platform.
records.solution: Diagnosis usually includes pressure-testing the cooling system, checking for combustion gases in the coolant, inspecting for coolant loss with no visible leak, and verifying whether the engine has been overheated. Repair typically involves replacing the head gaskets, checking head flatness, resurfacing if needed, and replacing related components such as intake gaskets, head bolts, thermostat, and coolant. If overheating was severe, the cylinder heads or engine may also need machine work or replacement.

records.title: Heater Core and HVAC Case Water Leak Causing Wet Passenger Floor
records.description: A recurring complaint on first-generation Equinox models is water or coolant intrusion into the passenger-side floor area. Owners report either a leaking heater core/coolant smell inside the cabin or water entering through HVAC case drains and cowl sealing issues, leaving carpets soaked and windows fogged. The problem can lead to mold, electrical connector corrosion under the carpet, and persistent interior odor.
records.solution: The source needs to be identified first: coolant residue and sweet odor point toward the heater core, while clear water after rain or A/C use suggests a blocked evaporator drain or body sealing issue. Repairs may include heater core replacement, clearing the A/C drain, resealing cowl/body seams, and drying the carpet and underlayment thoroughly to prevent mold and connector damage.

records.title: High-Pressure Direct-Injection Fuel Pump Failure Causing Stalling and Limp Mode (1.5L Turbo)
records.description: Owners of 2023-2024 Equinox models with the 1.5L turbo (LYX) report the engine-mounted high-pressure direct-injection fuel pump failing, often well under 60,000 miles (some as early as 28,000 miles). The pump can no longer maintain rail pressure, so the engine suddenly loses power, drops into 'Engine Power Reduced' limp mode (speed limited to roughly 5-55 mph), stalls, or won't restart, frequently leaving the vehicle undrivable and requiring a tow. CarComplaints logged 20 distinct 2023 fuel/propulsion complaints centered on this part, and many owners report the replacement pump being on national back-order for months. This is a separate failure from the earlier 2021-2022 in-tank low-pressure fuel pump module recall.
records.solution: Dealer diagnoses low fuel-rail pressure and replaces the high-pressure fuel pump (and gaskets); some cases also require fuel injectors or rail cleaning. Out of warranty, repairs have run roughly $1,000-$1,100. Owners should check for any GM warranty extension or special coverage and verify it is the high-pressure pump (not the in-tank module) before paying out of pocket.
symptoms: Sudden loss of power / stalling while driving
Engine Power Reduced / limp mode (speed capped 5-55 mph)
No-start or vehicle must be towed

records.title: HVAC Blend Door Actuator Failure Causing Clicking Noise and Incorrect Temperature/Airflow
records.description: A common first-generation Equinox/Torrent problem is failure of one or more HVAC door actuators, especially the temperature blend and mode actuators. Owners report repetitive clicking or knocking from behind the dash, inability to switch between defrost/floor/panel modes, or heat stuck hot/cold on one side. GM service information and owner reports point to stripped plastic gears or an actuator that loses calibration after battery disconnect or normal wear.
records.solution: Diagnose by commanding HVAC mode and temperature changes while listening for actuator clicking under the dash and verifying door movement with a scan tool or visual inspection where accessible. Recalibration can help if the actuator has only lost position, but most cases require replacing the failed actuator and then performing HVAC recalibration. Access can be time-consuming depending on which actuator failed.
symptoms: air only blows from defrost or floor vents
noise starts after key-on or after battery replacement
