records.title: P0174 — System Too Lean (Bank 2) from Failed EVAP Purge Valve / Intake Manifold Gasket Leak on the 3.5L & 3.6L V6
records.description: P0174 (lean, Bank 2) only sets on the V6 Malibus (3.5L LX9 in 2004-2007 and 3.6L LY7/LLT in 2008-2012), since the four-cylinder Malibus have only one bank. On these V6s the classic trigger is unmetered air reaching the cylinders on the bank opposite cylinder 1: a stuck-open or leaking EVAP purge solenoid (a widely reported GM 3.6L failure that drives both P0171 and P0174), a torn PCV/intake air hose, or an intake manifold gasket leaking vacuum to one bank. The ECM adds fuel to compensate, long-term fuel trims on Bank 2 climb past the +25% threshold, and the code sets.
records.solution: Confirm the lean condition with a scan tool (Bank 2 long-term fuel trim high) and perform a smoke test of the intake and EVAP system. Replace the EVAP purge valve if it fails closed/leaks, repair any torn PCV or intake boot hoses, and replace the intake manifold gasket if the leak is at the manifold. Clean or replace the MAF sensor if fuel trims are skewed on both banks. Re-check trims after repair.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 13V566 - Power-Seat Harness Can Chafe and Short

records.title: P0302 — Cylinder 2 Misfire from Failed Ignition Coil or Fouled Spark Plug
records.description: P0302 on the Malibu is most often a failing ignition coil or a worn/fouled spark plug at cylinder 2. On the four-cylinder Ecotec engines (2.2L, 2.4L, 2.5L) each cylinder has its own coil, so when the #2 coil weakens it can no longer produce a strong enough spark and that cylinder misfires. A carbon-fouled, worn, or wrong-gap plug at #2 does the same. Because oil consumption on the 2.4L can foul plugs prematurely, a repeat P0302 there can point back to that engine's oil-burning tendency. A flashing check-engine light with this code means raw fuel is reaching the catalytic converter and driving should stop.
records.solution: Swap the cylinder 2 ignition coil with an adjacent cylinder and clear codes — if the misfire follows the coil to the new cylinder, replace the coil. If P0302 stays on cylinder 2, inspect and replace the spark plug (check for oil/carbon fouling and correct gap). Replace worn plugs as a set and, if plugs foul repeatedly, investigate oil consumption or a leaking injector.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 04V188 - Front Seat-Belt Anchor Can Disconnect

records.title: P0303 — Cylinder 3 Misfire from Ignition Coil/Plug or Intake-Valve Carbon Buildup on the 1.5L Turbo
records.description: P0303 (cylinder 3 misfire) shows up frequently on the 2016-2018 Malibu 1.5L turbo (LFV) and is discussed heavily on the Malibu forums. The direct-injected 1.5T is prone to carbon buildup on the intake valves, which disrupts airflow and causes lean/rough combustion and misfires; a GM service bulletin describes misfire conditions from significant carbon buildup due to incomplete fuel burn. On top of that, a weak coil or worn spark plug at cylinder 3 is the classic ignition-side cause. Fuel injector #3 problems and PCV/vacuum leaks can contribute. Because the difference between a plug and a valve-carbon repair is large, proper diagnosis matters.
records.solution: Inspect and, if worn/fouled, replace the cylinder 3 spark plug; swap the #3 coil with an adjacent one to see if the misfire follows it and replace the coil if so. If ignition parts are good and misfire persists, check for carbon buildup on the intake valves (per GM bulletin) and perform a walnut-blast/intake-valve cleaning; verify injector #3 and check for vacuum/PCV leaks. Stop driving if the CEL flashes to protect the catalytic converter.
symptoms: Hesitation and loss of power on acceleration

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 04V094 - Sun-Visor Air-Bag Labels Can Be Incorrect

records.title: P0420 — Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1) from Oil-Consumption-Poisoned Converter on the 2.4L Ecotec
records.description: The single most common P0420 pattern on the Malibu is on the 2008-2012 2.4L Ecotec (LE5/LE9), whose low-tension piston rings are notorious for excessive oil consumption. Burned oil sends phosphorus and other contaminants into the exhaust, which glazes and poisons the catalytic converter. The downstream O2 sensor eventually mirrors the upstream sensor, telling the ECM the converter is no longer storing oxygen, and P0420 sets. The 2.5L (2013-2015) and 2.0L/1.5L turbos see it too, usually from a failed PCV in the valve cover or an aging original converter. Replacing the cat without fixing oil consumption first will kill the new one.
records.solution: Confirm no exhaust leaks, misfires, or slow O2 sensors first. Check oil consumption — if the engine burns oil, repair that (PCV valve-cover replacement on turbos, or piston-ring/short-block repair on the 2.4L) before touching the converter. Once the source is corrected, replace the Bank 1 catalytic converter (or the failed downstream O2 sensor if that is the actual fault) and clear the code.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 05V486 - Tire Label Lists the Wrong Spare Size

records.title: P0430 — Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2) from Aged/Failed Rear-Bank Converter on the V6
records.description: Like P0174, P0430 only applies to the V6 Malibus (3.5L 2004-2007, 3.6L 2008-2012) because it monitors the converter on Bank 2 — the rear/opposite bank from cylinder 1. On these V6s the code is almost always a worn-out rear-bank three-way catalytic converter that can no longer store oxygen, so the Bank 2 downstream O2 sensor tracks the upstream sensor too closely. A lazy Bank 2 downstream O2 sensor, an exhaust leak ahead of the sensor, or a rich condition (bad MAF/injector) can produce the same code, so those must be ruled out before condemning the converter.
records.solution: Verify there are no exhaust leaks near the Bank 2 sensors and no misfires or rich-mixture faults. Compare Bank 2 upstream vs downstream O2 waveforms; if the downstream sensor is switching in step with the upstream one, replace the Bank 2 catalytic converter. If the downstream sensor itself is slow/biased, replace that sensor instead. Clear and re-run the catalyst monitor.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 14V247 - Brake Vacuum Assist Can Be Lost

records.title: P0442 — Small EVAP Leak from Gas Cap O-Ring or Purge Valve (Capless Filler Seal on 2016+)
records.description: P0442 flags a small EVAP leak (roughly a 0.020-0.040 inch hole). On 2012-2016 Malibus with a conventional threaded gas cap, the most common cause is a cracked or flattened cap O-ring. On the 2016+ ninth-gen cars with the capless fuel filler, the culprit is usually the filler-neck seal or debris holding the spring-loaded flap slightly open. On all years, a leaking or weak EVAP purge valve — a well-known failure across GM platforms of this era — is the next most likely source. Cracked charcoal-canister hoses round out the list.
records.solution: Start with the cheapest checks: inspect/replace the gas cap and O-ring (or clear debris and inspect the capless filler seal on 2016+). If that does not resolve it, replace the EVAP purge valve. When the simple items check out, run a professional smoke test to pinpoint the leak (canister, hoses, or vent valve) and repair the leaking component.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 12V460 - Four-Speed Shift-Cable Tabs Can Fracture

records.title: P0455 — Gross EVAP Leak from Loose/Failed Gas Cap or Stuck Purge Valve
records.description: P0455 indicates a large EVAP leak (a hole ~0.040 inch or bigger). On the Malibu the leading cause — more than half of cases across GM cars of this era — is a loose, missing, or failed fuel cap (or, on 2016+ capless cars, a bad filler-neck seal). The second most common cause is a failed EVAP purge valve stuck open, a notoriously common GM failure shared across the Impala, Camaro, and others. Cracked or disconnected canister/vent hoses can also let enough vapor escape to trip the gross-leak monitor.
records.solution: Confirm the gas cap is present, tight, and its seal is intact (or inspect the capless filler seal on 2016+). If the cap is fine, replace the EVAP purge valve. If the code persists, smoke-test the system to find the large leak — commonly a cracked canister hose or a failed vent valve — and repair it.
symptoms: Fuel cap warning message in some models

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 09V073 - Shift-Cable Adjustment Clip Can Permit Rollaway

records.title: Passlock Anti-Theft System Causing No-Start and Intermittent Stalling
records.description: A common failure on early-2000s Malibu models is the Passlock security system falsely detecting a theft condition, which can disable fuel delivery and prevent the engine from starting. Owners report the SECURITY light flashing, long wait times before restart, and in some cases intermittent stalling or crank-no-start behavior. The root cause is typically failure in the ignition lock cylinder sensor/housing or related wiring causing incorrect resistance/voltage readings to the body control module.
records.solution: Diagnosis usually starts by checking for SECURITY lamp behavior, BCM-related codes, and verifying Passlock sensor data during crank. Repairs commonly involve replacing the ignition lock cylinder housing/switch assembly, repairing wiring at the column, and performing the Passlock relearn procedure. Some owners also replace the ignition switch if heat-related internal contact failure is present.
symptoms: SECURITY light flashing or staying on
Random no-start especially in hot weather

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 14V400 - Ignition Switch Can Move Out of Run

records.title: Electric Power Steering Motor Failure
records.description: The 2013+ Malibu uses an electric power steering (EPS) system with a column-mounted motor that is prone to failure. The motor develops internal faults causing intermittent or complete loss of power steering assist, making the car extremely difficult to steer at low speeds. GM issued TSB 18-NA-205 and NHTSA investigated numerous complaints. The steering column module and torque sensor can also fail, triggering a "Service Power Steering" message on the DIC.
records.solution: Have the EPS motor and torque sensor diagnosed with a scan tool — the module stores specific fault codes. Replacement of the EPS motor assembly costs $400-$800 for parts and $200-$400 for labor. In some cases, a software recalibration of the EPS module resolves intermittent faults. Check for applicable GM TSBs, as some vehicles may qualify for extended warranty coverage. Never ignore a power steering warning — sudden loss of assist at highway speed is a safety hazard.
symptoms: Intermittent loss and return of power assist
Steering wheel jerks or pulls to one side
Warning light clears after restart but returns

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 16V502 - Electronic Park-Lock Lever Can Permit Rollaway

records.title: Trunk Latch and Release Failure
records.description: The trunk latch mechanism on the Malibu fails due to a worn release cable, broken latch spring, or faulty trunk release actuator motor. Owners report the trunk will not open via the key fob, interior button, or the trunk release button on the lid. In some cases, the trunk will not latch closed and pops open while driving. Water intrusion into the latch mechanism accelerates corrosion and failure, especially in northern salt-belt states.
records.solution: Replace the trunk latch assembly ($50-$150 for the part) and inspect the release cable for fraying or binding. Labor is typically 1-2 hours ($100-$200). If the trunk will not open at all, access the latch through the rear seat pass-through (fold down the center armrest) and manually release it. Lubricate the latch mechanism with white lithium grease after replacement to prevent future corrosion. Check the trunk seal for damage that may be allowing water into the latch area.
symptoms: Trunk will not open from key fob or button
Trunk pops open unexpectedly while driving
Trunk release button clicks but trunk does not open
Have to slam trunk multiple times to latch
Grinding noise from trunk latch area

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 15V164 - Sunroof Switch Can Be Pressed Inadvertently

records.title: CV Joint Boot Tear and Joint Failure
records.description: CV joint boots tear allowing grease to escape and contamination to enter. Joint then develops clicking noise and eventually fails. Lightweight construction means shorter boot life.
records.solution: Replace CV axle assembly. Not worth rebooting — complete axle with new joints is inexpensive for this car.

citations.title: NHTSA Complaint ODI 10491875 - corrosion below rear doors
NHTSA Complaint ODI 10328473 - rocker-panel corrosion

records.title: Head Gasket Leak
records.description: Small Suzuki-sourced engines develop head gasket leaks, especially if overheated even once. 1.0L 3-cylinder particularly vulnerable due to thin gasket design.
records.solution: Replace head gasket. Check head for warpage. Replace thermostat and cooling system components as preventive measure.

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Severe Underbody and Rocker Panel Rust
records.description: Thin body panels and minimal undercoating cause rapid rust-through on rocker panels, floor pans, and wheel arches. Particularly bad in salt-belt states.
records.solution: For early rust, grind, treat with rust converter, and apply rubberized undercoating. Severe rust may make vehicle uneconomical to repair — body panels rust through.
symptoms: Visible rust bubbles on rocker panels

citations.title: NHTSA Complaint ODI 10376488 - frame rust and control-arm separation
NHTSA Complaint ODI 10313790 - excessive frame corrosion
NHTSA Complaint ODI 10306235 - body separated from frame
NHTSA Complaint ODI 10263599 - unibody control-arm support detached

records.title: 3.8L V6 Intake Manifold Gasket and Coolant Elbow Leak
records.description: The 3.8L Series II V6 develops intake manifold gasket leaks and the plastic coolant elbow on the front of the engine cracks. The supercharged SS models also have supercharger snout wear causing boost leaks.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 15V701 - Front Valve-Cover Oil Leak Can Cause an Engine Fire

records.title: 3.8L Supercharger Snout Coupler Wear (SS Models)
records.description: The Monte Carlo SS uses the 3800 Series II Supercharged (L67) engine. The plastic coupler connecting the supercharger snout to the rotor assembly wears out, creating a loud rattling noise at idle that sounds like a broken component. Despite the alarming noise, this is a minor maintenance item unique to the supercharged models. The supercharger oil also needs periodic replacement.
symptoms: Rattling or rock-crusher noise from supercharger at idle
Reduced supercharger whine indicating worn coupler
Slight boost loss in advanced cases

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 14V400 - Ignition Switch Can Move Out of Run on 2000-2005 Vehicles
NHTSA Recall 14V355 - Ignition Switch Can Move Out of Run on 2006-2007 Vehicles

records.title: Power Window Regulator Cable Failure
records.description: The cable-style window regulators in 2000-2007 Monte Carlos fail when the cable stretches, frays, or binds on the reel. The window can drop into the door or become stuck partway. Both front windows are commonly affected. Replacement regulators with added cable guides are an improvement over the original design.
symptoms: Window drops into door panel suddenly
Window moves unevenly or at an angle
Grinding or popping noise when operating window
Motor runs but window does not move

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 00V244 - Air-Bag Sensing Module Memory Error Can Prevent Deployment

records.title: Air Conditioning Stops Cooling — Expansion Valve Jamming
records.description: A chronic and widely reported air-conditioning fault affects second-generation Onix and Onix Plus models (2020+), with similar AC complaints also common on the first generation. The system cools normally for the first few minutes after start-up, then begins blowing warm air even though the compressor stays engaged and refrigerant pressure reads normal; cooling temporarily returns after the car is shut off and restarted. Brazilian AC specialists traced the recurring fault to the expansion valve jamming, which drastically reduces suction in the circuit. Because gauge pressures look normal, shops frequently misdiagnose the problem and replace the compressor (around R$2,000) without fixing anything. The original valve design is considered flawed, so replacement with the same OEM part can fail again; some specialists fit an alternative valve for durability. Complaints about the Onix AC blowing hot air and 'vinegar smell' from the vents are among the most common entries for the model on Reclame Aqui and the Opinautos defect database.
records.solution: Replace the AC expansion valve (part approximately R$300) rather than the compressor — confirm the diagnosis by checking evaporator suction behavior, not just static pressures. Replace the cabin filter and sanitize the evaporator if there is a sour smell. Under factory warranty, Chevrolet dealers replace the valve free of charge; out of warranty, some specialists install a more durable alternative valve to prevent recurrence.
symptoms: AC cools at first, then blows warm air after a few minutes
Compressor stays engaged but no cold air comes out
Cooling returns temporarily after turning the car off and on
Sour or vinegar-like smell from the vents
Weak airflow from dash vents in hot weather

citations.title: Chevrolet Brasil Official Recall Catalogue
Chevrolet Brasil Owner Manuals

records.title: Engine Fire Risk from ECM Calibration Defect — 1.0 Turbo (Brazil Recall)
records.description: Shortly after the second-generation Onix launched in Brazil, GM recalled 19,055 Onix Plus model-year 2020 sedans (produced April 29 to November 6, 2019, chassis LG100091-LG139164) because a faulty engine control module calibration on the new 1.0 turbo three-cylinder could cause abnormal pressure and temperature in the combustion chamber under certain conditions of atmospheric pressure, humidity and fuel composition. The resulting pre-ignition could break pistons, connecting rods or even the engine block, letting hot oil spray onto exhaust components and ignite. At least one vehicle fire was reported in Brazil's Northeast and another occurred at the Gravataí factory, and videos of burning units pressured Procon-SP to notify GM before the recall was formalized in November 2019. Some owners subsequently reported reduced power after the recalibration.
records.solution: Free ECM software recalibration at any Chevrolet Brazil dealership (recall service started November 18, 2019; GM offered loaner cars during repairs). Check recall completion on any used MY2020 Onix Plus/Onix 1.0 turbo via the Chevrolet Brasil recall portal using the chassis number. If the engine already suffered piston or block damage, GM replaced engine components under the campaign/warranty.
symptoms: Sudden loss of power while driving
Loud knocking or metallic banging from the engine
Oil leaking under the engine bay
Smoke or flames from the engine compartment
Check engine light after hard acceleration

citations.title: Chevrolet Brasil Official Recall Catalogue

records.title: Fuel Pump Retaining Nut Leak — Fire Risk Recall (2013-2014)
records.description: In December 2014, GM do Brasil recalled 400,940 vehicles — Chevrolet Onix and Prisma model years 2013-2014, plus Cobalt 2012-2014 and Spin 2013-2014 — because the plastic retaining nut that secures the fuel pump module to the top of the fuel tank could fail to seal properly. In atypical situations such as a rollover, the defect could allow continuous fuel leakage which, in contact with an external ignition source, could start a fire with risk of injury to occupants and third parties. The recall was publicized by Brazil's Ministry of Justice consumer-protection recall alert system. GM stated it had no confirmed fires linked to the defect at the time of the campaign. The free repair (replacement of the retaining nut or, where necessary, the entire fuel tank) takes about one hour.
records.solution: Verify recall completion on any 2013-2014 Onix/Prisma using the chassis number via the Chevrolet Brasil recall portal or a dealer — Brazilian recalls have no expiration date and the fix is free. The service replaces the fuel pump retaining nut (or the fuel tank if sealing surfaces are damaged). Any persistent fuel smell, especially after filling the tank, should be inspected immediately.
symptoms: Gasoline or ethanol smell near the rear of the car
Fuel odor stronger after filling the tank completely
Damp spots or fuel stains on top of the tank area
Fuel leak visible under the rear of the vehicle

citations.title: Chevrolet Brasil Official Recall Catalogue

records.title: MyLink Infotainment Freezing, Black Screen and Wireless Android Auto Dropouts
records.description: Owners of 2020-2023 Onix and Onix Plus report recurring failures of the MyLink infotainment system: the screen freezes on the boot logo or with a frozen image, flickers or goes black, the touchscreen and hard buttons stop responding, and the unit reboots randomly. A separate but related software defect causes wireless Android Auto to disconnect intermittently with a 'Wi-Fi interference' message. Because the reversing camera displays through the head unit, a frozen or black screen also takes out the camera image. Complaints are concentrated on Reclame Aqui and the Clube do Onix owner forum across MY2020-2023 vehicles, and GM's fix is a software update applied via official USB pendrive at dealerships — some out-of-warranty owners report being charged for the update, which itself generated complaints.
records.solution: Have the dealer apply the latest MyLink firmware update (official GM pendrive procedure) — free under warranty. A temporary workaround for a frozen screen is a system reboot (hold the power button, or lock/unlock the car and let it sleep). For wireless Android Auto dropouts, updating both the head unit firmware and using a quality USB cable connection avoids the Wi-Fi interference bug. Persistent hardware-level failures require head unit replacement under warranty.
symptoms: Screen frozen on the MyLink boot logo
Screen flickers, blinks or goes black while driving
Wireless Android Auto disconnects with Wi-Fi interference message
Reverse camera image unavailable when screen freezes

citations.title: Chevrolet Brasil Official Recall Catalogue
Chevrolet Brasil Owner Manuals

records.title: Premature Failure of Oil-Bathed Timing Belt (1.0 Turbo CSS Prime)
records.description: The second-generation Onix and Onix Plus 1.0 turbo (CSS Prime three-cylinder, introduced 2019 for MY2020) use a timing belt that runs immersed in engine oil. GM rates the belt for 240,000 km or 15 years, but Brazilian owners, mechanics and the automotive press have documented widespread premature degradation and outright belt failures between roughly 50,000 and 100,000 km — sometimes under 50,000 km. Oil that does not meet the required Dexos specification (0W-20 for naturally aspirated, 5W-30 for turbo), extended oil-change intervals, sludge or contaminated fuel attacks the belt rubber, which dries, sheds teeth and disintegrates; debris can also clog the oil pickup. When the belt snaps on this interference engine, pistons strike valves and the repair can involve a full cylinder head rebuild or engine replacement, easily exceeding R$10,000. The problem became serious enough that GM South America announced a service action to inspect and replace belts on affected Onix, Onix Plus, Tracker and Montana units, while many warranty claims were initially denied over oil-spec documentation.
records.solution: Use only Dexos-certified oil of the exact specification (5W-30 Dexos 1 for the turbo) and change it strictly on schedule at shorter real-world intervals. Independent Brazilian mechanics recommend preventive belt replacement around 60,000-70,000 km instead of the 240,000 km book interval. Have the belt inspected for swelling, cracking or tooth loss at every oil change; if debris is found in the oil, replace the belt and clean the oil pickup. Vehicles with documented dealer maintenance can claim the GM verification/replacement campaign or warranty coverage.
symptoms: Ticking or rattling noise from the timing cover area
Rubber debris or dark sludge found in the engine oil
Check engine light with cam/crank correlation faults
Engine cranks but will not start after belt failure
Sudden engine stop with loss of power steering assist

citations.title: Chevrolet Academy - Oil-Bathed Timing Belt Guidance
Chevrolet Brasil Official Recall Catalogue

records.title: Underhood Fuse Box Water Ingress — Unintended Starter Activation and Fire Risk Recall (2017-2019)
records.description: GM do Brasil recalled Onix and Prisma (along with Cobalt and Spin) vehicles produced between 2016 and 2018 — model years 2017 to 2019 — plus vehicles that received genuine GM replacement fuse boxes in 2018, because the underhood fuse box relay terminals could be installed without adequate insulating protection. Water entering and accumulating at the relay terminals in the engine compartment can cause a short circuit that triggers involuntary, continuous activation of the starter motor. The constantly-engaged starter can overheat to the point of fire, and on a manual-transmission car left parked in gear the cranking starter can move the vehicle on its own. The fix is a 20-minute free service in which the dealer applies insulating sealant to the fuse box relay terminals.
records.solution: Check recall completion by chassis number on the Chevrolet Brasil recall portal or by phone (0800 702 4200); the insulation service is free and takes about 20 minutes. Warning signs — the starter cranking by itself, clicking from the underhood fuse box after rain or engine washing, or a burning smell — mean the car should be parked away from structures, the battery disconnected, and the dealer service performed immediately. Never leave an unrepaired manual-transmission car parked in gear.
symptoms: Starter motor cranks by itself with the key out
Clicking sounds from the underhood fuse box after rain or washing
Burning smell from the engine bay
Car lurches or creeps while parked in gear
Intermittent no-start or electrical faults in wet weather

records.title: Excessive Oil Consumption
records.description: Toyota 1ZZ-FE engine (shared with Corolla) consumes excessive oil due to piston ring design. Can burn 1 quart every 1,000-2,000 miles. Toyota issued a TSB for Corolla with same engine.
records.solution: Monitor oil level frequently and top off between changes. Permanent fix requires piston ring replacement which is often not cost-effective. Some owners switch to 5W-30 from 5W-20.
symptoms: Catalytic converter failure from oil fouling

records.title: Oxygen Sensor Failure
records.description: Oxygen sensors fail causing poor fuel economy and check engine light. Both upstream and downstream sensors prone to failure. Oil consumption issues accelerate sensor fouling.
records.solution: Replace failed oxygen sensor(s). Use Denso or NTK OEM-quality sensors. Address any oil consumption issue to prevent premature fouling of new sensor.

records.title: Rear Strut Mount Noise and Wear
records.description: Rear strut mounts wear causing clunking noise over bumps and poor ride quality. Rubber mounts deteriorate and bearing fails.
records.solution: Replace rear strut assemblies with mounts. Quick-strut assemblies include mount, spring, and strut as pre-assembled unit for easier install.
symptoms: Clunking noise from rear over bumps
Knocking when going over speed bumps

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 10E002 - Aftermarket Front Strut Mount Missing Weld

records.title: 2.2L Four-Cylinder Head Gasket Failure
records.description: The 2.2L OHV four-cylinder (base engine from 1994 on, replacing the 2.5L Iron Duke) is well known among owners for head gasket failure, frequently following an overheat event. Once the gasket lets go, combustion gases, coolant, and oil cross-contaminate; repeated overheating also warps the head and can crack it. It is one of the most commonly cited S-10 2.2L complaints, part of the broader GM 2.0/2.2/2.4 head-failure reputation.
records.solution: Replace the head gasket with new head bolts; have the cylinder head resurfaced (milled) and pressure-tested at a machine shop to rule out a crack or warpage, and replace valve seals while it is off. Address the root-cause cooling issue (thermostat, radiator, fan) to prevent recurrence.
symptoms: Loss of coolant with no external leak

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 94V228 - Brake-Booster Vacuum Hose Can Detach

records.title: 4.3L Vortec CSFI "Spider" Injector Poppet Valve Leaking/Clogging
records.description: The 1996+ 4.3L Vortec V6 uses a Central Sequential Fuel Injection (CSFI) 'spider' assembly under the upper intake plenum: a central injector body with flexible nylon tubes feeding poppet-valve nozzles at each intake port. Residual fuel bakes into varnish on the ball-to-seat face, so the poppets clog and, more importantly, lose their ability to seal, leaking fuel into the intake and opening at the wrong pressure. This is one of the most-documented S-10 4.3L driveability faults. GM issued warranty extension 99066F (to 10yr/200k mi) covering the poppet spray nozzles on 1996-2003 CSFI systems, confirming its prevalence.
records.solution: Replace the CSFI spider assembly. The accepted permanent fix is the updated MPFI (multi-port) conversion spider, a direct-fit unit that uses conventional injectors with proper needle-and-seat sealing instead of the failure-prone poppets. A spider-plug/fuel-pressure test isolates a leaking poppet before replacement.
symptoms: Hard starting / long crank (especially hot restart)
Hesitation and loss of power on acceleration
Fuel smell and drop in fuel economy

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 95V180 - Cooling-Fan Blade Can Separate

records.title: 4.3L Vortec Lower Intake Manifold Gasket Coolant Leak
records.description: The 4.3L V6's lower intake manifold gaskets (original composite/plastic-carrier design) degrade with heat cycling and age, typically failing in the ~100k-150k mile range. Because the intake manifold and heads expand at different rates, the gasket seal breaks down and lets coolant leak — externally into the valley/engine bay or, worse, internally into the crankcase or intake, diluting the oil and risking bearing damage before it is noticed. A classic GM Vortec 4.3L failure shared across the Astro/Blazer/S-10 family.
records.solution: Replace the lower intake manifold gaskets with upgraded Fel-Pro rubber-coated metal-carrier gaskets rather than the OE plastic units; clean and chase the head bolt holes and torque to spec. Confirm the oil has not been coolant-contaminated; if it has, an engine flush and inspection is warranted.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no obvious external leak
Coolant seeping in the intake valley / around manifold
Rough running if coolant enters intake

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 97V208 - Underhood Harness Clip Can Cause a Fire

records.title: 4L60E Automatic Transmission 3-4 Clutch and Sunshell Failure
records.description: S-10s with the electronically controlled 4L60E four-speed automatic (introduced in trucks for 1993, behind the 4.3L) commonly suffer 3-4 clutch pack burnup and a cracked/stripped factory sunshell ('reaction shell'). The OE 3-4 clutch discs wear and burn, causing slip when shifting to 3rd/overdrive; the weak sunshell fractures at the hub and causes loss of reverse plus 2nd/4th. Related weak points include the plastic 1-2 accumulator and the 2-4 band. Heat and towing accelerate failure.
records.solution: Rebuild the transmission with upgraded internals: heavy-duty 3-4 clutch pack, a hardened aftermarket sunshell, updated valve-body/accumulator parts, and a new 2-4 band. Regular fluid and filter service plus an added cooler reduce recurrence. A shift that flares or 'skips' 2nd-to-4th is the classic 3-4 clutch symptom; sudden loss of reverse points to the sunshell.
symptoms: Slipping or no engagement in overdrive (3-4)
Sudden grinding/loss of 2nd, 4th and reverse (broken sunshell)

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 96V035 - Manual Transmission Can Seize

records.title: 4WD Front Axle Vacuum Actuator Engagement Failure
records.description: 4x4 S-10s use a vacuum-operated front-axle engagement system: a transfer-case vacuum switch directs engine vacuum to an actuator (near the battery/driver-side of the front diff) that pulls a cable/fork to lock the right front axle into the differential. With age the diaphragm actuator, brittle vacuum lines, and the transfer-case vacuum switch fail — often aggravated by battery-acid corrosion nearby — so 4WD selects at the dash but the front axle never physically engages. Incomplete engagement can also break the shift fork. A very common S-series 4x4 complaint.
records.solution: Diagnose the vacuum circuit and replace the failed actuator, cracked vacuum lines, and/or transfer-case vacuum switch. The accepted permanent cure is a cable-operated manual axle-engagement kit (4x4 Posi-Lok) that deletes the vacuum actuator entirely and reliably engages the front axle from inside the cab, unaffected by cold or lost vacuum.
symptoms: 4WD selected but front wheels don't pull
Front driveshaft turns but axle doesn't engage

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 99V193 - 4WD-Mode Switch Can Increase ABS Stopping Distance

records.title: In-Tank Electric Fuel Pump Failure / No-Start
records.description: The in-tank electric fuel pump is a common wear-out item on 1990s S-10s and a frequent cause of intermittent no-starts and stalling. A worn pump loses pressure/volume; a failed internal check valve bleeds pressure back to the tank so the truck cranks but won't fire (or is hard to start after sitting). Premature failure of replacement pumps is often traced to tank rust/sediment being drawn into a new pump when the tank isn't cleaned. One of the most reported fuel-system problems for the generation, though no NHTSA recall covers it.
records.solution: Replace the in-tank fuel pump (module), thoroughly clean or replace the tank and use a fresh strainer/sock, and replace the fuel filter. Preventively change the inline fuel filter around every 30,000 miles to reduce pump strain and premature failure.
symptoms: Cranks but won't start (no fuel pressure)
Whining noise from tank or no pump prime hum
Sputtering as if out of fuel

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 91V108 - Fuel-Tank Sender Seal Can Leak in a Rollover

records.title: 4.3L V6 Intake Manifold Gasket Leak
records.description: The 4.3L Vortec V6 develops intake manifold gasket leaks that allow coolant to leak externally or mix with engine oil. The plastic gaskets deteriorate from heat cycling. This is a very common problem on all GM 4.3L V6 trucks.
records.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the intake manifold-to-head sealing area for external coolant seepage; if coolant contamination is suspected, check the engine oil for a milky appearance and verify with a combustion leak/cooling system test. The proper repair is to remove the upper components and intake manifold, clean the sealing surfaces thoroughly, and install the updated GM/revised metal-core intake manifold gasket set with new seals, then refill with fresh coolant and change the engine oil and filter if any coolant entered the crankcase. On the 4.3L Vortec, it is also wise to inspect the distributor, CPI/CSFI lines, and manifold bolts during reassembly and torque bolts in the correct sequence to spec. Typical repair cost is about $700-$1,400 at a shop depending on labor rates and whether oil service, coolant flush, or related parts are needed.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 97V218 - Rear Brake Pipe Can Fracture

records.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump Failure
records.description: The 1994-2004 S-10 in-tank fuel pump is prone to premature failure. Running the tank below 1/4 accelerates pump death because fuel cools and lubricates the pump. The integrated fuel level sender also fails, causing erratic gauge readings. Hot restart problems are a classic early warning sign as heat exacerbates pump weakness.
records.solution: Confirm the failure by checking fuel pressure at the rail with a gauge; the 4.3L CPI/CSFI systems are very sensitive to low pressure, and a weak pump will often show hard hot restarts, low pressure under load, or a no-start with little or no prime. Inspect the fuel pump electrical connector and ground at the frame, then replace the in-tank pump module with a quality complete assembly that includes the strainer and fuel level sender rather than installing the pump motor alone; on these trucks it is common to drop the tank, though lifting the bed is often faster and reduces rusted strap bolt issues. Replace the fuel filter at the same time and inspect the harness pigtail for heat damage, then verify pressure and gauge operation after repair. Typical repair cost is about $450-$900 parts and labor depending on whether a full module, sender, and connector are needed.
symptoms: Engine cranks but will not start
Engine sputtering or surging at highway speeds
Loss of power under load or climbing hills
Difficulty restarting when engine is hot
Whining noise from rear of vehicle

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 99V220 - Brake-Pipe Union Can Leak

records.title: Lower Ball Joint Failure
records.description: The lower ball joints on S-10 trucks wear prematurely, especially on 4WD models. Excessive play develops which can lead to sudden separation and loss of steering control. Subject to multiple NHTSA investigations.
records.solution: Raise the front suspension and check the lower ball joints for vertical and lateral play with a pry bar and dial indicator, following GM service specs; also inspect the control arm, tire wear pattern, and front-end alignment because worn joints often damage related components. If any looseness or torn boots are found, replace both lower ball joints on the axle as a pair using quality greasable joints or complete control arms where applicable, then torque all fasteners to spec and perform a full front-end alignment. On 4WD S-10 models, inspect the upper joints, idler arm, and tie-rod ends at the same time since wear commonly occurs together. Typical repair cost is about $300-$700 for both lower ball joints with alignment, but can exceed $900 if control arms or additional steering parts are needed.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 90V193 - Suspension Attachment Nuts Can Strip

records.title: 12V battery drain after over-the-air (OTA) update / Serial Data Gateway Module programming (GM CSP N242435630/N242435631)
records.description: Certain 2022-2024 Silverado 1500 trucks (and Tahoe, Suburban, GMC Sierra/Yukon siblings) can experience excessive 12V battery drain following an over-the-air software update. GM traced it to programming in the Serial Data Gateway Module (SDGM) — the network gateway that manages communication between modules — which fails to let the vehicle's electronics fully sleep after an OTA update, leaving parasitic loads active and discharging the battery. Symptoms include a dead or weak 12V battery, no-start, and various electrical warnings the morning after an update. GM addressed it with Customer Satisfaction Programs N242435630 and N242435631 (2024), a software reprogram with no parts required; the program runs through October 31, 2026.
records.solution: Dealer reprograms (reflashes) the Serial Data Gateway Module under CSP N242435630/N242435631 to correct the post-OTA sleep behavior; no parts required and performed at no charge. If the battery has been deeply discharged, it may need recharging or replacement. Confirm eligibility by VIN; courtesy transportation is provided while the fix is applied.
symptoms: Battery drains overnight after software update

citations.title: GM Program N242435630 - Serial Data Gateway Module

records.title: 2.7L Turbomax (L3B) Cold-Start Rattle and Wastegate Actuator Wear
records.description: The turbocharged 2.7L Turbomax four-cylinder develops a metallic rattle/knock on cold start-up, most pronounced in the first few seconds before oil pressure builds. The root cause is premature wear in the turbocharger wastegate linkage/actuator, which can also throw a turbo-underboost code. Owners also report VVT camshaft-actuator (CPAS) solenoid faults and engine-harness chafing on this engine. Because the L3B is direct-injection only (no port injection), intake-valve carbon buildup compounds the rough-idle/misfire complaints as miles accumulate.
records.solution: GM TSB 23-NA-058 addresses the cold-start rattle with a worn wastegate linkage — the fix is replacement of the wastegate actuator or, when the linkage is worn through, the complete turbocharger assembly. For the P0011/P0014 camshaft-timing codes, replace the failed camshaft position actuator magnet (solenoid) per PIP5855 and re-torque the loose intake-cam actuator cover-plate screws per PIP5921B. Walnut-blast the intake valves to clear carbon on higher-mileage engines.
symptoms: Turbo lag or limp mode under boost
Rough idle and misfires at higher mileage

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 2.7L TurboMax (L3B) cracked engine block from hot-core-pin casting defect (GM CSP N232415060)
records.description: A subset of 2023 Silverado 1500 trucks (also Colorado and GMC Sierra 1500) built with the 2.7L L3B TurboMax engine left the factory with engine blocks that were cracked or could crack in the main oil gallery, traced to a 'hot core pin' casting defect during block manufacturing. A crack in the main oil gallery — the primary pressurized-oil channel feeding the whole engine — can cause loss of oil pressure and catastrophic engine damage. GM addressed it with Customer Satisfaction Program N232415060 (released February 2024) rather than a formal safety recall; the affected U.S. population was small (reported around a dozen trucks), but the remedy is a full long-block engine replacement with no patch available. Coverage under the program runs through March 31, 2026.
records.solution: Dealer verifies VIN eligibility under CSP N232415060 and, if covered, replaces the engine (long-block swap) at no charge. Owners noticing low oil pressure, oil leaks at the block, or oil-pressure warnings on a 2023 2.7L truck should have it inspected promptly and reference the program by VIN.

citations.title: GM Program N232415060 - Block Main Oil Gallery Hot Core Pin Casting Defect

records.title: 2.7L TurboMax (L3B) lifter failure, intake-valve carbon buildup, and high oil consumption
records.description: The turbocharged 2.7L inline-4 (RPO L3B, marketed as TurboMax) used in fourth-gen Silverado 1500 work-grade and mid-trim trucks has generated a growing body of owner complaints distinct from the better-known 5.3L/6.2L V8 problems. Reported failures include collapsed/failed valve lifters (some at very low mileage — one documented 2022 Silverado Custom failed at ~22k miles), heavy carbon accumulation on the direct-injection intake valves causing rough idle, hesitation and 'chugging' under load, sticking PCV valves, and elevated oil consumption (owners report roughly a quart every 1,000-1,500 miles). Because the 2.7L is heavier-loaded in the full-size Silverado than in the Colorado/Canyon, it spends more time under boost and heat, which owners and shops link to accelerated valvetrain and turbo wear. GM issued repair campaigns in 2024 touching L3B/L2R engines.
records.solution: Diagnose lifter/misfire with a scan tool; a collapsed lifter typically requires lifter and often camshaft replacement. Carbon buildup on intake valves is cleaned via walnut-blasting (direct injection means no fuel washes the valves). Monitor oil level between changes and document consumption for warranty; sticking PCV valves are replaced. Check for applicable GM service bulletins/campaigns by VIN. Catch-can installation is a common owner mitigation for carbon/oil-vapor.
symptoms: Rough idle and hesitation under load
Excessive oil consumption (1 qt per 1,000-1,500 miles)

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 3.0L Duramax (LM2) engine coolant control valve failure (GM Special Coverage N252508341)
records.description: Silverado 1500 trucks with the 3.0L LM2 Duramax inline-6 turbodiesel are prone to failure of the electronically actuated engine coolant control valve. Failure illuminates the check-engine light, can leave cooling fans running after the key is off (draining the battery), and in some cases causes the engine to run hotter than normal. A frequent root cause is corrosion/terminal damage in the coolant flow control valve actuator harness connector. GM announced Special Coverage N252508341 (September 2025) extending warranty to 15 years / 150,000 miles from in-service date for the affected valve on 2021-2022 Silverado 1500 (and 2021-2023 Tahoe/Suburban and GMC/Cadillac siblings). Owners have reported multi-month back-orders on the replacement valve (part 40009644).
records.solution: Scan for codes (P1098 / P26BB are commonly reported); confirm the coolant control valve or its harness connector is at fault. Under Special Coverage N252508341 the dealer replaces the coolant control valve (part 40009644) at no charge within 15 years/150k miles. Inspect/repair the actuator harness connector for terminal corrosion. Reimbursement is available for owners who previously paid for the repair.
symptoms: Cooling fans run after engine is shut off

citations.title: GM Special Coverage N252508341 - LM2 Coolant Control Valve Replacement

records.title: 3.0L Duramax 'Service Emission System' Limp-Mode From DEF/NOx Sensor Faults
records.description: The 3.0L Duramax throws a 'Service Emission System' warning with a staged speed-limit countdown (e.g. 'In 175 miles speed will be limited to 65 mph', then 55 mph, then a no-restart threshold), frequently dropping the truck into limp mode. Root causes are faulty DEF level/quality sensors, NOx sensors, or a bad DEF injector/reductant heater, often triggered even when DEF is topped off. GM addressed several false-trigger cases with a software update (TSB 21-NA-071 family) but sensor hardware failures remain common and leave owners stranded on countdowns.
records.solution: Scan for the specific reductant/NOx code before parts. Apply the latest GM ECM/emissions software update (dealer TSB) for false MIL/DEF-level triggers; replace the failed DEF level/quality sensor, NOx sensor, or reductant injector as indicated. Use only fresh, spec DEF and confirm the countdown resets after repair. Many repairs fall under emissions/powertrain warranty.
symptoms: 'Service Emission System' message with mileage countdown
speed limited to 65 then 55 mph (limp mode)
'DEF Quality Poor' or false 'DEF Low' messages

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 4L60E Automatic Transmission 3-4 Clutch Pack and Sun Shell Failure (Slipping, Loss of 3rd/4th Gear)
records.description: The 4L60E 4-speed automatic behind the half-ton Silverado is notorious for wearing out its 3-4 clutch pack and cracking the input 'sun shell' (reaction sun gear shell) as mileage climbs. Owners report the truck suddenly loses 3rd and 4th gear (revs up but won't pull) while reverse and low gears still work, or a hard grinding/no-move with a fractured sun shell. The 3-4 clutch is the known weak point and often burns up first; the larger input drum on 2004-and-up units also likes to crack internally. This is one of the single most-searched failures for these trucks.
records.solution: Confirm with a scan for gear-ratio/slip codes and a pressure test before condemning the unit. Fix is a transmission rebuild or reman: replace the 3-4 clutch pack, install a hardened 4L60E sun shell (aftermarket beast/heavy-duty shell over the stamped OEM piece), fresh bands/steels, and rebuild or replace the valve body. Adding an auxiliary transmission cooler and shortening fluid-change intervals to ~30k miles greatly extends life. Reman units are widely available; a full-service rebuild with upgraded shell is the durable fix.
symptoms: Engine revs but truck won't accelerate in 3rd/4th (slipping)
Sudden loss of 3rd and 4th gear, still has 1st/2nd/reverse
Grinding or clunk then no forward movement (broken sun shell)
Check engine light with transmission codes

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 5.3L L83 Stretched Timing Chain / Cam Phaser Wear Setting Crank-Cam Correlation Codes
records.description: On the Gen V 5.3L L83 (and 6.2L L86) in the Silverado 1500, the timing chain can stretch and the VVT cam phasers/actuators can wear, causing the camshaft to drift out of correlation with the crankshaft beyond what the variable-valve-timing system can correct. This sets crank/cam correlation and VVT codes, a startup rattle (slack chain before oil pressure builds), rough idle, reduced power, and on higher-mileage trucks a risk of the chain jumping. AFM operation and extended oil-change intervals accelerate the wear. It is a more involved repair than a sensor because it requires removing the front timing cover.
records.solution: Diagnose with a scan tool — confirm correlation/VVT codes and check live cam/crank phase data; rule out a stuck VVT solenoid or low oil pressure first. The fix when the chain is stretched is replacement of the timing chain, both cam/crank sprockets (phaser), tensioner and guides, plus an oil/filter service, and addressing any AFM-related oil consumption that contributed. Keeping oil changes on a shorter interval and using the correct spec oil reduces recurrence.
symptoms: Rattle from the front of the engine on cold start
Check engine light with timing/VVT codes
Rough idle and reduced engine performance
Engine may run rich or stumble
Ticking or knocking that does not clear with an oil change

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 5.3L V8 (AFM/DFM) collapsed/failed lifter causing ticking and cylinder misfire
records.description: The EcoTec3 5.3L V8 (L83, and later L84 with Dynamic Fuel Management) uses Active Fuel Management to deactivate cylinders 1, 4, 6, and 7 under light load. The AFM lifters that collapse to deactivate those cylinders are prone to sticking or mechanical failure, often during a mistimed cylinder-mode switch event. A failed lifter stops actuating its valve, producing a loud ticking/tapping noise, rough idle, a flashing check-engine light, and a single-cylinder misfire (cylinder 7 is the most commonly reported). If a lifter disintegrates it can wipe the camshaft lobe, turning a lifter job into a cam-and-lifter job. Owners on CarComplaints report this surfacing anywhere from 80,000-120,000 miles, and it is the subject of multiple GM lifter/AFM lemon-law and class-action discussions.
records.solution: Diagnose with a running-compression test on the misfiring cylinder (an AFM lifter that stays below ~25 PSI regardless of solenoid command is collapsed). Repair requires replacing the failed lifter set (typically all 16) and pushrods, and replacing the camshaft if a lobe is worn. Many owners pair the repair with an AFM/DFM delete (range device or full delete kit keeping the engine in V8 mode) to prevent recurrence. Use only the correct oil and keep oil changes on schedule, as low/dirty oil accelerates failure.
symptoms: Loud ticking or tapping from the engine
Rough idle and loss of power

citations.title: GM Service Update 13330 - Active Fuel Management System Calibration

records.title: 5.3L V8 (AFM) excessive oil consumption fouling spark plugs
records.description: Silverado 1500 trucks with the AFM-equipped 5.3L V8 are known for burning excessive oil, with many owners reporting roughly 1 quart per 1,000 miles (GM's stated acceptable rate is up to 1 quart per 2,000 miles). The consumption is attributed to oil being drawn through the PCV system and to oil spray released from the AFM pressure-relief valve in the crankcase coating the cylinder walls; over time carbon buildup sticks the low-tension piston rings, worsening the problem and fouling spark plugs. The issue is the subject of a GM 5.3L oil-consumption class-action lawsuit. (Note: most acute on earlier Gen IV engines; the EcoTec3 L83 is improved but owners still report it on early K2 trucks.)
records.solution: GM TSBs address the PCV-path consumption by installing an updated valve cover (and updated oil pan/AFM valve with shield) so oil is not pulled into the intake. For ring-related consumption, the dealer fix is replacing the pistons and rings. Disabling AFM (range device/delete) reduces consumption if rings are not yet damaged. Owners should monitor oil level between changes and clean/replace fouled plugs.
symptoms: Burning about 1 quart of oil per 1,000 miles
Low oil level / low oil pressure warning between changes
Blue smoke on startup or acceleration

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 5.3L Vortec 5300 (Gen IV LC9/LMG) Excessive Oil Consumption from Piston Rings/AFM
records.description: Generation IV 5.3L Vortec engines burn an abnormal amount of oil — many owners report a quart or more every 1,000-2,000 miles. The defect is a combination of low-tension piston rings that fail to control oil, oil spray from the Active Fuel Management (AFM) system during cylinder deactivation, and a PCV path that draws oil mist into the intake. The oil fouls and prematurely wears spark plugs, causing rough idle, misfires, and a check-engine light. This was the subject of the Siqueiros v. GM class action (N.D. Cal., No. 3:16-cv-07244), which reached a final settlement in October 2025.
records.solution: GM's progression of TSBs added an AFM oil-deflector/shield and revised PCV provisions and ultimately upgraded the piston rings under warranty. Verified fix is replacement of the pistons/rings (and AFM oil-pressure relief valve / valley-cover shield); many owners opt for an AFM delete with a non-AFM cam, lifters, and tune to permanently resolve it. Monitor and top off oil between changes; replace oil-fouled spark plugs. Settlement payments (~$3,380) were available to eligible owners in CA, ID, and NC who had not already received free warranty piston repairs.
symptoms: Excessive oil consumption (1 qt per 1,000-2,000 mi)
Low oil level warning between changes

citations.title: GM Bulletin 10-06-01-008H - AFM Engine Oil Consumption

records.title: 6.2L L87 V8 connecting-rod/crankshaft bearing failure causing loss of propulsion (recall 25V274)
records.description: The 6.2L V8 L87 in 2021-2023 (and some 2024) Silverado 1500 trucks is subject to NHTSA recall 25V274 (GM N252494) for a supplier manufacturing defect: sediment/contamination on connecting rods and crankshaft oil galleries causing rod-bearing damage, plus out-of-spec crankshaft dimensions and surface finish. A failing rod bearing produces a deep knock and can seize the engine, causing sudden loss of propulsion. GM's investigation logged over 28,000 field complaints, including more than 14,000 alleging loss of propulsion, with crash, injury, and fire allegations, and NHTSA opened a follow-up probe into post-recall failures. About 107,000 Silverado 1500 units are covered.
records.solution: Under the recall, dealers inspect the engine; trucks that pass receive a higher-viscosity oil (0W-40), a new oil fill cap, oil filter, and an owner's-manual insert, while engines that fail inspection or have already failed are repaired or replaced at no charge. Owners should verify recall status by VIN at NHTSA.gov, watch for any knocking or low-oil-pressure warning, and stop driving immediately if a deep knock develops.
symptoms: Deep engine knocking or rod knock
Sudden loss of motive power / engine stall while driving
Metallic noise that worsens under load

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 25V-274 - L87 Engine Manufacturing Defects

records.title: 6.2L L87 V8 Connecting Rod / Crankshaft Failure (Loss of Propulsion Recall 25V274)
records.description: Certain 6.2L L87 V8 engines left the factory with manufacturing defects in the connecting rods and/or crankshaft — sediment/debris left in the crankshaft oil galleries and out-of-spec crankshaft finish starve the rod bearings of oil. The bearings spin, the rod can knock or seize, and the engine can suffer a sudden loss of propulsion at speed. This is the subject of a large 2025 safety recall covering roughly 600,000 U.S. trucks and SUVs (Silverado 1500, Tahoe, Suburban, Sierra 1500, Yukon, Escalade).
records.solution: Under NHTSA recall 25V274 / GM N252494000, dealers inspect the engine. Failed or out-of-spec engines receive a full long-block replacement; engines that pass inspection get an oil-and-filter change switching from 0W-20 to the heavier 0W-40, a new oil-fill cap, and an owner's-manual insert. Owners hearing knocking, seeing low oil pressure, or noticing metallic debris should stop driving and contact a dealer. (Note: NHTSA has continued probing failures on the post-fix 0W-40 cars, so a failure after the oil-spec change still warrants a dealer claim.)
symptoms: Sudden loss of power / loss of propulsion while driving

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 8-speed (8L90/8L45) torque converter clutch shudder and harsh shifting
records.description: Silverados equipped with the GM 8L90 (and the lighter 8L45) eight-speed automatic suffer a widespread torque-converter-clutch (TCC) shudder, often described as driving over a rumble strip during light cruising, plus harsh/clunky 1-2 and 2-1 shifts and slipping. GM traced it largely to the torque converter and to the original transmission fluid degrading and creating friction, which can shed metal debris into the unit. The defect is documented in GM TSBs 18-NA-355 and 19-NA-219 and was the basis of a consolidated class-action lawsuit alleging the 8L90/8L45 are defective. Early-build 2015-2017 trucks are worst affected; later 2018-2019 units shudder less but are not immune.
records.solution: Per GM's bulletins, the first step is a complete transmission fluid flush-and-fill with the updated low-shudder fluid (Mobil 1 Synthetic LV ATF HP / Dexron HP), which resolves many cases. Persistent shudder or hard shifts after the flush typically require torque converter replacement, and in severe cases (metal contamination) a valve body or transmission overhaul. Some owners use aftermarket friction-modifier additives as a stopgap.
symptoms: Shudder or vibration during light-throttle cruising (rumble-strip feel)
Shaking felt through the cabin around 35-50 mph

citations.title: GM Bulletin 18-NA-355 - 8-Speed Torque-Converter-Clutch Shudder

records.title: Auto Stop/Start Quits Working ('Auto Stop Unavailable') From Battery State-of-Charge Faults
records.description: The auto stop/start feature stops engaging and the DIC shows 'Auto Stop Unavailable' or the feature simply never activates. GM traces most cases to the Body Control Module reading the battery as perpetually below ~75% state-of-charge, which disables stop/start to protect restart capability. Contributing factors are a weak/aged AGM battery, loose battery terminal, or a corroded/disconnected ground. Some owners also see premature original-battery failure that leaves the truck slow to crank.
records.solution: Load-test the battery and clean/tighten the terminals and negative ground. Replace a weak battery with a correct Group 94R AGM (ACDelco 94RAGM / GM 88864542) — a flooded battery or wrong size will keep the feature disabled — then have the BCM battery sensor recalibrated/relearned. If the battery is good, check for parasitic draw and verify BCM state-of-charge data with a scan tool.
symptoms: engine no longer shuts off at stoplights
message appears after a jump-start or dead battery

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Blower Motor Resistor and Connector Overheating (No Low Fan Speeds, Burning Smell)
records.description: On GMT800/early-GMT900 Silverados with manual A/C controls, the HVAC blower motor resistor and its wiring connector overheat. Owners lose the lower fan speeds (blower works only on high, or drops speeds 1-4) or lose the blower entirely, often with a burning smell and a melted/scorched connector. The failure is usually driven by an aging blower motor pulling excess amperage plus moisture entering the fresh-air intake — bad enough that GM issued special warranty coverage citing an overheating/fire risk.
records.solution: Replace the blower motor resistor AND the melted connector pigtail together (GM 89019088 / ACDelco 15-81086 / Dorman 973-405, cross-ref 22807123) — most aftermarket kits include the harness. Inspect the blower motor itself for worn bearings/high current draw and replace if it caused the burnout. The resistor is on the lower passenger side of the dash, a sub-1-hour DIY.
symptoms: fan only works on the highest setting
burning/electrical smell from the passenger footwell
melted or scorched connector at the resistor

citations.title: GM Special Coverage 10240 - HVAC Blower Resistor and Connector

records.title: Bose Amplifier / Speaker Crackling, Static and No-Sound (Refreshed Cabin)
records.description: Silverados with the Bose audio system develop crackling, popping, and static, distortion at higher volume, or entire sections of speakers (e.g., all driver-side, or the center dash speaker) going silent. Causes range from a software/firmware bug in the IOK/Google-built-in radio, to internal Bose amplifier channel failures, to a physically failed center-dash speaker. GM acknowledged the software-related crackling in a TSB but a full fix has lagged, frustrating owners of the 2022 refreshed models.
records.solution: First apply the latest radio/amplifier software update (dealer TSB) which resolves many crackle/static complaints on IOK-radio trucks. If a channel is dead or a single speaker distorts, replace the Bose amplifier or the affected speaker (commonly the center-dash speaker). Check for loose door-panel mounting bolts, which cause rattle mistaken for speaker failure.
symptoms: persistent static regardless of source or volume
one side or all speakers go silent

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Brake / Fuel Line Corrosion Failure (Galvanized Steel Lines, Salt-Belt)
records.description: The original galvanized-steel brake (and fuel) lines on these trucks lack the modern nylon/PVF anti-corrosion coating, so in cold-weather/road-salt states the lines rust from the outside in and rupture. A brake-line burst causes sudden, often warning-light-free loss of brake pressure and a long/soft pedal; NHTSA logged hundreds of complaints and opened (then closed without recall) an investigation into salt-belt GM trucks. GM addressed it with a TSB and a pre-formed replacement-line kit rather than a recall.
records.solution: Inspect all underbody brake and fuel lines for surface rust/flaking, especially over the rear axle and along the frame rails. Replace corroded sections with GM's pre-formed brake-line kit (TSB 13-05-22-001) or aftermarket coated/stainless lines; bleed the system afterward. Proactively replace lines as a set in salt-belt trucks before failure, and wash the underbody regularly through winter. Any soft/sinking pedal or visible fluid leak should be treated as do-not-drive.
symptoms: Sudden soft or sinking brake pedal
Brake fluid leak under the truck
Loss of stopping power with no warning light
Visible rust/flaking on brake or fuel lines
Fuel smell from corroded fuel line

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Brake vacuum pump degradation reducing power brake assist (NHTSA recall 19V645)
records.description: The engine-driven brake vacuum pump on 2014-2018 Silverado 1500 trucks (5.3L and 6.2L V8) can lose vacuum output over time as oil sludge and debris are trapped by the pump's oil inlet filter screen. As vacuum drops, power brake assist decreases, producing a hard brake pedal, increased pedal effort, and longer stopping distances, most noticeably at low speed (parking lots, slowing for crosswalks). GM recalled roughly 3.4 million trucks and SUVs for this condition under NHTSA campaign 19V645000 (GM recall N192268490), and NHTSA's underlying investigation was closed after the recall.
records.solution: Under the recall, dealers reprogram the Electronic Brake Control Module (EBCM) software to better detect low vacuum and compensate via the ABS/stability system; affected owners should confirm the recall remedy has been applied via VIN at NHTSA.gov. Out-of-recall vehicles experiencing a hard pedal should have the vacuum pump tested and replaced if output is low, and the oil change interval kept current to limit sludge.
symptoms: Hard brake pedal / increased braking effort
Longer stopping distances, especially at low speed
Service brake assist or ABS warning
Reduced power brake assist when maneuvering slowly

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 19V-645 - Reduced Vacuum Brake Assist

records.title: Broken Exhaust Manifold Bolts on 5.3L/6.2L V8 Causing Exhaust Tick and False P0420
records.description: GM's small-block V8s (Gen III/IV LS and Gen V LT) in the Silverado 1500 are notorious for snapping exhaust manifold bolts. The steel bolts and the aluminum cylinder heads expand and contract at different rates through countless heat cycles, fatiguing the bolts until the heads snap off — usually the front and rear corner bolts. The resulting manifold-to-head gasket leak produces a loud 'exhaust tick' (often mistaken for a lifter) that is loudest on cold start, and the leak draws outside air past the upstream O2 sensor, frequently setting a false P0420 catalyst-efficiency code even with a good converter. Left alone it can also burn nearby wiring and worsen the leak.
records.solution: Inspect the manifold flanges for soot/leak tracks and the corner bolts for breakage. Repair is to extract the broken bolt shanks (often requires drilling/extractor or a slide-hammer style broken-bolt kit), replace the manifold gaskets, and reinstall with upgraded fasteners — ARP 134-1102 header bolts on Gen III/IV LS (4.8/5.3/6.0) or ARP 134-1104 on Gen V LT (5.3 L83 / 6.2 L86) — torqued in sequence with anti-seize. Re-evaluate any P0420 after the leak is sealed before condemning the catalytic converter or O2 sensors.
symptoms: Ticking/tapping exhaust noise, loudest on cold start
Tick that quiets as the engine warms up
P0420 catalyst-efficiency code with an otherwise good converter
Soot or carbon tracks at the exhaust manifold flange

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

fixParts.note: MAHLE Clevite MS16124. Fitment confirmed against the ShowMeTheParts catalog for this vehicle's year and engine.
fixParts.provenance: ShowMeTheParts fitment lookup by year and engine; buy links verified to carry the part number on a matching brand

records.title: A/C condenser cracking/leaking causing loss of cooling (blows hot air)
records.description: The factory air-conditioning condenser on 2014-2018 Silverado 1500 trucks is prone to cracking and refrigerant leakage, frequently at the spot welds on the sides of the condenser where vibration concentrates stress (revised replacement units add welds to spread the load). The result is a slow R134a leak and the A/C gradually blowing warm/hot air, often with under 50,000-70,000 miles. The problem is heavily documented on CarComplaints (13 condenser-cracked complaints on the 2016, 26 A/C-blowing-hot complaints on the 2015) and led to a GM A/C class-action that survived dismissal. Owners report parts backorders and limited 3-year/36k warranty coverage adding to frustration.
records.solution: Confirm the leak (UV dye / electronic sniffer at the condenser welds), then replace the condenser with the revised-design unit, evacuate and recharge the system with the correct R134a charge, and replace the receiver/drier and any contaminated orifice/expansion components. Out-of-warranty owners often use a quality aftermarket condenser to control cost.
symptoms: A/C blows warm or hot air
Gradual loss of cooling over weeks
Refrigerant low / leak detected at condenser
Oily residue or dye trace at condenser welds

records.title: A/C High-Side Hose Cracking at the Compressor-to-Condenser Bend (Loss of Refrigerant)
records.description: Early K2XX Silverado 1500 trucks have a documented A/C failure separate from the well-known condenser leak: the high-side discharge hose/tube running from the compressor to the condenser cracks at the sharp metal bend near the receiver/drier, dumping the entire refrigerant charge so the A/C blows warm. GM acknowledged a design flaw in the rigid metal section of this line in a technical service bulletin (PIT5331), redesigned the tube for 2016, and instructs technicians to replace the line with the updated part and add a support bracket to limit flex. Out-of-warranty owners pay for the repair, and an unsupported replacement can re-crack.
records.solution: Recover the system, replace the high-side discharge line with the updated GM tube, and install the support bracket per TSB PIT5331 to minimize movement/flex; replace the receiver/drier and any damaged components, evacuate, and recharge to spec. Confirm whether the failure is the discharge line versus the separately-known condenser leak, as both exist on these trucks. Pressure/dye test after repair to confirm the leak is sealed.
symptoms: A/C suddenly blows warm after working fine
Loss of refrigerant with no obvious external cause
Oily/dye residue at the high-side line near the drier
Refrigerant leak found at the metal bend of the compressor-to-condenser hose
A/C cools again only briefly after a recharge

citations.title: GM PIT5331 - Compressor-to-Condenser Refrigerant Line Leak

records.title: Catalytic Converter Theft Vulnerability (High Ground Clearance, Easily Accessed Converters)
records.description: The full-size Silverado 1500 is one of the most frequently targeted vehicles in the U.S. for catalytic converter theft. Its high ground clearance and underbody-mounted, easily reached converters let thieves cut them out in seconds, often in broad daylight, and lifted trucks are even easier to get under. Owners discover the theft by a sudden extremely loud, raspy exhaust on startup, a check-engine light, and reduced performance. Replacement of OEM converters plus the O2 sensors and pipe is expensive, and repeat thefts are common because nothing about the factory design deters re-targeting. This is a high-search, high-demand ownership problem rather than a manufacturing defect, but it is specific and well documented for this model.
records.solution: Replace the stolen converter(s) — OEM or CARB-compliant aftermarket — along with any damaged O2 sensors and exhaust pipe sections, then add theft deterrents: a welded catalytic-converter shield/cage (e.g., CatClamp / model-specific plate), etched/engraved converter ID, and parking in lit or secured areas. A tilt/vibration alarm can also help. Insurance comprehensive coverage often applies. Note: a separate 2019 emissions recall addressed an ECM that could fail to illuminate the malfunction-indicator light on a converter fault — unrelated to theft but worth checking by VIN.
symptoms: Extremely loud, deep roaring exhaust noise on startup
Visible missing converter / cut pipe under the truck
Check engine light (catalyst efficiency) after the theft
Strong exhaust smell entering the cabin

records.title: CSFI/CPI 'Spider' Fuel Injector Assembly Failure (Misfire, Rough Idle, Poor Fuel Economy)
records.description: The Central Sequential/Port Fuel Injection ('spider') assembly used on Vortec 4.3L/5.0L/5.7L engines feeds nylon lines to poppet or MPFI nozzles inside the intake. Over time the poppet valves gum up and stick, O-rings and the pressure regulator leak, and the nylon lines crack. The result is misfires, hard starting, rough idle, a noticeable drop in fuel economy, and often a raw-fuel/rich condition. A leaking regulator can even flood a cylinder (hydrolock risk). Very high-demand failure on these older trucks.
records.solution: Test fuel pressure and look for a leak-down after key-off; inspect the spider for wet fuel/leaking poppets. The durable repair is to replace the entire spider assembly, ideally upgrading the early poppet-style CSFI unit to the later MPFI-style spider (a GM-engineered redesign that bolts in on 1996-2001 engines with no modification). Reman upgraded assemblies with new regulator and Viton O-rings are widely sold; verify the exact GM/ACDelco part for your specific engine before buying rather than guessing.
symptoms: Loss of power and poor throttle response
Smell of raw fuel / rich exhaust, sometimes white smoke

records.title: Dashboard Cracking and Splitting Across the Top Pad (One-Piece Dash, Sun/UV Degradation)
records.description: GMT900-generation Silverado 1500 trucks (and platform-mates Tahoe/Suburban/Avalanche/Sierra/Yukon/Escalade) are widely reported to develop long cracks and splits across the top of the dashboard pad, typically radiating from the passenger airbag seam, defroster vents, and the corners near the windshield. GM moved to a large one-piece molded dash for these years with no relief joints, and the plastic dries out and loses plasticizer under windshield heat and UV exposure, causing the surface to fracture. Owners commonly see it appear between 4 and 8 years of age, worse in hot/sunny climates. A class-action suit was filed and dismissed in 2019, and GM treats it as a cosmetic, non-warranty item, so owners pay out of pocket. Beyond appearance, owners raise concern about cracked plastic over the passenger airbag becoming projectiles or affecting deployment, though that has not been the subject of a recall.
records.solution: There is no recall or warranty coverage. Common remedies are: install a molded ABS/poly dash cap (overlay) bonded over the cracked pad, replace the full dashboard pad assembly, or fit a carpeted/molded dash cover. Dealers will not warranty it as it is classified cosmetic. To slow it on an intact dash, use a windshield sun shade and a UV-protectant (e.g., 303 Aerospace Protectant). Verify any airbag-cover integrity if the crack runs over the passenger airbag door.
symptoms: Long cracks or splits across the top of the dashboard near the windshield
Cracks radiating from the passenger airbag seam or defroster vents
Pieces of dash plastic lifting or curling at the edges
Worsening rapidly after summer heat or in sunny climates

records.title: Factory Paint and Clear-Coat Peeling / Delamination (Roof, Hood, A-Pillars, Door Edges)
records.description: K2XX-generation Silverado 1500 owners report the factory clear coat and paint peeling and flaking off in sheets, most often on the roof, hood, A-pillars, the corners of rear-door windows, and lower door edges. White colors (Summit White, Pearl White, and the tri-coat whites) are reported as the worst affected. The accepted cause is poor adhesion between the e-coat/primer and the color/clear layers, so the paint delaminates with no impact or environmental trigger. A class-action lawsuit was filed covering 2015-2019 Chevrolet/GMC full-size trucks and SUVs. GM provides no separate paint warranty beyond the standard corrosion terms, so most owners face out-of-warranty refinishing, with GM sometimes offering only partial goodwill assistance.
records.solution: No recall exists; repair is a body-shop refinish of the affected panels (strip to substrate, re-prime, re-base, re-clear). Costs scale with how many panels are involved — a single panel respray is a few hundred dollars while a roof + hood + pillars job runs into the low thousands. Owners are advised to open a goodwill/customer-assistance case with GM (some receive partial reimbursement) and to keep documentation in case of class-action eligibility. Correcting it early on one panel prevents spread of the lifted clear coat.
symptoms: Clear coat bubbling, lifting, or peeling off in sheets
Paint flaking on the roof, hood, or above the windshield
Peeling at A-pillars, rear-door window corners, and lower door edges
Bare primer or metal exposed under peeled areas

records.title: Fuel Level Sensor / Sending Unit Failure Causing Erratic or Stuck Fuel Gauge
records.description: The in-tank fuel level sensor/sending unit fails as its resistor card and electrical contacts corrode (accelerated by sulfur in gasoline). The fuel gauge then jumps around, sticks on empty or full, reads inaccurately, or trips a false low-fuel light. It is one of the longest-running and most-searched Silverado complaints and sets fuel-level circuit DTCs. The sensor is integrated with the fuel pump module, so replacement usually means dropping the tank.
records.solution: Confirm with fuel-level circuit codes and by monitoring sensor voltage with a scan tool. Replace the fuel level sensor (part of the fuel pump/sender module); inspect and clean the tank-side connector for corrosion. Because the sender is inside the tank, most owners replace the complete pump/sender module while the tank is down.
symptoms: fuel gauge jumps or reads erratically
gauge stuck on empty or full
gauge reads correct only in part of the range

records.title: Google Built-in (13.4-inch) infotainment freezing, lockups, and audio dropouts (2022+ refreshed cabin)
records.description: Trucks with the larger Google Built-in infotainment system (rolled out on the refreshed 2022+ Silverado 1500 interior and continuing through 2024-2025) suffer frequent screen freezing, full lockups, Bluetooth dropouts, navigation errors and streaming-audio (e.g., Spotify) lockups. Owners commonly have to switch the ignition off and wait several minutes for the head unit to recover. Internal GM bulletins attribute many freezes to the system being overloaded when processing too many tasks at once, and to communication errors between the infotainment system and the body control module. This is a newer-generation, Google-OS-specific complaint distinct from earlier MyLink/Infotainment 3 freezing on pre-refresh trucks.
records.solution: Apply the latest GM software/over-the-air updates, which have targeted several freeze/reboot bugs; perform an infotainment system reset (or battery disconnect) to clear a lockup; check for applicable customer-satisfaction programs by VIN. Persistent failures may require head-unit/module reprogramming or replacement under warranty.
symptoms: Infotainment screen freezes or goes black

records.title: Headlight Housing Condensation / Moisture From Failed Lens Seal
records.description: The adhesive bead sealing the clear lens to the headlamp housing deteriorates (and factory vent tubes can clog), letting moisture accumulate inside the headlight. Owners see fogging, water droplets, or standing water in the housing; once heavily contaminated the lens never fully clears, and trapped moisture can shorten LED/DRL and bulb life. It is a widely reported cosmetic-and-reliability annoyance across multiple model years.
records.solution: Remove the assembly, dry it thoroughly (low heat / hairdryer), verify the vent tubes are open, and reseal the lens-to-housing joint with butyl-rubber caulk (preferred over silicone, which cracks with thermal cycling). Severely water-stained or electrically damaged units should be replaced with a new assembly that has a reinforced factory seal.
symptoms: fog or water droplets inside the headlight lens
moisture returns after rain or car wash
