records.title: Inaccurate / Stuck Fuel Gauge (Fuel Level Sender Wear + 2014 ECM Recall)
records.description: The fuel level sender inside the tank (part of the fuel pump module) can give false readings: the gauge sticks, reads full or empty regardless of actual level, or fluctuates by 1/8 to 1/4 tank as the resistor card contacted by the float wears. Reported across first-gen (2009-2016) Traverse. Separately, GM issued NHTSA recall 14007 for certain 2014 Traverse/Enclave/Acadia built Mar 26-Aug 15, 2013, where defective ECM calibration could misreport the fuel level by up to a quarter tank at both high and low ends, risking an unexpected stall.
records.solution: For sender wear, replace the in-tank fuel sender / fuel pump module assembly (sender is not sold separately on most years). For the recalled 2014 build window, an ECM reprogram (recall 14007, free of charge) corrects the software-caused inaccuracy. Verify with a scan tool that reported level tracks actual fill.
symptoms: Fuel gauge stuck on Full or Empty
Gauge reads empty with full tank

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 14V-223 - Inaccurate Fuel Gauge Reading

records.title: Infotainment Touchscreen Blackout / Freezing
records.description: The MyLink/infotainment touchscreen on 2018-2020 Traverse units can go black or freeze (in some cases the radio, volume and USB still function while the screen stays dark) and does not always recover with a normal restart. Owners have traced some failures to blown resistors on the screen's power-circuit board, requiring display/board replacement; software-related freezes are also common.
records.solution: Try a system reset (hold Home + Fast-Forward ~10 seconds) or a soft reboot (ignition off, door open, wait ~10 minutes). If the blackout persists, the display board/head unit is replaced; blown power-circuit resistors require the screen or board to be swapped.
symptoms: Radio/audio still works while the screen stays dark
Screen does not recover after restarting the vehicle

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Intermittent No-Crank / No-Start from Connector X203 and Wake-Up Faults
records.description: Many second-gen Traverse owners experience random no-crank / no-start events, sometimes after the engine shuts off while driving. GM service bulletins identify two patterns: bent or backed-out terminals at body connector X203 causing loss of communication on the HSLAN data bus with multiple stored DTCs, and a separate intermittent no-crank condition on 3.6L models flagged by crank/relay wake-up codes. The result is being stranded with a vehicle that will not respond to the start button.
records.solution: Have a technician scan for HSLAN/loss-of-communication DTCs and inspect/repair connector X203 for bent or damaged terminals per the GM bulletin; the second bulletin addresses the no-crank codes with module diagnosis and reprogramming. Owners should also rule out the simpler offenders first — loose/corroded battery terminals, a weak main battery, and a dead key-fob battery, all of which mimic the same symptom.
symptoms: Engine shuts off while driving then won't restart
Multiple unrelated warning lights / loss of communication

citations.title: GM Preliminary Information PIT5684A - Intermittent No Start and X203 Terminals

records.title: Intermittent "Shift to Park" Message — Faulty Shifter Park Switch
records.description: Owners frequently report a "Shift to Park" warning that appears even when the transmission is already in Park, often preventing the ignition from shutting off and risking battery drain (the radio stays on and the doors won't lock). The root cause is a weak/failing park switch in the console shifter assembly (often bad harness connectors) that fails to pull the Body Control Module signal low, a defect documented across multiple GM models and addressed in a GM service bulletin.
records.solution: Scan for transmission-range/shifter codes, then inspect and replace the faulty transmission control (shifter) assembly per the GM TSB; check shifter wiring connectors for corrosion. As a temporary workaround, cycle the shifter through drive and back to park, or hold the start button to clear the message.
symptoms: "Shift to Park" message displayed while already in Park
Vehicle will not turn off / radio stays on
Battery drain because the car won't fully power down
Doors will not lock until the message clears

citations.title: GM Service Bulletin 19-NA-206 - Intermittent Shift to Park Message

records.title: Power Liftgate Strut Failure
records.description: The Traverse power liftgate struts lose gas pressure over time, causing the liftgate to drop slowly when opened or slam shut unexpectedly. On models with power liftgate, the electric motor can also fail, leaving the liftgate inoperative via the button. The struts typically fail between 5-8 years, with cold weather accelerating the failure as the gas charge loses pressure faster at low temperatures. A dropping liftgate is a safety concern, especially when loading cargo or with children nearby.
records.solution: Replace both liftgate struts as a pair ($50-$120 for a pair of gas struts). This is a simple DIY repair — the struts have ball-socket ends that pop off with a small pry tool (15-minute job). For power liftgate models, if the electric motor has failed, the motor assembly costs $200-$500 and requires 1-2 hours of labor to replace. StrongArm and Sachs/Stabilus are quality aftermarket strut brands. Always replace both struts at the same time — they wear at the same rate.
symptoms: Have to hold liftgate up manually
Power liftgate button does not work
Liftgate opens only partway in cold weather

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Loss of Power Steering Assist from Hydraulic Power Steering Pump Wear
records.description: First-generation Traverse owners report an intermittent or sudden drop in power-steering assist, with heavy/hard steering especially at low speed and parking, often preceded by a whine from the pump. This is a HYDRAULIC power steering system (engine-driven pump), and the failure is internal flow-control-valve/seal wear in the pump that causes a loss of hydraulic pressure; the vehicle can revert to a manual-effort state. GM issued Special Coverage Adjustment #14329 for this pump-wear condition on 2009-2011 Traverse (and 2008-2011 Enclave, 2007-2011 Acadia, 2007-2010 Saturn Outlook), extending pump coverage to 10 years / 150,000 miles. NOTE: this is NOT the electric-power-steering (motor/column/control-module) issue found on some other GM cars.
records.solution: Diagnose the hydraulic power steering system for pressure loss; the fix is typically replacement of the power steering pump (and repair of any leaking high-pressure line or rack). Check eligibility for GM Special Coverage #14329 (10yr/150k on 2009-2011) before paying out of pocket.
symptoms: Intermittent loss of power steering assist
Whining noise from power steering pump
Increased effort at low speed / parking

citations.title: GM Special Coverage 14329 - Loss of Power Steering Assist

records.title: Engine Oil Consumption (3.6L V6)
records.description: The 3.6L V6 in the Traverse consumes oil at a rate that many owners find unacceptable, particularly on 2009-2017 models with the LLT and LFX engine variants. Owners report consuming 1 quart every 2,000-3,000 miles. The oil consumption is related to piston ring design and the PCV system routing oil vapor back into the intake. The issue is not accompanied by visible external leaks. GM has acknowledged elevated oil consumption on the 3.6L but considers up to 1 quart per 2,000 miles within their acceptable range.
records.solution: Check oil level at every fuel stop and top off as needed. Use the GM-specified dexos1 Gen 3 approved 5W-30 synthetic oil. An oil consumption test at the dealer involves measuring consumption over a set mileage interval — if it exceeds GM limits, warranty coverage may apply. For out-of-warranty vehicles, using a slightly heavier 5W-40 European-spec oil can reduce burn-off. Severe cases may require piston ring replacement ($2,500-$4,000) or valve stem seal replacement ($1,000-$2,000).
symptoms: Oil level drops 1 quart every 2,000-3,000 miles
Slight blue smoke on hard acceleration
Fouled spark plugs from oil contamination

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Service StabiliTrak / Traction Control Warnings with Reduced Power
records.description: Traverse owners frequently see 'Service StabiliTrak' and 'Traction Control Off' messages appear together while driving, sometimes accompanied by an engine power reduction. The warning is a downstream symptom rather than a single fault: common triggers are a failing wheel speed sensor, an ABS/EBCM module or wiring-harness fault, or an underlying engine misfire that disables the stability system. The intermittent nature makes it frustrating to diagnose without scanning stored codes.
records.solution: Always pull DTCs first — wheel speed sensor codes point to a sensor/tone-ring replacement, while misfire codes (P0300-series) mean the StabiliTrak light is secondary and the misfire/ignition cause must be fixed. Inspect the ABS module connector and wiring for corrosion. Resist clearing the light without diagnosis; the fix ranges from a single wheel speed sensor to ignition/coil work depending on the root cause.
symptoms: ABS / traction lights cycling on and off

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Start/Stop Accumulator Missing Bolts Causing Transmission Fluid Leak / Loss of Propulsion (Recall N202313440)
records.description: Certain 2018-2020 Traverse units (with the global front-wheel-drive 6- or 9-speed transmission) left the factory with missing or loose bolts on the start/stop transmission accumulator endcap. This can cause a transmission fluid leak that may progress to a loss of propulsion while driving, and leaking ATF near an ignition source raises fire risk. GM issued safety recall N202313440 (NHTSA 20V-668) covering this defect across multiple GM models, with the remedy beginning December 15, 2020.
records.solution: Free recall remedy under GM N202313440: dealers inspect the start/stop transmission accumulator and replace it if any bolts are missing. Owners should check VIN eligibility at NHTSA.gov and have the recall performed; contact Chevrolet customer service at 1-800-222-1020.
symptoms: Transmission fluid leak / spots under vehicle
Loss of propulsion or vehicle won't move
Burning smell from leaking ATF near hot components

citations.title: GM Recall N202313440 / NHTSA 20V-668 - Transmission Accumulator Bolts Missing

records.title: Sunroof/Moonroof Drain Clog Causing Interior Water Leak from Headliner
records.description: The moonroof feeds rainwater into a rain tray above the headliner that drains through tubes routed down the pillars. Debris clogs the tubes (and tray outlets), so the tray overflows and water runs down the inside of the headliner, dripping from the overhead console, dome/map light area, or near the rearview mirror. Second-generation (2018-2024) and earlier owners report soaked headliners, wet front floors, and damaged overhead electronics. Some cars also have poorly seated/kinked or leaking quick-connect drain hoses that leak even after the tubes are cleared.
records.solution: Clear the moonroof drain tubes with low-pressure air/water from the top (avoid high pressure that can pop hoses off). Verify hose routing and reseat/replace kinked or disconnected drain hoses and leaking quick-connect couplings; in severe cases the sunroof drain assembly is serviced. Dry the headliner to prevent mold.
symptoms: Water dripping from headliner or overhead console
Water near rearview mirror or dome light

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Failure (3.6L V6 LLT/LFX)
records.description: The 3.6L V6 (LLT and LFX variants) in the first-generation Traverse is notorious for premature timing chain stretch. The engine uses three timing chains — one primary and two secondary chains driving the variable valve timing actuators. The chains stretch beyond the tensioner capacity, causing the engine timing to slip. Symptoms progress from a rattle on cold start to a check engine light with camshaft correlation codes. If ignored, the stretched chains can skip teeth, causing catastrophic engine damage. The issue typically manifests between 80,000-120,000 miles.
records.solution: Replace all three timing chains, tensioners, guides, and VVT actuator solenoids. This is a major repair requiring 10-15 hours of labor because the engine must be partially removed or the front cover fully disassembled. Parts cost $300-$600 for a complete timing kit; labor runs $1,200-$2,500. Total cost: $1,500-$3,500. GM extended warranty coverage to 10 years/120,000 miles on some model years (Special Coverage 14311). Always replace all three chains together — replacing just one is false economy as the others will fail soon after.
symptoms: Rattling or clattering noise on cold start
Check engine light with camshaft position codes
Rough idle that improves as engine warms up
Metallic rattling from front of engine

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Water Pump Shaft Seal Coolant Leak (3.6L V6)
records.description: The engine-driven water pump on the 3.6L V6 develops a leak at the shaft seal, weeping coolant from the pump 'weep hole' at the front/side of the engine. GM acknowledged the condition with Customer Satisfaction Program #13079 covering 2009-2013 Traverse (and Lambda-platform siblings Enclave/Acadia/Outlook) with the HFV6 engine (LY7, LLT), noting that operating with a low coolant level shortens shaft-seal life. Water-pump leaks are widely reported across first-gen years through 2017. Left unaddressed the pump can lose enough coolant to cause overheating.
records.solution: Replace the water pump (and thermostat/gaskets while accessed), pressure-test the cooling system, and refill with DEX-COOL. Keeping coolant topped to spec extends seal life. #13079 (a coolant-level check/top-off program, not a free pump replacement) applied to eligible 2009-2013 cars until April 30, 2015; otherwise owner-pay.
symptoms: Coolant drips or crusty residue at front of engine

citations.title: GM Customer Satisfaction Program 13079 - Water Pump Shaft Seal Leaks

records.title: 11-Inch Infotainment Screen Freezing, Blacking Out, or Rebooting
records.description: Owners of the redesigned 2024-2025 Trax have reported the center infotainment display freezing, going black, losing touch response, or repeatedly rebooting. Because HVAC controls, backup camera display, audio, and vehicle settings are integrated into the screen, the failure is more than a convenience issue. GM issued service guidance addressing intermittent blank or inoperative radio/display behavior on vehicles using the newer infotainment architecture.
records.solution: Confirm battery voltage and check for software updates or radio module calibrations before replacing hardware. Dealers typically reprogram the radio/HMI modules first; if the concern persists, diagnosis focuses on display, radio, or communication faults on the infotainment network. If the backup camera image is also lost, document that separately because it can elevate the safety significance.
symptoms: HVAC or audio controls inaccessible through screen
Apple CarPlay or Android Auto disconnects

citations.title: GM Service Bulletin 24-NA-084 - Radio Software Version 169.3

records.title: 12-Volt Battery Drain or No-Start After Sitting
records.description: A number of owners have reported dead batteries, slow cranking, or complete no-start conditions after the vehicle sits overnight or for a few days. On new vehicles this often traces to software modules not going to sleep properly, telematics/infotainment wake-up issues, or a weak original battery rather than a traditional charging-system failure. The problem tends to appear early in ownership and can be intermittent.
records.solution: Load-test the battery, verify charging voltage, and perform a parasitic draw test after all modules should be asleep. Dealers may update module software, inspect for modules staying awake on the network, and replace the battery if it fails testing. Repeated jump-starting without root-cause diagnosis can mask the actual draw problem.

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Coolant Leak from Water Outlet Housing
records.description: The plastic water outlet housing on the 1.4L turbo engine is prone to cracking and leaking coolant. The housing sits on the back of the engine block and deteriorates from heat cycling. Coolant loss can lead to overheating if not addressed.
records.solution: Replace the plastic water outlet housing with an updated design. Many owners opt for aftermarket aluminum replacements for improved durability.
symptoms: Temperature gauge rising higher than normal

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Forward Collision Alert / Automatic Emergency Braking False Warnings or Unexpected Activation
records.description: Some 2024-2025 Trax owners have reported forward collision warnings triggering unexpectedly, emergency braking intervening without an obvious obstacle, or driver-assistance warnings appearing intermittently. These complaints are significant because they can startle the driver or create a rear-impact risk if the vehicle brakes unexpectedly. Reports point to camera calibration, sensor visibility, or software logic issues rather than a single mechanical failure.
records.solution: Scan all ADAS modules for stored faults and verify windshield camera alignment/calibration status, especially after windshield replacement or front-end impact. Dealers typically inspect for obstruction, update software if available, and perform static or dynamic calibration of the forward camera. If warnings persist, the camera or related module may need replacement after confirming power, ground, and network integrity.
symptoms: forward collision warning with no vehicle ahead

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Front Brake Squeal or Grinding from Premature Pad/Rotor Wear
records.description: Owners of the current-generation Trax have reported front brake squeal, scraping, or grinding noises at surprisingly low mileage, sometimes accompanied by rotor scoring or vibration. While some brake noise can be normal, repeated complaints at low mileage suggest pad material, hardware fitment, or rotor surface issues on some vehicles. The concern is usually more annoying than dangerous at first, but it can become a safety issue if wear is ignored.
records.solution: Inspect pad thickness, rotor condition, slide pins, and anti-rattle hardware rather than assuming the noise is normal. Dealers may resurface or replace rotors and pads if wear is abnormal, and should verify caliper movement and proper hardware lubrication. If the vehicle has been driven while grinding, rotor replacement is usually required.

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Rearview Camera Image Missing, Delayed, or Blue/Black Screen
records.description: Multiple owners have reported the rearview camera failing to display when shifting into reverse, showing a blank/blue/black screen, or appearing only after a long delay. This issue is documented in owner complaints and overlaps with infotainment/display faults, but the safety impact is distinct because the camera is federally required equipment. In some cases the problem is intermittent, making it difficult to reproduce at the dealer.
records.solution: Check for related GM service bulletins, software updates, and camera/radio module faults. Diagnosis should include verifying camera power/ground, coax or video signal integrity, and whether the issue is isolated to the camera or part of a broader infotainment dropout. If software updates do not resolve it, dealers may replace the camera or radio/display components depending on test results.
symptoms: no rear camera image in reverse
black screen when shifting into reverse
camera image appears after several seconds

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 1.4L Turbo Wastegate Actuator Failure
records.description: The 1.4L turbocharged engine in the Trax (shared with Cruze, Sonic, and Buick Encore) develops wastegate actuator failures. The wastegate seal degrades, allowing exhaust gases to bypass the turbine wheel and reduce boost. The wastegate actuator arm design has a known mechanical weakness. GM TechLink bulletin noted many returned turbochargers had no fault and emphasized proper diagnosis before replacement.
records.solution: Confirm the fault before replacing parts by scanning for P0299, logging commanded vs. actual boost, and inspecting the turbo wastegate lever/actuator for excessive play, sticking, or a loose flapper; also smoke-test the intake/charge-air system and check the bypass valve, PCV system, and vacuum/pressure control plumbing so a boost leak is not mistaken for turbo failure. If the wastegate arm or flapper is worn, GM typically services this as a complete turbocharger assembly rather than the actuator alone; replace the turbo assembly with new gaskets, oil feed/return seals, and related hardware, then clear codes and verify boost on a road test. Typical repair cost is about $1,200-$2,000 at an independent shop or $1,800-$2,800 at a dealer depending on labor rates and whether the catalytic converter fasteners/oil lines also need replacement.
symptoms: Clanking or rattling noise near turbo
Loss of turbo boost at higher RPMs
Turbo whistle changes tone or disappears

citations.title: GM Preliminary Information PIP5495G - P0299/P0234 Turbocharger Diagnosis

records.title: Intake Manifold Gasket Coolant Leak
records.description: The 3.5L and 3.9L V6 develop intake manifold gasket leaks, continuing the GM V6 gasket legacy. Coolant leaks externally or into engine oil.
records.solution: Replace intake manifold gaskets with updated design. Flush cooling system and oil after repair.

citations.title: GM Service Bulletin 07-06-02-006E - Coolant Crossover Pipe Gasket Leak

records.title: Electric Power Steering Failure
records.description: Electric power steering motor or control module fails causing loss of power assist. Steering becomes very heavy. GM issued recalls on some model years.
records.solution: Replace power steering motor or control module. Check for GM recall coverage first (recall 14V-153). Some aftermarket rebuilt units available.

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Rear A/C Line Corrosion and Refrigerant Leak
records.description: Rear A/C lines running under the van corrode and leak refrigerant. Road salt accelerates corrosion. System loses charge gradually.
records.solution: Replace corroded A/C lines. Evacuate and recharge system. Inspect all lines and connections. Some owners bypass rear A/C entirely.
symptoms: Oily residue on A/C lines under vehicle
Front A/C also weak due to low charge
Visible corrosion on metal A/C lines

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Lower Intake Manifold Gasket Leak (Dex-Cool)
records.description: The 3.4L V6 in the Venture is infamous for lower intake manifold gasket failure. The original gaskets react with Dex-Cool coolant, causing them to erode and leak coolant into the engine oil or externally. This can lead to catastrophic engine damage if coolant mixes with oil.
records.solution: Replace the lower intake manifold gaskets with updated Fel-Pro design that resists Dex-Cool degradation. Flush the cooling system and change the oil immediately if coolant contamination is found.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no visible external leak
Milky substance on oil cap or dipstick
Oil level rising above full mark

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Power Sliding Door Motor and Cable Failure
records.description: The power sliding door system fails due to worn cables, motor burnout, and latch mechanism jamming. The door can become stuck partially open or refuse to open/close on the power setting.
records.solution: Inspect the power sliding door for frayed or broken drive cables, a weak/burned-out motor, worn center roller, and latch/track binding before replacing parts; also check the door module fuse, wiring at the door harness, and verify the latch and track move freely by hand with the power function disabled. On these Venture vans, the usual repair is replacement of the sliding door motor/cable assembly and any damaged rollers or latch components, followed by cleaning/lubricating the upper, center, and lower tracks and performing a door relearn/calibration if applicable. If the cable has wrapped or jammed in the drum, do not keep cycling the door, as it can damage the regulator and rear latch. Typical repair cost is about $400-$900 depending on whether an aftermarket cable kit or complete OEM-style motor/regulator assembly is used, with higher costs if latch or track hardware also needs replacement.

citations.title: GM Recall 04110 / NHTSA 04V-597 - Right-Hand Power Sliding Door Interior Handle

records.title: 120V Charging Cord (EVSE) Overheating and Melting at the Plug
records.description: Early Gen 1 Volts shipped with a 120V portable charge cord (EVSE) that could overheat at the wall plug, becoming too hot to touch, melting the connector, and in at least one case causing a burn. GM initially blamed household outlet wiring but ultimately replaced the units. The original cord used thinner 16-gauge wire (orange short lead); replacements used heavier 14-gauge wire (black lead and improved NEMA plug).
records.solution: GM ran a customer-satisfaction service campaign (11888, not a formal safety recall) replacing the original 120V EVSE on affected 2011-2012 Volts (US and Canada) with an upgraded 14-gauge unit, free of charge. Owners were also advised to plug directly into a dedicated, properly-wired outlet.
symptoms: Burning smell at outlet while charging

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 12V Auxiliary Battery Parasitic Drain / APM (DC-DC Converter) Failure Leaving Car Dead
records.description: A widely documented Volt fault where the 12V auxiliary battery drains while the car sits, leaving an otherwise fully-charged EV completely dead and unable to power up. Root causes include parasitic draw from modules that fail to sleep (OnStar/telematics hang-ups, software bugs) and, in worse cases, a failing Accessory Power Module (APM/DC-DC converter) that no longer keeps the 12V battery charged. Owners frequently need a jump-start after the car sits a few days. Note: Gen 1 used three non-interchangeable APM variants under one GM part number, which matters when sourcing a replacement.
records.solution: Diagnose parasitic draw and update software; replace the weak/aged 12V AGM auxiliary battery. If the APM (DC-DC converter) has failed, replace it (professional HV service). Some cases traced to modules (e.g. OnStar) not powering down are resolved by software reflash.
symptoms: Car completely dead / won't power on after sitting
Needs a jump-start despite full main battery
Repeated dead 12V battery every few days

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: Gen 1 'Reduced Propulsion Power' — HV Battery Low-Voltage / Cell-Balancing Fault
records.description: Gen 1 Volts (2011-2015) commonly display a 'Propulsion Power is Reduced' message with reduced acceleration and electric range, often with DTC P0A7F. GM traced this to an HPCM2 (Hybrid Powertrain Control Module 2) software update that could disable the cell-balancing function, causing a low-voltage condition and potential loss of propulsion. Addressed via NHTSA recall 18V397 and GM recalls N172130460/461/462 (rolled out across 2011-2015 by year). Note: the frequently-cited Customer Satisfaction Program 17228 is the analogous program for the Gen 2 (2016-2017) Volt, not Gen 1; badly degraded packs out of the 8yr/100k HV warranty can still require costly module/pack replacement.
records.solution: Dealers reprogram/recalibrate the HPCM2 free of charge under the recall to restore proper cell balancing and provide adequate warning. If a battery module has degraded beyond limits and is out of the HV warranty, module/pack replacement is required and expensive.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 18V-397 / GM 18215 - VICM Service Software

records.title: Inner Tie Rod Separation from Steering Gear (2015 Recall 15V442)
records.description: A small number of 2015 Volts (built April 11, 2014) left the factory with an inner tie rod not tightened to specification due to a supplier assembly-machine error, allowing the tie rod to separate from the steering gear and cause loss of steering control. Recalled under NHTSA campaign 15V442 (GM recall 15386) alongside 2014-2015 Cruze models. Note: the Volt portion of this recall was very small in scope (roughly 10 units total across Cruze and Volt), so real-world prevalence is low.
records.solution: Under recall, dealers replace the entire steering gear assembly free of charge. Owners noticing clunking, play, or wandering steering should have the tie rod torque inspected immediately.
symptoms: Clunking or looseness in the steering

citations.title: GM Recall 15386 / NHTSA 15V-442 - Inner Tie Rod Not Torqued to Specification

records.title: Post-Crash High-Voltage Battery Coolant Leak and Delayed Fire Risk (2011 NHTSA PE11-037)
records.description: During a May 2011 NHTSA NCAP side-pole crash test, a lateral member intruded the HV battery enclosure, damaging cells and causing a battery-coolant leak; 21 days later the coolant (conductive when the pack is charged) created an electrical short that sparked a fire consuming the test Volt. NHTSA opened investigation PE11-037. No defect trend was established and the probe was closed January 20, 2012, but GM issued a proactive January 2012 customer-satisfaction campaign to reinforce the structure.
records.solution: GM's January 2012 campaign strengthened the vehicle safety structure around the battery in side impacts, added a sensor in the coolant reservoir to monitor HV battery coolant level, and added a tamper-resistant bracket to help prevent coolant overfill. Performed free of charge.
symptoms: Delayed fire after a severe crash
HV battery coolant leak after impact
Coolant conductivity / electrical short in damaged pack

citations.title: NHTSA PE11-037 Closing Resume - Post-Crash EV Fire Hazard

records.title: Rear Brake Caliper Piston Gas Pocket — Reduced Rear Braking (2018-2019 Recall 18V576)
records.description: On certain 2018-2019 Volts, supplier ZF failed to properly apply the surface coating to the rear brake caliper pistons, allowing gas to form in the rear brake hydraulic circuit. This produces a soft/spongy pedal, reduced rear-brake performance and longer stopping distances. Recalled under NHTSA campaign 18V576 (GM recall 18279), part of a broader GM brake recall of roughly 210K-240K vehicles; the same ZF defect affected other automakers.
records.solution: Under recall, dealers bleed the vehicle's brake system to purge the trapped gas, free of charge. If a spongy pedal persists, affected caliper pistons/calipers are inspected and replaced.

citations.title: GM Recall N182167900 / NHTSA 18V-576 - Rear Brake Piston Degassing

records.title: AWD Transfer Case Encoder Motor and Chain Failure
records.description: AWD-equipped Astros suffer from transfer case issues including encoder motor failure and stretched drive chains. The encoder motor controls the AWD engagement and when it fails, the system may default to 2WD or make grinding noises. Chain stretch causes a noticeable clunk on acceleration from a stop.
records.solution: Replace the encoder motor if the AWD is not engaging properly. For chain noise, the transfer case must be opened and the chain replaced. Change transfer case fluid every 30,000 miles with AutoTrak II fluid. Do not use conventional ATF — the Astro AWD system requires the specific NP-233 fluid.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 03V093 - Exterior-Mirror Switch Short Circuit

records.title: Unwanted ABS Activation Increasing Stopping Distance
records.description: First-generation Avalanches (2002-2006) can experience unwanted ABS activation during normal low-speed braking. The antilock brake system activates inappropriately, causing a pulsating brake pedal and increased stopping distances when it should not be engaging. The issue is more likely in environmentally corrosive areas where road salt deteriorates the ABS wheel speed sensor wiring and tone rings. This creates a safety hazard as the vehicle takes longer to stop than expected during routine braking.
records.solution: Inspect and clean all four ABS wheel speed sensors and tone rings. Replace corroded sensor wiring or connectors. If the ABS module itself is faulty, replacement costs $600-$1,200. Applying dielectric grease to sensor connectors during brake service can prevent corrosion. In some cases, ABS module reprogramming at the dealer resolves the issue.
symptoms: ABS activates during normal low-speed braking
Pulsating brake pedal when it should not be pulsating
Increased stopping distances during routine stops
ABS warning light illuminated on dashboard
Grinding or buzzing noise from brakes during normal stops

citations.title: NHTSA Manufacturer Communications Data Corpus

records.title: 5.3L Vortec AFM Active Fuel Management Oil Consumption and Lifter Failure
records.description: The 5.3L Vortec V8 with Active Fuel Management (AFM/DOD) in 2007-2013 Avalanches suffers from excessive oil consumption and premature lifter failure. The AFM system deactivates four cylinders for fuel economy, but the AFM lifters have a coating that wears off prematurely, leading to collapsed lifters, bent pushrods, fouled spark plugs, and catastrophic engine damage. GM issued TSB 10-06-01-008A for oil deflector installation but never recalled the vehicles. Oil consumption of 1 quart per 1,000 miles is commonly reported.
records.solution: Monitor oil level weekly and top off as needed. For a permanent fix, perform an AFM delete which involves replacing the camshaft, all 16 lifters, and valley cover with non-AFM components ($2,000-$4,000 parts and labor). An AFM disabler device ($300-$500) can reduce the issue by preventing cylinder deactivation. Change oil every 5,000 miles with full synthetic.
symptoms: Oil consumption of 1 quart per 1,000 miles or more
Blue smoke from exhaust on startup or acceleration
Check engine light with cylinder-specific misfire codes
Lifter tick or knock noise from engine

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 06V289 - Fuel-Rail Pulse-Damper Retainer

records.title: Body Cladding Fading, Cracking, and Clip Failure
records.description: The first-generation Avalanche (2002-2006) features distinctive gray plastic body cladding that is prone to fading, cracking, and clip failure. The unpainted plastic panels that encircle the body deteriorate from UV exposure, turning chalky white and developing cracks. The clips holding the cladding in place become brittle and break, causing panels to loosen or detach. The cladding issues are cosmetic but affect vehicle appearance and can expose underlying metal to corrosion.
records.solution: Restore faded cladding with dedicated plastic restorer products (Solution Finish, Cerakote Trim Coat). Replace broken clips with new GM clips or aftermarket equivalents. For severely damaged cladding, replacement panels are available from aftermarket suppliers. Some owners choose to paint the cladding to match the body color for a permanent solution ($500-$1,500 for professional paint).
symptoms: Gray plastic cladding turning white or chalky
Underlying metal visible where cladding has pulled away

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 05V552 - Tire and Loading Information Label

records.title: Dashboard Cracking Above Instrument Cluster and Airbag Panel
records.description: The 2007-2013 Chevrolet Avalanche (and related GMT900 trucks) suffers from widespread dashboard cracking. The upper dashboard material shrinks and cracks due to UV exposure and heat cycling, with cracks typically developing above the instrument cluster, over the passenger airbag panel, and at the windshield defroster vents. Over 100 complaints have been filed with NHTSA. There are safety concerns that dashboard fragments could become projectiles during airbag deployment in a crash.
records.solution: Dashboard replacement is the proper fix but costs $1,500-$2,500 installed at a dealer. More affordable options include dash covers ($50-$100), dashboard replacement kits ($200-$400), or professional dashboard repair services ($300-$600). A class-action lawsuit was filed but GM has not issued a recall.
symptoms: Visible cracks in dashboard above instrument cluster
Cracks appear primarily in sun-exposed areas
Dashboard surface becomes brittle and flaky

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 21V054 - Passenger Frontal Air-Bag Inflator

records.title: Reduced Engine Power Mode from Throttle Body and Pedal Sensor Faults
records.description: The 2007-2013 Avalanche frequently enters "Reduced Engine Power" mode, severely limiting acceleration. The most common causes are the electronic throttle body wearing out or the accelerator pedal position sensor (APP sensor) developing faults. The vehicle becomes barely drivable in this mode, struggling to accelerate to highway speeds. The issue can occur intermittently before becoming permanent.
records.solution: Diagnose with a scan tool to determine if the throttle body or accelerator pedal position sensor is the cause. Throttle body replacement costs $200-$400 parts and labor. APP sensor replacement costs $100-$250. A remanufactured throttle body from a quality source works well. Clear codes after repair and road test to verify.
symptoms: "Engine Power Reduced" or "Reduced Engine Power" message on dash
Vehicle struggles to accelerate past 20-30 mph
Check engine light with P2128 or P2138 codes
Intermittent power loss that resolves after restart

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 09V154 - Fuel-System Control Module Water Intrusion

records.title: Rear Brake Proportioning Valve Malfunction
records.description: The height-sensing rear brake proportioning valve, mounted on the rear axle area, corrodes and sticks, causing improper brake balance. When the valve sticks, the rear brakes may lock up prematurely during normal braking, or provide insufficient rear brake force, both creating dangerous handling characteristics.
records.solution: Replace the proportioning valve assembly. The valve is connected to the rear suspension by a link that measures ride height. Ensure the link is properly adjusted after installation. Bleed the entire brake system starting from the wheel furthest from the master cylinder. Check rear brake hardware for glazing from lockup.
symptoms: Rear wheels locking during normal braking
Uneven brake wear front to rear

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 94V176 - Right Rocker Reinforcement Panel

records.title: 3.1L V6 Distributor Gear Wear Causing Timing Issues
records.description: The 3.1L V6 engine uses a nylon distributor drive gear that wears prematurely, causing ignition timing to become erratic. As the gear teeth wear, timing retards inconsistently, leading to poor performance, misfires, and increased fuel consumption. The gear material is simply not durable enough for sustained use.
records.solution: Replace the distributor assembly with one that has an updated drive gear. Check the camshaft gear for wear as well — if the cam gear teeth are damaged, the camshaft must be replaced. Set base timing to 10 degrees BTDC after installation. Consider upgrading to an aftermarket brass gear if available.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 98V027 - Interior Lamp Control Module

records.title: Door Striker Fracture Allowing Unexpected Door Opening
records.description: GM recalled certain 2024 Blazer EV vehicles where the door strikers may fracture, allowing the door to open unexpectedly while driving. A fractured door striker compromises vehicle structural integrity and occupant safety, especially at speed. The door may not properly latch or may open during side impacts.
records.solution: Contact Chevrolet dealer immediately to check recall eligibility. Dealers will inspect and replace door strikers at no cost. Test each door by firmly pulling on the exterior handle with the door closed - any unexpected movement or noise warrants immediate dealer inspection.
symptoms: Door ajar warning light when doors are closed
Door does not feel solidly latched when closed
Clicking or unusual noise when closing a door
Wind noise suggesting door seal issue
Visible damage to door striker mechanism

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 23V869 - Door Strikers

records.title: Infotainment System Black Screen, Freezing, and Software Glitches
records.description: The 2024 Blazer EV has widespread infotainment system issues including black screens, frozen displays, camera glitches, audio dropouts, CarPlay/Android Auto disconnects, virtual control malfunctions, and cluster display errors. The 17.7-inch touchscreen controls most vehicle functions including HVAC, making software failures particularly disruptive. GM has released multiple software campaigns but OTA updates have been problematic, with some updates causing additional issues like checkered screen backgrounds.
records.solution: Schedule a dealer visit for the latest software campaign updates. Not all updates can be delivered OTA - some require USB installation at the dealer. If the screen goes black, try holding the home button for 10 seconds to force a restart. Contact Chevrolet customer service at 1-800-222-1020 if dealer cannot resolve the issue.
symptoms: Infotainment system freezes and becomes unresponsive
Display shows checkered pattern after OTA update
CarPlay or Android Auto disconnects repeatedly
Backup camera feed cuts out or displays incorrectly

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 24V487 - Right Front Lower Control Arm

records.title: Rear Parking Brake Wiring Harness Defect Causing Unintended Activation
records.description: GM recalled approximately 40,233 Blazer EV vehicles from 2024-2025 model years due to a defect in the rear parking brake wiring harness. The defect can cause the parking brake to activate unintentionally while driving (causing rear wheel lock-up) or fail entirely when needed. Between August 2023 and May 2025, 97 complaints were filed, including two instances of rear-wheel lock-up while driving and one report of complete parking brake failure.
records.solution: Contact Chevrolet dealer for free recall repair. The dealer will inspect and replace the rear parking brake wiring harness as needed. Do not ignore parking brake warning messages. If you experience rear wheel lock-up while driving, pull over safely and have the vehicle towed to a dealer.
symptoms: Parking brake activates unexpectedly while driving
Rear wheels lock up without driver input
Parking brake fails to engage when activated
Service parking brake message on display

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 26V031 - Incorrect Prior Parking-Brake Harness Repair

records.title: Rear Drive Unit Motor Insulation Failure Causing Power Loss
records.description: GM recalled certain 2024 Blazer EV vehicles where the electric motors in the rear drive units may have insufficiently insulated wires that can contact each other, resulting in an electrical short and loss of drive power. This manufacturing defect can cause sudden propulsion loss while driving, creating a serious safety hazard particularly at highway speeds.
records.solution: Contact Chevrolet dealer to check recall eligibility. The rear drive unit motor will be inspected and replaced if insulation deficiency is found. This is a free repair under the recall. Do not drive the vehicle if you experience sudden propulsion loss - have it towed to the dealer.
symptoms: Reduced power warning message on display
Unusual sounds from rear axle area

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 24V320 - Rear Drive Unit Wire Insulation

records.title: Central Port Injection Fuel Leak Under Intake
records.description: The early central port injection (CPI) system uses pressurized fuel lines under the upper intake manifold that develop cracks and leaks over time. Fuel leaks directly onto the hot engine, creating a serious fire hazard. The plastic fuel lines become brittle with age and heat exposure.
records.solution: Replace the CPI unit and all associated fuel lines under the upper intake. Updated kits with more durable fuel lines are available. Inspect the fuel pressure regulator diaphragm for leaks. Clean the intake manifold thoroughly before reassembly. Test for leaks with a fuel pressure gauge before closing up.
symptoms: Visible fuel leak under intake manifold

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 96V142 - Rear Seat-Belt Buckles

records.title: Transfer Case Vacuum Actuator Failure
records.description: The 4WD engagement system uses a vacuum-operated front axle actuator controlled by a thermal actuator on the transfer case. The vacuum lines crack and the thermal actuator diaphragm tears, preventing the front axle from engaging when 4WD is selected. This leaves you in 2WD when you need 4WD most.
records.solution: Inspect all vacuum lines from the transfer case to the front axle actuator and replace any cracked or brittle lines. Replace the thermal actuator if it is not holding vacuum. Some owners upgrade to a cable-operated actuator for more reliable engagement. Test the system by engaging 4WD on a loose surface.
symptoms: Clicking from transfer case when shifting

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 94V114 - Trailer-Hitch Bolt Torque

records.title: Auto Start-Stop Battery Degradation and System Faults
records.description: The AGM battery required for the auto start-stop system degrades prematurely, often failing within 2-3 years. When the battery weakens, the start-stop system disables itself and various electrical warnings appear. The auxiliary battery (on equipped models) can also fail, compounding the issues.
records.solution: Replace the AGM battery with a genuine ACDelco AGM battery — standard flooded batteries are not compatible with the start-stop system. After replacement, a battery sensor reset via a scan tool is required. Some owners permanently disable start-stop with aftermarket modules if they find the feature annoying.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 24V737 - Improperly Heat-Treated Door Strikers

records.title: 10-Speed Transmission Wheel Lock-Up (10L80)
records.description: Vehicles equipped with the 10-speed automatic transmission may experience momentary wheel lock-up when shifting from 8th to 5th gear. A transmission control valve is susceptible to premature wear, leading to pressure loss and potential wheel lock-up.
records.solution: Recall repair: Software update to monitor valve wear and prevent use of affected gears. Transmission valve body replacement if wear is detected. Complete transmission replacement in severe cases.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 25V148 - 10-Speed Transmission Damage Can Lock the Wheels

records.title: 2.0L Turbo (LTG) Engine Problems
records.description: The 2.0L turbocharged LTG engine experiences fuel injector failures, significant turbo lag, poor NVH characteristics, and has been the subject of a class action lawsuit filed in April 2023.
records.solution: Fuel injector cleaning or replacement. Spark plug replacement. Software updates for turbo lag improvement. Carbon buildup cleaning (direct injection engines).
symptoms: Check engine light with injector-related codes

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 76V088 - Incorrect Brake Combination Valve Can Reduce Stopping Ability

records.title: 8-Speed Automatic Transmission Shudder (8L90/8L45)
records.description: The 8L90 and 8L45 8-speed automatic transmissions experience torque converter clutch shudder, causing vibration and shaking during gear changes. The issue is caused by the lock-up clutch slipping and chattering. This defect has been the subject of class action lawsuits against GM.
records.solution: Transmission fluid flush with updated Mobil 1 Synthetic LV ATF HP fluid. Torque converter replacement (may not permanently fix issue). TCM software reflash/update. Complete transmission replacement in severe cases.
symptoms: Shuddering or shaking between 25-80 mph during gear shifts
Vibration under light acceleration at 1000-1500 RPM
Feeling like driving over rumble strips at highway speeds
Sudden lurching or jerking during acceleration

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 01V381 - Lower Driver-Door Hinge Welds May Be Inadequate

records.title: Driver Airbag Emblem Separation Hazard
records.description: The plastic 'Camaro' emblem located on the steering wheel airbag cover may separate during frontal airbag deployment. In a crash, plastic emblem pieces can become projectiles, increasing risk of injury to the driver.
records.solution: Recall repair: Replace frontal driver side airbag module (free of charge).
symptoms: Loose or rattling emblem on steering wheel (inspect visually)

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 21V211 - Steering-Wheel Camaro Emblem Can Become a Projectile

records.title: Cooling System Problems and Engine Overheating
records.description: Camaro owners report persistent overheating issues, particularly at idle, caused by cooling fan failures, faulty fan relays, clogged radiators, failing water pumps, and thermostat problems. Temperatures reaching 240-250°F have been reported.
records.solution: Radiator flush or replacement for clogged radiators. Cooling fan motor or relay replacement. Thermostat replacement. Water pump replacement. Coolant system pressure test to find leaks.
symptoms: Overheating primarily at idle or low speeds
Coolant loss without visible external leaks
Steam or coolant smell from engine bay

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 74V027 - Brake-Booster Housing Can Separate

records.title: Electric Power Steering (EPS) Failure
records.description: The electric power steering assist system may fail suddenly while driving due to defective control boards in the Bosch-supplied EPS system. Loss of power steering requires significantly greater steering effort, especially at low speeds. Approximately 26,772 vehicles were affected by the recall.
records.solution: Recall repair: Replace power steering gear assembly (free of charge). EPS control module replacement.
symptoms: Sudden loss of power steering assist while driving
Steering wheel becomes very difficult to turn
Greater steering effort required at low speeds

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 25V175 - Electric Power-Steering Assist Can Fail

records.title: Electrical System and Parasitic Battery Drain
records.description: Approximately 8% of Camaro owners report electrical problems including parasitic battery drain, infotainment system failures, gauge cluster shutdowns while driving, and water intrusion in the trunk causing electrical system shutdowns.
records.solution: Parasitic draw test to identify faulty module. HMI module replacement for infotainment failures. Fuse box replacement. Seal trunk and battery compartment from water intrusion. Software updates for various control modules.
symptoms: Dead battery after sitting overnight or a few days
Backup camera, radio, and MyLink system failures
Gauge cluster and infotainment shutting down while driving

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 76V132 - Intermediate Steering Shaft Can Separate

records.title: Rear Differential Noise and Wear
records.description: The rear differential may develop gear whine, clutch chatter (on limited-slip models), howling, or clunking noises. Some owners have experienced premature differential wear with excessive metal fragments found in gear oil.
records.solution: Differential fluid flush with correct limited-slip additive. Differential clutch pack replacement. Complete differential rebuild or replacement. Ring and pinion gear replacement.
symptoms: Whining noise from rear end while driving
Gear whine and posi unit clutch chatter
Clunking sounds on turns, especially left turns
Howling noise that changes with speed

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 80V108 - Lower Ball-Joint Nut Can Back Off

records.title: Lower Intake Manifold Gasket Coolant Leak
records.description: The 2.2L and 2.4L engines in the Cavalier are prone to intake manifold gasket failure, allowing coolant to leak externally or internally mix with oil. The composite gaskets deteriorate over time due to heat cycling. Dex-Cool coolant interaction with these gaskets accelerates deterioration.
records.solution: Replace the lower intake manifold gasket with an updated Fel-Pro design. Flush the cooling system and switch to conventional green coolant if desired. Check the oil for milky contamination — if present, perform multiple oil changes to flush the system. Torque intake bolts to specification in the correct sequence.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no visible external leak

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 04V300 - Rear Seat-Belt Anchorage Can Separate

records.title: Passlock Anti-Theft System Prevents Starting
records.description: The Passlock security system frequently malfunctions, reading the wrong resistance from the ignition cylinder sensor and refusing to allow the engine to start. The security light flashes and the car cranks but will not fire. This commonly occurs in cold weather or after the ignition cylinder wears internally.
records.solution: The temporary fix is to turn the key to ON (not start), wait 10 minutes for the security light to stop flashing, then turn off and restart. The permanent fix is to bypass the Passlock sensor by wiring a 2.2K ohm resistor in place of the hall-effect sensor in the ignition cylinder. Some owners replace the entire ignition lock cylinder assembly.
symptoms: Engine cranks but will not start

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 04V036 - Ignition Switch Can Melt During an Extended Start Attempt

records.title: Ecotec Engine Timing Chain Stretch and Guide Wear
records.description: The 2.2L and 2.0L Ecotec engines in the Cobalt develop timing chain stretch and timing chain guide deterioration. The plastic timing chain guides wear over time, causing the chain to become slack and noisy. If left unaddressed, the timing chain can skip teeth, causing valve timing misalignment and potential engine damage. The issue typically develops between 80,000-150,000 miles. The water pump is driven by the timing chain on these engines, so both should be addressed together.
records.solution: Replace the timing chain, tensioner, guides, and water pump as a kit when chain noise develops. DIY timing chain kit with water pump runs $200-$400 for parts. Labor at a shop runs $600-$1,200 due to the front-of-engine teardown required. Do not ignore chain rattle on cold start - it will worsen and can cause catastrophic engine damage.
symptoms: Rattling or slapping noise on cold start
Chain noise that worsens over time
Check engine light with timing-related codes
Rough idle or hesitation on acceleration
Reduced engine power if timing has jumped

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 14V171 - Ignition Key Can Be Removed Before the Switch Is Off

records.title: Premature Front Wheel Hub Bearing Failure
records.description: Front wheel hub bearings commonly fail prematurely, sometimes as early as 50,000 miles. The sealed bearing units develop excessive play and noise due to poor sealing that allows water intrusion. Road salt environments accelerate failure dramatically.
records.solution: Replace the front hub bearing assembly. This is a bolt-on unit that does not require a press. Torque the axle nut to 159 ft-lbs. Inspect the ABS tone ring on the new hub before installing. Replace in pairs if high mileage.
symptoms: Humming noise that changes with speed
Steering wheel vibration at highway speed

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 07V014 - Headliner Trim May Not Provide Required Head-Impact Protection

records.title: Fuel Pump Module Failure Causing Stalling and No-Start
records.description: The in-tank fuel pump assembly is prone to failure, often due to deteriorating fuel pump wiring harness connections or internal pump motor wear. Symptoms appear gradually with intermittent stalling before complete failure. Hot weather exacerbates the problem as heat-soaked pumps lose pressure.
records.solution: Replace the fuel pump module assembly. Use an OEM-equivalent pump with updated wiring harness connector. Drop the fuel tank for access — the Cobalt has no trunk access panel. Run the tank low before removal for safety.
symptoms: Hard starting when engine is hot

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 12V459 - Fuel-Pump Module Port Can Crack and Leak

records.title: Defective Ignition Switch Causing Engine Shutoff and Airbag Failure
records.description: The Chevrolet Cobalt was at the center of the largest safety scandal in GM history. Defective ignition switches could turn from "Run" to "Accessory" or "Off" position while driving, triggered by heavy keychains, road vibrations, or knee contact. When the ignition turns off, the engine shuts down, power steering and power brakes are lost, and critically, airbags are disabled. GM knew about the defect as early as 2005 but did not issue a recall until February 2014. The defect is linked to 124 compensated deaths and hundreds of injuries.
records.solution: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls for recall eligibility. The recall remedy is ignition switch replacement, free of charge. Until repaired, remove all items from keychain and use only the ignition key alone. Never hang heavy items from the key. If the engine shuts off while driving, shift to Neutral and steer to safety.
symptoms: Engine shuts off unexpectedly while driving
Loss of power steering and power brakes simultaneously
Key can be removed from ignition while not in OFF position
Vehicle stalls when key is bumped by knee or heavy keychain

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 14V047 - Ignition Switch Can Move Out of Run and Disable the Air Bags

records.title: Electric Power Steering Motor Sudden Failure
records.description: The Cobalt equipped with electric power steering (EPS) is subject to a recall for sudden loss of power steering assist while driving. The EPS motor can fail without warning at any speed, requiring significantly more effort to steer the vehicle. The 2005 model year alone has 128 complaints for power steering failure. GM issued a recall in March 2010, but some owners report the issue recurring even after the recall repair.
records.solution: Check VIN for recall eligibility. Dealers replace the electric power steering motor free of charge under the recall. If power steering fails while driving, pull over safely - the vehicle can still be steered but requires much more physical effort. Report recurring failures to NHTSA.
symptoms: Sudden loss of power steering assist
Steering becomes very heavy without warning
Steering effort increases in cold weather
Intermittent power steering that cuts in and out

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 10V073 - Electric Power-Steering Assist Can Fail Suddenly

records.title: A/C Compressor Failure
records.description: The A/C compressor can fail prematurely, often due to internal clutch issues or compressor seal failure. When the compressor fails internally, it can contaminate the A/C system with metal debris, requiring extensive repairs.
records.solution: Replace A/C compressor assembly. If internal failure occurred, flush entire A/C system, replace condenser, receiver/drier, and expansion valve. Use quality replacement parts. Verify proper oil charge in new compressor.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 14V645 - Driver Air-Bag Deployment Sequence Can Be Reversed

records.title: Parasitic Battery Drain
records.description: Some Colorado owners experience unexplained battery drain that can result in a dead battery after sitting for a few days. This can be caused by various electronic modules not going to sleep properly, OnStar module issues, or faulty door switches.
records.solution: Have dealer perform parasitic draw test to identify source. Common causes include OnStar module, BCM, or radio. Update software to latest version. If vehicle sits for extended periods, use a battery maintainer.
symptoms: Dead battery after sitting a few days
Accessories staying on after vehicle off

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 15V157 - Driver Air-Bag Inflator Can Separate from Its Backplate

records.title: Diesel Emissions System Issues (DEF/DPF)
records.description: The 2.8L Duramax diesel can experience issues with the emissions system including DEF (Diesel Exhaust Fluid) quality sensors, DPF (Diesel Particulate Filter) regeneration problems, and NOx sensor failures. These can cause reduced power mode and check engine lights.
records.solution: Use quality DEF fluid from reputable sources. If DEF quality warning appears, have system diagnosed - may need sensor replacement. Allow DPF regeneration cycles to complete (don't shut off during regen). Replace NOx sensors when faulty.
symptoms: Check engine light with emissions codes

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 15V267 - Front-Seat Frame Hooks May Not Be Secured

records.title: Infotainment System Freezing/Rebooting
records.description: The MyLink infotainment system can freeze, become unresponsive, or reboot randomly. This affects the radio, navigation, backup camera display, and phone connectivity. Issues are often software-related but can indicate hardware failure.
records.solution: Update to latest software version via dealer or USB. Perform a hard reset by holding power button. Clear paired Bluetooth devices. If problems persist, the radio module may need replacement under warranty or extended coverage.
symptoms: Bluetooth won't connect or stay connected

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 11V552 - Driver Seat-Belt Warning Connection Can Be Intermittent

records.title: Front Suspension Clunk Over Bumps
records.description: A clunking or knocking noise from the front suspension when going over bumps is common. This is often caused by worn sway bar end links, upper control arm bushings, or strut mounts. The issue can be amplified by rough roads or off-road use.
records.solution: Inspect and replace sway bar end links (most common cause). Check upper control arm bushings for play. Inspect strut mounts for wear. Ensure all suspension bolts are properly torqued. Consider upgraded components for off-road use.
symptoms: Noise when turning at low speeds

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 24V237 - Damaged Front Wheel-Hub Bolts Can Loosen or Break

records.title: Transfer Case Encoder Motor/Switch Issues
records.description: The electronic transfer case can have difficulty shifting between 2WD and 4WD modes. The encoder motor or position switch can fail, causing the Service 4WD message and preventing proper engagement. Issues are more common in vehicles that don't regularly use 4WD.
records.solution: Have dealer diagnose which component is failing. Replace encoder motor or position switch as needed. Regularly cycling through 4WD modes helps prevent issues. Ensure transfer case fluid is at proper level and condition.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 12V594 - Secondary Hood Latch May Be Missing

records.title: 8-Speed Transmission Shudder/Harsh Shifts
records.description: The 8L45 8-speed automatic transmission can develop a shudder during light acceleration, typically between 25-50 mph. This is caused by torque converter clutch issues, similar to problems in other GM vehicles with this transmission family.
records.solution: Perform transmission fluid flush with GM-approved fluid and friction modifier. Multiple fluid changes may help. GM has extended warranty coverage for some affected vehicles. In severe cases, torque converter replacement may be needed.
symptoms: Clunk when shifting at low speeds

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 24V133 - Front Camera Can Trigger Unexpected Emergency Braking

records.title: Water Pump Failure (3.6L V6)
records.description: The water pump on the 3.6L V6 can fail, causing coolant leaks and potential overheating. The pump is driven by the timing chain, making replacement labor-intensive as it requires significant disassembly to access.
records.solution: Replace water pump when symptoms appear. Replace thermostat at same time. Consider replacing timing chain components preventatively if high mileage. Flush cooling system after repair. Monitor for proper bleeding of cooling system.
symptoms: Whining noise from front of engine

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 18V358 - High-Pressure Fuel Pump Can Detach and Damage the Fuel Line

records.title: 2.2L OHV Head Gasket Failure
records.description: The 2.2L OHV four-cylinder engine is prone to head gasket failure, particularly on higher-mileage examples. Overheating from cooling system neglect or a failing water pump accelerates gasket failure. Once the gasket fails, coolant enters the combustion chamber causing white smoke and potential hydro-lock.
records.solution: Replace the head gasket and have the cylinder head checked for warpage — machine the head if out of specification (max 0.003" deviation). Replace the thermostat and inspect the water pump while accessible. Use a quality multi-layer steel gasket and torque head bolts in sequence. Perform a cooling system pressure test after repair.

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 93V157 - Front Suspension-Support Weld Can Fail
